Start Date: Immediate

JHNA, CTSi, and EXPANSIA have come together to form a Defense Technology platform named Aether Aerospace focused on delivering high-impact technologies, technology-enabled services and advanced manufacturing solutions to the U.S. Department of Defense and related national security customers. Backed by Falfurrias Management Partners, the platform brings together deep domain expertise across Army, Navy, and Air Force and Space Force programs, digital engineering, systems integration, and specialized manufacturing capabilities.

The combined organization operates as a multi-entity aerospace and defense technology and tech-enabled services and manufacturing enterprise positioned for scalable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation

OVERVIEW

Full-time/Permanent Employee

Location: Remote
As a Software Factory Engineer III, you will implement and aid mission software teams in the onboarding and use of software factory capabilities. You will integrate development tools, cloud services, CI/CD pipelines, security controls, and observability into reliable workflows, using reusable templates and automation to reduce the effort required to onboard applications. You will work with programs that use established Department of the Air Force software factories, such as Platform One, ODIN, and DAF CloudWorks, and help teams navigate their onboarding, access, application integration, security, and release processes. Working under general direction, you will independently resolve complex technical issues and collaborate with developers, cybersecurity personnel, and government stakeholders to improve the developer experience and delivery outcomes.

RESPONSIBILTIES

    • Integrate source control, CI/CD, artifact repositories, container registries, automated testing, security scanning, secrets management, and observability into software delivery workflows

    • Work with program teams and factory providers to assess application fit, prepare onboarding information, obtain access, and map existing development and release processes to available factory services

    • Configure and use established software factories, including Platform One, ODIN, or DAF CloudWorks as applicable, to build, test, secure, and deploy program applications

    • Develop and maintain reusable CI/CD templates, infrastructure-as-code modules, container baselines, and deployment patterns that teams can adopt with minimal customization

    • Automate builds, tests, vulnerability checks, artifact promotion, deployments, and operational monitoring across development, test, and production environments

    • Implement security controls and evidence collection within delivery workflows in coordination with cybersecurity and RMF/ATO teams; address application-specific control responsibilities and findings

    • Provision and configure cloud and container services, including identity, networking, storage, compute, Kubernetes, and secrets, within approved environments

    • Troubleshoot onboarding, integration, pipeline, deployment, and performance issues; document fixes and improve the shared platform

    • Create self-service documentation, examples, and onboarding guidance so development teams can use factory capabilities effectively

    • Provide technical guidance to application teams on factory tools, DevSecOps practices, and secure releases

    • Maintain configuration standards, monitor service health and delivery metrics, and improve reliability and developer experience

    • Provide technical support to operational strategies aligned within your program and initiatives that optimize processes, enhance productivity, and ensure quality across all program functions

    • Ensure 100% of planned hours are worked and recorded

    • Identify and forward to your leadership any opportunities that could lead to growth within your work area

    • Participate in growth efforts as requested

    • Ensure all contractual deliverables are met/exceeded to the customer's satisfaction

    • Complete personal PDP and attend Staff Meeting and Storytime (with camera on)

    • Within your program, build productive and positive professional relationships with clients

    • Execute all contract requirements as assigned in accordance with the contract-specific LCAT and requirements

    • Perform other related duties as assigned

KEY QUALIFICATIONS

    Clearance:Active TS/SCI
    Education and Years of Experience:Bachelor's (or equivalent) with 5 - 7 years of experience, or a Master's and 3 to 5 years of experience in software factory engineering, DevSecOps, cloud/platform engineering, IT operations, or software development

    • Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipelines, automated tests, artifact workflows, and reusable delivery templates

    • Experience onboarding or supporting applications in an established software factory or shared development platform, including access, toolchain integration, and release workflows

    • Proficiency with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Ansible, or CloudFormation and scripting languages such as Python, Bash, or PowerShell

    • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure and container technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes

    • Understanding of DevSecOps security scanning, vulnerability remediation, monitoring, and the application team’s role in RMF/ATO processes

PREFERRED ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATIONS

    • Experience using Platform One, ODIN, DAF CloudWorks, or a comparable DoD software factory as an application team member or onboarding engineer

    • Experience with artifact repositories, hardened containers, SBOMs, secrets management, and software supply-chain controls

    • Familiarity with observability tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, or ELK Stack

    • Experience creating developer documentation or self-service onboarding workflows for multiple teams

    • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum and responsibly integrating AI-assisted or agentic development tools into delivery workflows

    • Familiarity with AI-assisted development and agentic workflows, including coding agents, MCP integrations, automated tests, and documentation, with human review and configuration control

Trillium Health Resources is a Tailored Plan and Managed Care Organization (MCO) serving 46 counties across North Carolina. We manage services for individuals with serious mental health needs, substance use disorders, traumatic brain injuries, and intellectual/development (IDD) disabilities. Our mission is to help individuals and families build strong foundations for healthy, fulfilling lives.

Why Work for Us?

Trillium believes that empowering others begins with supporting our team. We offer our employees:

  • Competitive benefits and work-from-home options for most positions
  • Opportunities for professional growth in a diverse inclusive culture

If you are looking for a unique opportunity to make a tangible impact on the lives of others, apply today!

What We’re Looking For

Trillium Health Resources has a career opening for a Utilization Management Specialist III - MH/SU to join our team! The Utilization Management Specialist III - MH/SU is responsible for providing comprehensive clinical review of services requests for people who experience psychiatric symptoms related to mental health issues and/or co-occurring or co-morbid conditions or symptoms or addictions to substances and/or developmental disabilities.

On a typical day, you might:

  • Provide clinical review of services for members or enrollees with mental health, substance use, and/or developmental disabilities including diagnosis review, medical necessity criteria, determining member eligibility; level of care needed and making service authorization decisions regarding individual service authorizations with timely, clear, concise documentation.
  • Provide clinical triage for members seeking services through Screening, Triage and Referral.
  • Provide consultation and technical assistance to providers regarding clinical care needs, levels of care, Client Rights Rules, evidenced based practices, scope of practice issues etc.
  • Provide ongoing review/staffing/consultation of treatment documentation of needs for members participating in group, family or individual services.

Employee Benefits:

Trillium knows that work/life balance is essential. That’s why we offer:

  • Typical working hours: 8:30 am – 5:00 pm; flexible work schedules with some roles with management approval.
  • Work-from-home options available for most positions
  • Health Insurance with no premium for employee coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 24 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) plus 12 paid holidays in your first year
  • NC Local Government Retirement Pension (defined-benefit plan)
  • 401k with 5% employer match and immediate vesting
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) qualifying employer
  • Quarterly stipend for remote work supplies

Qualifications

  • Master's degree in health and human services or related field and one (1) year of experience

providing Utilization Management services.

    • Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
    • Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor (LCMHC)
    • Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT)

Preferred:

jobs.title: Scientist, Plume Modeling and Forecasting
jobs.excerpt: Sunlight reflection may be the only available option, alongside dramatic emissions reductions, adaptation, and rapid scaling of carbon removal, to rapidly limit many climate impacts over the coming decades.
jobs.description:
Sunlight reflection may be the only available option, alongside dramatic emissions reductions, adaptation, and rapid scaling of carbon removal, to rapidly limit many climate impacts over the coming decades. But we don’t know nearly enough about it to make a scientifically-informed decision about potential deployment – and we’re not on a trajectory for rapid, legitimate decision making.

Reflective is a global, non-profit research organization aiming to radically accelerate the pace of sunlight reflection research. We equip the world with the data and tools needed to make informed decisions about sunlight reflection, fast enough to matter.

What you'll do

Reflective studies stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) through modeling and, where the science requires it, by assessing the feasibility of small-scale outdoor experiments. Our modeling work includes AIDE-SAI, a linked set of machine-learning emulators that simulates SAI end to end, from stratospheric circulation through aerosol microphysics to radiation. Both the modeling framework and experiment feasibility assessment require better representation of plume evolution at scales our current global tools do not resolve: the global emulators only carry injected material once it has spread across a grid box, while a field study would need to forecast where a plume is and how it dilutes over days to weeks.

As Reflective’s Scientist for Plume Modeling and Forecasting, you’ll own that scale. You’ll lead plume forecasting for balloon-based tracer campaigns run with external partners, which test forecasting methods without any aerosol release, and build Reflective’s own forecasting capability out to the 24- to 72-hour horizons a field study would require. You’ll run plume-resolving simulations from release through dispersion and turn the results into dilution rates, an effective source term, and a parameterization the global framework can use. Should a field study proceed, you’ll serve as mission scientist.

The role sits between the multi-scale team and the experiment team and reports to Reflective’s Head of Research, Marianna Linz. You’ll work daily with the OSSE Senior Scientist, who owns observing-system design and parameter estimation and runs that work from your plume simulations; the In-Situ Observing Lead and instrument specialists, who own the instruments and rely on you to tell them where to look; the experiment operations lead, who owns aircraft contracting, shipping, permitting, and in-country operations; and Reflective’s external forecasting and modeling partners.

Responsibilities

  • Lead plume forecasting for balloon-based tracer campaigns run with external partners, working within the partner’s data assimilation and forecasting process while developing in-house capabilities. These campaigns test forecasting methods and are distinct from the potential aerosol microphysics experiment.
  • Develop and evaluate plume forecasting capabilities over the 24- to 72-hour horizons a potential field study would require, documenting performance limits and their implications for feasibility.
  • Quantify forecast uncertainty well enough to plan against it: where the ensemble spread puts the plume, how that spread grows with lead time, and what it implies for search patterns and instrument settings.
  • Translate forecast results into requirements for the observing team, including viewing geometry, altitude, timing, and expected plume extent for daytime visualization systems.
  • Model detailed plume evolution to support numerical experiments that test candidate observing suites and sampling cadences at realistic density and instrument fidelity.
  • Verify forecasts from each tracer campaign against what was observed and report plainly where they failed.
  • Own Reflective’s plume-scale modeling: large-eddy and plume-resolving simulations of injected material from release through dispersion, covering the regime the global emulators cannot resolve.
  • Turn plume-scale results into inputs the global framework can use: dilution rates, an effective source term, and a parameterization of plume-scale effects as a function of background conditions.
  • Serve as the multi-scale team’s point of contact for the experiment team on plume-scale questions: what the modeling can predict today, what it can’t, and what observations could settle.
  • Should a field study proceed, serve as mission scientist: real-time forecast updates, go/no-go input, and direction to pilots and instrument operators on where to sample.

Who you are

Minimum qualifications

  • PhD in atmospheric science, fluid dynamics, or a closely related field, or equivalent research experience.
  • Experience running high-resolution or large-eddy simulations of dispersing material (plumes, tracers, or reacting flows) and comparing them against measurements.
  • Hands-on forecasting or mission-science experience on an airborne or balloon field campaign: planning flights from ensemble forecasts and making real-time calls during them.
  • Comfortable in Python and, ideally, Fortran on high-performance computing systems
  • Ability to state clearly what a model result does and does not support, and to write it down so others can act on it.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially with mixed scientific, engineering, and non-technical audiences.
  • You’re creative and attached to outcomes, not process — you’re constantly looking for new paths to the destination and excited to switch gears if there’s a faster, better way to get something done.
  • You are low ego, and have a proven track record for working well across disciplines and with external partners.
  • You are passionate about Reflective’s mission.

Strongly preferred

  • Experience with JAX or other differentiable modeling frameworks.

Not needed

  • Stratospheric experience is helpful but not required. Most of our team learned it on the job.
  • A nonprofit résumé - Reflective is technically a nonprofit, but it doesn’t feel like one — mission fit and rigor matter more than sector pedigree.
  • Formal people-management experience - this role leads technical work and coordinates a team, but is not required to be anyone’s formal manager.

We encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply, regardless of whether you feel you meet 100% of the qualifications. The top candidates will bring their own unique perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds from a variety of industries along with many but not necessarily all the skills listed above. We offer professional learning and training opportunities to help you develop skills you may not have had the opportunity to cultivate yet.

Location

Our goal is to hire the right person for the role regardless of location, but we have a slight preference for candidates who can work from our Bay Area office 2-3 days/week. The role can be fully remote and we are open to candidates based anywhere in the world who can overlap with our core working hours (9am-1pm PST). Au sein de la Tribe Data Platform, la Feature Team (FT) Forge conçoit et fait évoluer les services, outils et standards qui permettent aux équipes Data, Analytics et AI de développer leurs produits dans les meilleures conditions et en autonomie.

Positionnée comme une équipe d'experts Cloud, DataOps, MLops et Platform Engineering, la FT Forge fournit les briques technologiques essentielles de la plateforme data : ingestion, Transformation, orchestration, observabilité, automatisation et expérience développeur.

L'équipe joue également un rôle clé dans l'accélération des initiatives Data Science, Machine Learning et GenAI en mettant à disposition des solutions robustes pour permettre le développement et le déploiement à l’échelle de tout type de modèle IA/ML/DL.

Dans un contexte de forte évolution des usages et des technologies, nous recherchons un.e Cloud Data Platform Engineer capable de combiner expertise technique, pragmatisme et autonomie afin de contribuer à la construction de la plateforme Data de demain et d'accompagner sa montée en échelle.

Votre mission :

  • Construire une offre de services Data Platform orientée produit et Self-Service, en définissant des patterns réutilisables, des services d'ingestion et de transformation standardisés, les SLA associés et les responsabilités claires entre Forge et les Feature Teams.

  • Développer et industrialiser une plateforme data centrée sur Snowflake, en supportant les usages Data Engineering (dbt, Airflow), Analytics, Machine Learning et GenAI, tout en optimisant les performances, la sécurité et les coûts.

  • Jouer un rôle de référent technique et accélérer la montée en compétence des équipes, en concevant les bons parcours d’onboarding, en produisant la documentation digeste, en animant les communautés de pratique, et en promouvant les standards cloud, data, sécurité et FinOps pour garantir une utilisation performante et responsable de la plateforme.

Et vous ?

  • Diplôme d'ingénieur, Master universitaire ou formation équivalente en Informatique, Data, Cloud Computing ou systèmes d'information.

jobs.title: Peer Mentor (Volunteer)
jobs.excerpt: Here at Youth4Youth, we have grown a strong, tight-knit community of individuals who are passionate about making a difference and improving the lives of young people across the UK.
jobs.description:
Here at Youth4Youth, we have grown a strong, tight-knit community of individuals who are passionate about making a difference and improving the lives of young people across the UK. Our growing team of volunteers all contribute, significantly, to the impact that we have as a charity on our direct beneficiaries, regardless of the department that they work in of the level of time that they are able to commit. Our servicesprimarily offer a peer-support network to young people right across the UK, allowing them to access a peer mentor who is of a similar age to them and somebody that they feel more comfortable speaking with.

If successful, you will be joining a growing team of diverse, but likeminded individuals, collaborating to increase the reach of the Charity and improve support provisions available to young people. All of our volunteers and employees are remote workers,but that doesn't stop us keeping in touch and maintaining a strong positive culture amongst our whole team.

About the role

Our Peer Mentors are at the forefront of our Youth Services delivery, tackling head on the issues that young people are facing everyday. As a Peer Mentor, you will engage with young people who reach out to Youth4Youth for support, taking time to coach and guide them through the difficulties that they are facing. This exciting opportunity, targeted at individuals who are between the ages of 16 and 25, provides young people with the space to directly impact and transform the lives of young people, significantly improving their overall wellbeing.

Ideal candidates are those who are able to commit to regular volunteering activity of at least 2 hours per week (on average) and who are able to comfortably communicate via written e-mail and other remote chat functionalities.

Responsibilities:

Your core responsibilities as a Peer Mentor at Youth4Youth include:

  • Building strong, professional relationships with young people seeking mentoring support.
  • Demonstrating commitment to the charity by regular volunteer engagement to maintain ongoing communication with young people (which includes responding to young people within an agreed and reasonable time frame).
  • Providing light support, advice and guidance to young people in relation to the troubles that they are facing, in line with the resources provided to you by the charity.
  • Maintaining professional boundaries with young people and not seeking to offer support beyond your capability that may put a young person at risk.
  • Maintaining regular contact with your Youth4Youth supervisor, with the expectation that you will meet at least once per month for a supervision session that involves reflective practice and a focus on your development as a mentor.
  • Providing support as part of our Peer Mentor network to colleagues across the Charity who are also directly supporting young people.
  • Maintaining compliance with all policies. Most importantly this means maintaining the right level of confidentiality around your conversations with young people and recognising your safeguarding responsibilities in raising concerns as they arise to keep young people safe.

Peer Mentors are also actively encouraged to get involved in fundraising, outreach and social media activities where they feel comfortable and able to.

Skills

  • Strong written communication skills, such as being able to effectively compose a written e-mail in response to a young person.
  • Ability to build strong, professional relationships and maintain trust between yourself and a young person, such as through active listening and adapting to the individual needs of different young people.
  • Ability to demonstrate empathy to others.
  • Ability to work in a challenging environment and recognise when you may need support yourself.
  • Proficient in the use of IT tools, such as Microsoft Outlook.

Our mission is to continue to grow towards becoming one of the best charities in the UK. Our aim is to do this by building a diverse team, rich with different backgrounds and perspectives. Therefore, even if you feel you only are a 75% match, we would still love to hear from you. Skills can be learned, but diversity cannot.

Skills development for you:

As a Peer Mentor at Youth4Youth, you will be required to take part and graduate our Youth Services Academy. This program requires an upfront commitment of 10 - 13 hours of training prior to taking on the role of communicating with young people. This investment in you not only equips you with the understanding of what it takes to be a successful peer mentor, and the skills that you will need, but also is an investment in you. This training will provide you with core soft skills that are transferrable to many opportunities, whether that's in everyday life for you, your education setting or your place of work. All Mentors graduating from the Youth Services Academy will be provided with an electronic certificate to demonstrate your successful completion of the program, which can be shared with potential employers.

Benefits of volunteering with Youth4Youth

We recognise that you will be joining us and giving your time as an 'in-kind' donation, but there must be benefits for you too. When joining our team, you will be open to the following benefits:

  • Professional and personal development opportunities in a variety of skill areas through volunteering in real roles. This may be general development or tailored to your specific needs or ambitions
  • Becoming a member of a strong network of likeminded individuals, spread across the UK, who you can connect with and collaborate with both within and outside of the Charity
  • Access to bespoke discounts, specifically designed for non-profit workers and Youth4Youth volunteers
  • Opportunities to truly shape the future of the Charity, having a direct influence over the impact that Youth4Youth has on its direct beneficiaries

The hiring process:

Unlike other roles at Youth4Youth, the hiring process has been simplified for peer mentors, recognising the demographic of individuals that we are seeking to fill these positions. To put you at ease, the hiring process includes:

  • An initial application, stating your reasons for wishing to become a Peer Mentor
  • A remote interview conducted via Microsoft Teams

Successful candidates at this stage will be invited into the final stage of the recruitment process which includes:

  • Satisfactory references being received (these do not need to be employment references)
  • A satisfactory DBS check being received
  • Successful completion of the Youth Services Academy

jobs.excerpt: Storyblok is a headless CMS that enables marketers and developers to create with joy and publish with confidence.
jobs.description:
Storyblok is a headless CMS that enables marketers and developers to create with joy and publish with confidence. It empowers you to deliver structured and consistent content everywhere: websites, apps, AI search, and beyond.

Legendary brands like Virgin Media O2, Oatly, and TomTom use Storyblok to make a bigger, faster market impact.

WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU

You will be joining a growing company where you can contribute to many “firsts”. Plus these benefits:

  • Monthly remote work stipend (home internet costs, electricity). Home office equipment package right at the start (laptop, keyboard, monitor…)
  • Home office equipment upgrade (furniture, ear plugs …) or membership to a local co-working space after your onboarding
  • Sick leave benefit, parental leave and 25 days of annual leave plus your local national holidays
  • Personal development fund for courses, books, conferences, and material
  • The annual international team-building trip, quarterly and monthly online get-togethers
  • As a fully remote company, with work-life balance at its core, you’ll enjoy flexible schedules
  • An international team that loves to have fun at work and works hard together to accomplish shared goals

JOB SUMMARY

You will own the reliability, performance, and cost efficiency of the PostgreSQL data platform behind our flagship CMS — primarily Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL — along with the infrastructure and automation around it.

This is a reliability engineering role, not a classic administration one. Aurora takes care of patching, backups, failover, and storage growth; you own what it does not — query and index strategy, plan regressions across major version upgrades, vacuum and bloat, connection management, zero-downtime schema change, logical replication, and capacity and cost modeling. Alongside this, you work as a full member of the Infrastructure team on Terraform, CI/CD, observability, and security tooling, and you share the on-call rotation.

You will work in a shared-ownership model: backend teams own their queries and schemas, and you own the platform, guardrails, tooling, and knowledge-sharing that make their decisions safe. You will collaborate closely with backend engineers, DevOps engineers, Security, product owners, and the Data team.

We measure success by the reliability and predictable performance of the data platform, the quality of your incident response, and how well other engineering teams are equipped to make sound database decisions without you in the room.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Database platform (approx. 60%)

  • Own the reliability, performance, and scalability of our PostgreSQL platform (primarily Amazon Aurora): query and index strategy, execution plans, configuration tuning, and capacity planning, with particular attention to hot multi-tenant read paths.
  • Lead zero-downtime version upgrades and schema migrations at scale, including diagnosing and preventing plan regressions across Aurora major versions.
  • Own the operational health of the platform: vacuum strategy and bloat, long-running transactions and wraparound risk, connection management and pooling (including RDS Proxy), lock contention, and logical replication and slot hygiene.
  • Review schema changes and DDL from backend teams for lock behavior, migration safety, and performance impact, and build the guardrails and tooling that make safe changes to the default path.
  • Own backup, restore, and disaster recovery end-to-end, including rehearsed restore drills and the access, encryption, and auditing controls our compliance obligations require.
  • Model database capacity and cost (I/O-Optimized vs. Standard, Serverless v2 sizing, read replica strategy) and drive cost-efficiency without compromising reliability.

Infrastructure and automation (approx. 40%)

  • Deliver infrastructure and automation as a full member of the Infrastructure team, using Terraform and cloud-native tooling on AWS, and contribute to CI/CD pipelines including the safe automated handling of database changes.
  • Build and maintain monitoring, alerting, and observability for database and platform systems (e.g. pg_stat_statements, Prometheus exporters, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry) so problems surface before customers feel them.
  • Use cloud security and vulnerability management tooling (such as Aikido) to triage findings and keep the team's services compliant.

Team, incidents, and collaboration

  • Take part in the on-call rotation, incident response, and postmortems, driving root cause analysis and remediation that prevents recurrence.
  • Raise the database competence of the wider engineering organization through design reviews, documentation and runbooks, and mentoring — so this expertise is not concentrated in one person.
  • Demonstrate AI literacy, leveraging AI tools to enhance productivity, decision-making, and quality of work while applying sound judgment and critical thinking.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE; QUALIFICATIONS

Required — PostgreSQL depth

  • 7+ years in database engineering, database reliability, infrastructure, or SRE roles, including significant hands-on ownership of production PostgreSQL.
  • Deep PostgreSQL expertise: internals and MVCC, reading and acting on EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), indexing strategy, vacuum behavior, locking, connection pooling, and configuration tuning.
  • Strong experience with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and AWS-managed database services.
  • Proven track record of zero-downtime upgrades and complex schema migrations on large, busy tables.
  • Hands-on experience with physical and logical replication, partitioning, read scaling, and designing and validating backup and disaster-recovery strategies.

Required — Infrastructure and ways of working

  • Solid experience with Infrastructure-as-Code, primarily Terraform, on AWS.
  • Strong Linux fundamentals plus fluency in at least one scripting language (Bash, Python, Ruby, or Go) for automation and tooling.
  • Experience with monitoring and observability tooling, and a solid grasp of security practices (IAM, secrets management, network segmentation).
  • Experience with change, incident, and problem management in production, and with Git and modern CI/CD workflows applied to database changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication in a remote-first organization, including the ability to explain database trade-offs to backend engineers and non-specialists.
  • Willingness and ability to participate in an on-call rotation.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with backend frameworks that interact with PostgreSQL (Ruby on Rails preferred; Python, Rust, or Elixir valued).
  • Experience with caching layers (Redis, Memcached) and their interaction with database load.
  • Exposure to analytics pipelines and warehousing (Redshift, Snowflake, ClickHouse) or CDC-based data flows.
  • Experience with container platforms (ECS, EKS, Fargate), NoSQL or vector databases, or AWS certification (Database – Specialty, DevOps Engineer – Professional).

MENTAL, PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS

Remote (home) work opportunity or funded by Storyblok co-working space

At Aztec Group we credit our technology as one of the core ingredients to our award-winning outsourced solutions. We are currently looking for an Enterprise Data Architect to join our architecture team and help Aztec to deliver their exciting new technology strategy, leveraging Databricks.

  • Design data architectures that enable AI adoption — ensuring data is discoverable, well-governed, and AI-ready for machine learning, GenAI, and agentic use cases across the business.

Skills, knowledge and expertise:

  • Practical experience with Databricks Delta Sharing and designing integration patterns for external data sharing (e.g. Delta Sharing, secure APIs, event streaming, managed file transfer), including the security and contractual considerations involved.

  • Demonstrable expertise in Databricks performance and cost optimisation at scale.

  • Strong data modelling skills (dimensional, 3NF, Data Vault or similar) and experience defining enterprise data models.

  • Solid grounding in Azure, including storage, networking, and identity concepts relevant to data platforms.

  • Experience with data governance frameworks and tools (e.g. Microsoft Purview), data quality management, metadata, and lineage tooling.

  • Strong SQL and working knowledge of Python and/or Spark.

  • Understanding of data security and privacy: encryption, access control (RBAC/ABAC), data masking, and regulatory compliance (GDPR).

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain architectural decisions in plain language to executive and non-technical audiences.

jobs.title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner Remote (Alaska Residents Only)
jobs.excerpt: About Frontier Psychiatry Frontier Psychiatry is a physician-led, tech-enabled telehealth organization on a mission to improve the mental wellbeing of people in rural communities nationwide.
jobs.description:
About Frontier Psychiatry
Frontier Psychiatry is a physician-led, tech-enabled telehealth organization on a mission to improve the mental wellbeing of people in rural communities nationwide. We deliver timely, scalable, and evidence-based care in psychiatry and addiction medicine through innovative virtual solutions that expand access to those who need it most.

Since our launch, Frontier Psychiatry has grown rapidly while maintaining a deep commitment to our founding purpose — lifting the mental wellbeing of underserved populations. Our work is guided by healthcare’s Quintuple Aim, which drives every decision we make:

  • Deliver excellent patient care.
  • Support the well-being of our team.
  • Lower the total cost of care.
  • Improve the population health of the communities we serve.
  • Advance health equity.

If you’re passionate about meaningful work, innovation in behavioral health, and making a lasting difference in people’s lives, we’d love for you to join our team.

This is a fully remote position. While you'll enjoy the flexibility of working from home, applicants must reside within the state of Alaska to be considered for this opportunity.

Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner

Remote. Alaska residents only.

$160,000 to $195,000 per year in total compensation

The Short Version

  • Full-time means 36 scheduled patient-care hours per week. Documentation time is built into the work week, not added on top of it.
  • No call. No nights. No weekends. Your time off is actually off.
  • 1-hour initial evaluations and 30-minute follow-ups. We do not run 15-minute med checks, and we do not want you to.
  • Alaska providers caring for Alaskans. You will live in the state you serve. Fully remote from anywhere in Alaska.
  • W-2 employee. Base salary plus production-based income, totaling $160,000 to $195,000.
  • Healthie EHR with Nabla AI documentation, so your notes are largely written by the time the visit ends.
  • Direct access to experienced subspecialty psychiatrists for mentorship and case guidance, plus a clinical pharmacist on staff.

Why This Role Exists

Alaska has some of the lowest per-capita access to psychiatric care in the country. Patients in rural counties wait months for an appointment, then drive hours to keep it. Many never make the drive.

Frontier Psychiatry exists to close that gap. Our Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners carry that work. You will hold your own panel, evaluate and treat a broad range of psychiatric conditions, and give patients timely care they could not otherwise get.

We are hiring an Alaskan-based provider on purpose. Telehealth makes it easy to beam a clinician in from anywhere, and plenty of companies do exactly that. We think care is better when the person delivering it knows the towns, the winters, the distances, and the local resources a patient can actually reach. If you live here, you already understand what your patients are describing.

This is direct clinical work with a clear purpose behind it.

Schedule & Commitment

This is a full-time, W-2 position.

Full-time is defined as 36 scheduled patient-care hours per week. Those hours are the appointment slots on your calendar. The remaining hours in your standard work week are yours for documentation, refills, care coordination, and required meetings.

We say this plainly because clinicians have been burned by postings that do not.

What your schedule looks like

  • Initial evaluations are 1 hour. Follow-ups are 30 minutes.
  • We discourage 15-minute med checks. Short visits move volume and produce worse care, and we have built the schedule to avoid them.
  • No call, no after-hours coverage, no weekend rotation.
  • Weekly Provider Rounds and a monthly All-Staff meeting, both inside the work week.

What You'll Do

Clinical care

  • Evaluate, diagnose, and treat patients across a broad range of psychiatric conditions using evidence-based practice
  • Prescribe medications and deliver psychotherapeutic interventions as appropriate
  • Manage your panel based on clinical acuity, keeping follow-up intervals appropriate to patient need

Collaboration and mentorship

  • Bring complex cases to experienced subspecialty psychiatrists on our clinical team, including child and adolescent and addiction specialists
  • Consult with our clinical pharmacist on complicated medication questions
  • Coordinate with primary care providers, therapists, schools, and families as appropriate
  • Contribute to interdisciplinary treatment planning discussions

Documentation

  • Complete accurate notes for every encounter in Healthie, supported by Nabla AI documentation
  • Close documentation within 48 hours of the visit
  • Follow clinic policies, prescribing standards, and state and federal regulatory requirements

Growth

  • Stay current on developments in psychiatric treatment
  • Use your CME benefit and bring what you learn back to the team

What Success Looks Like

In your first 30 days: You are credentialed, onboarded, and seeing patients. You know your scheduler, your pharmacist, and the psychiatrists you can call by name.

By 90 days: Your panel is full. Your notes close within 48 hours. You are comfortable bringing complex cases forward and you know who to bring them to.

Over your first year: Your patients stay engaged and get better. Your colleagues rely on your clinical judgment. You are practicing at the top of your license without drowning in administrative work.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • MSN or DNP with a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner specialization
  • Board certification as a PMHNP-BC
  • Active, unrestricted Alaska Nurse Practitioner license, or eligibility for one before your start date
  • Clinical experience diagnosing and treating psychiatric conditions
  • A home setup that supports private, reliable telehealth visits
  • Strong written communication, since much of your collaboration will happen in writing

Helpful, not required

  • Experience with rural or underserved populations
  • Child and adolescent experience
  • Buprenorphine prescribing experience
  • Additional state licenses

If you meet most of this and not all of it, apply anyway. We would rather read your application than guess.

What We Offer

Expanding access to psychiatric care depends on supporting the clinicians who deliver it. That means real support, not a mission statement.

  • 100% remote
  • 3 weeks of paid vacation (120 hours), plus 40 hours of sick time
  • Your birthday off, paid
  • 9.5 paid holidays
  • 401(k) with company match
  • 100% employer-paid premiums for employee-only medical, dental, vision, and accident coverage
  • HSA option
  • Stock options
  • Company-provided equipment
  • $500 per year toward continuing education
  • Malpractice insurance fully covered
  • Licensure costs covered in every state where you provide care

Pay: $160,000 to $195,000 per year in total compensation for Alaska. Pay is a base salary plus production-based income. The range above reflects expected total earnings, not base alone.

About Frontier Psychiatry

Frontier Psychiatry is a physician-led, tech-enabled telehealth organization improving mental wellbeing in rural communities. We deliver psychiatry and addiction medicine through virtual care built specifically for places where care is hardest to reach.

We are a training site for the Yale Child Study Center, and our published research in JAMA Network Open found 38% lower hospitalization rates among the Montana Medicaid patients we serve. We are guided by healthcare's Quintuple Aim: excellent patient care, a supported team, lower total cost of care, better population health, and greater health equity.

How to Apply

Apply through the link on this page. You will hear from us within one week. The process is a 30-minute recruiter call, a clinical conversation, and a final conversation with a peer clinician. Most candidates finish in two to three weeks.

Frontier Psychiatry is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by law.

Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA)

Remote | Chiropractic Clinic | 30 Hours/Week | $5/hour with performance-based increase after 6 months

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly capable Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA) to support the overall operational health of a busy healthcare clinic. This role is ideal for someone who is very sharp, proactive, detail-oriented, emotionally intelligent, and able to take ownership of important clinic workflows with minimal supervision.

This is not a basic task-following role. The ideal candidate must be able to think ahead, identify operational gaps, take initiative, and help remove administrative and billing-related tasks from the provider's plate.

We are looking for someone with excellent English communication skills, strong executive presence, high accountability, and the ability to build a trust-based working relationship with the provider and care team.

Key Responsibilities

Insurance Verification

Verify patient insurance after the patient checks in, typically around 15 minutes after the scheduled appointment time. Ensure all insurance information is accurate, updated, and properly documented.

Denied Claims Management

Review denied claims, identify denial reasons, and assist with claim reprocessing. Track issues, follow up on missing information, and help prevent repeat claim errors.

EOB Processing

Review and process Explanation of Benefits documents. Help organize, validate, and clear EOB backlogs while ensuring billing and insurance documentation is accurate.

Patient Balance Resolution

Review outstanding insurance balances and patient account issues. Track unresolved balances, identify the source of the issue, and coordinate next steps for resolution.

Claims Processing

Support claims-related workflows, including Cigna and Veterans Affairs claims. Ensure claims are reviewed, tracked, and escalated when necessary.

Payment Coordination

Assist with vendor payment coordination, including check payments when needed. Ensure payment-related tasks are completed accurately and on time.

SOAP Note Monitoring

Monitor SOAP note completion, accuracy, and compliance. Track missing, incomplete, or delayed documentation and communicate concerns appropriately.

Appointment Tracking

Track missed appointments, canceled appointments, and scheduling trends. Identify patterns that may affect clinic revenue, patient flow, or provider productivity.

Reports and Operational Tracking

Prepare reports on outstanding balances, missed appointments, canceled appointments, EOB backlog, denied claims, and other operational metrics. Reports should include clear insights and practical recommendations when needed.

Team Coordination

Support smooth communication between the provider, care team, and administrative staff. Help ensure updates are clearly shared, priorities are followed through, and important tasks are not missed.

Operational Support

Proactively identify workflow gaps, billing concerns, documentation delays, scheduling issues, and patient account problems. Recommend practical solutions to improve clinic efficiency.

Mandatory Requirements

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant

  • Experience supporting a US healthcare practice

  • Experience with insurance verification, EOBs, claims, denied claims, patient balances, or billing support

  • Exposure to CPT and ICD-10 codes

  • Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal

  • Strong executive presence and professional communication style

  • Must be a Mac OS user

  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

  • Proven leadership, ownership, or high-accountability experience in a previous role

Required Soft Skills

  • Proactive and able to anticipate needs before being asked

  • Highly detail-oriented with billing, documentation, and reporting tasks

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

  • Emotionally intelligent and patient when working with a busy provider

  • Confident, professional, and organized in communication

  • Able to take personal responsibility for assigned work

  • Resourceful and self-motivated when learning new workflows

  • Trustworthy, dependable, and comfortable handling sensitive information

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience supporting a chiropractic clinic

  • Experience with Cigna or Veterans Affairs claims

  • Experience clearing EOB or billing backlogs

  • Experience preparing operational or billing reports

  • Experience mentoring, training, or supporting new team members

  • Experience working closely with a clinic owner, provider, or executive-level leader

Schedule and Compensation

  • Schedule: Monday to Friday

  • Hours: 6 hours per day, 30 hours per week

  • Rate: $6 per hour

  • Work Setup: Remote

The ideal candidate is someone who does not wait to be told every step. This person should be observant, organized, and confident enough to identify what needs attention.

They should be able to manage detailed billing and administrative tasks while also thinking about the bigger picture of clinic operations. The right candidate will be sharp, emotionally intelligent, highly reliable, and capable of becoming a trusted operational support partner for the provider and care team.

In addition to driving rule implementation, the Senior Technical Specialist will act as a key liaison between the operations team and the BRMS Center of Excellence—ensuring strong alignment with end-user needs—and will maintain comprehensive documentation, impact analysis, and reporting for all rule activity. This role supports continuous improvement by conducting root cause and gap analyses to identify where rules are not producing the intended outcomes, and by developing data-driven solutions to optimize performance.

  • Receive business rules from various internal Cotiviti teams.
  • Collaborate with internal partners to clarify the intent and context of each rule.

  • Conduct testing and validation of rules in non-production environments to verify accuracy.

  • Communicate rule deployment outcomes and changes to operations and key stakeholders.

  • Clear Explanations: A mindset of simplifying complex technical issues and presenting them in a way that the customer or user can understand.

jobs.excerpt: At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the Product team

The Product team listens to our customers’ needs and translates those insights into a clear product vision. The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision.

About the role

Millions of people use the Affirm Card, but we don’t yet give them a reason to keep coming back beyond the product itself. You’ll build our consumer loyalty program from scratch: what people earn, how they move up, and why Affirm becomes their default way to pay.

What you’ll do

  • Own the vision and roadmap for Affirm’s consumer loyalty program, setting the hypotheses, success metrics, and sequencing across multiple quarters

  • Launch the first version of rewards and tiers, including earn mechanics, member benefits, redemption, and the surfaces that make the value obvious in app, at checkout, and after a purchase

  • Build the engagement loops (progress, milestones, personalized offers) that turn a one-time borrower into someone who reaches for Affirm every week

  • Own the program economics: reward liability, funding mix across merchant-funded offers, interchange and network incentives, and the case for incremental GMV against cost per member

  • Set up the measurement foundation for loyalty, including holdouts, incrementality testing and long-run LTV, then tune earn and burn rates and tier thresholds off what the data says

  • Partner with Risk, Credit, Legal, Compliance, Finance and Marketing to design rewards that are compliant and clearly disclosed, with no hidden fees or fine print that surprises people

  • Align senior stakeholders and pull together dependencies across Card, Shopping, Servicing and Marketing, leading embedded engineering and design pods through a lot of ambiguity

What we look for

  • 8+ years in Product Management, with a track record in consumer mobile apps, fintech, or neobanks

  • Built or scaled a loyalty, rewards or engagement program: card rewards, points, tiers, subscription benefits, or something equivalent. You know earn and burn mechanics and what makes a program pay for itself

  • History of launching products from scratch, not just optimizing what already exists

  • Owned repeat usage, cohort retention or share of wallet as a primary metric, and know which levers actually move them

  • Comfortable building the financial model yourself and defending reward cost, funding mix and payback to Finance and leadership

  • Strong UX instincts and a high bar for design. You know the difference between a reward that feels good and a badge buried in a settings menu

  • Deep fluency in experiment design, incrementality/attribution, and LTV measurement; data chops (SQL/Amplitude-level self-serve) and a bias for shipping, learning and iterating quickly

  • Track record shipping consumer financial or regulated products; comfort partnering with Risk/Credit, Legal, and Compliance

  • Excellent cross-functional leadership, including experience leading without authority

  • AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and others to research, analyze and prototype, and help develop better product vision

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience

Base Pay Grade - P

Equity Grade - 7

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).

CAN base pay range per year: $181,000 - $241,000

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Remote-first with flexibility built inAffirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

Benefits designed for youOur benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

  • Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
  • Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
  • Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
  • Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.

For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.

jobs.excerpt: EN will followÀ propos d’Akinox Akinox est une entreprise canadienne de santé numérique qui vise à améliorer l’accès des patients aux soins ainsi que la façon dont les organisations de santé les offrent.
jobs.description:
EN will follow

À propos d’Akinox

Akinox est une entreprise canadienne de santé numérique qui vise à améliorer l’accès des patients aux soins ainsi que la façon dont les organisations de santé les offrent. Depuis plus de 15 ans, Akinox collabore avec des organisations de santé et des gouvernements afin de concevoir et d’exploiter des solutions de santé numérique à grande échelle. Nos activités couvrent notamment les soins de première ligne, les soins virtuels, l’accès aux soins et la transformation des processus cliniques.

Le rôle

Nous recherchons une personne rigoureuse et organisée pour soutenir et coordonner les activités de conformité, de sécurité de l’information et de gouvernance de l’organisation. Un intérêt marqué pour l’intelligence artificiel sera considéré comme un important atout.

Dans ce rôle à temps partiel (3 jours/semaine), vous serez responsable du maintien des activités courantes de conformité et contribuerez aux différents cycles d’audit, de gestion des risques et de certification. Vous collaborerez étroitement avec les équipes de sécurité, technologie, produit et opérations, ainsi qu’avec différents partenaires externes.

Principales responsabilités

  • Administrer et maintenir le programme de conformité et la plateforme GRC, incluant les contrôles, preuves et suivis.
  • Maintenir le registre des risques et assurer le suivi des vulnérabilités, non-conformités, mesures correctives et échéances.
  • Maintenir et mettre à jour les politiques, procédures et contrôles de conformité.
  • Coordonner la préparation aux audits, certifications et autres activités de conformité, notamment ISO 27001 et ISO 9001.
  • Maintenir les indicateurs requis pour les objectifs ISO 27001 et les activités liées à ISO 9001, et préparer les éléments nécessaires aux revues de gestion.
  • Coordonner les tests d’intrusion, attestations et autres évaluations de sécurité lorsque requis.
  • Soutenir la gouvernance des changements et les exigences de conformité associées aux mises en production.
  • Participer aux évaluations de risques liées aux nouveaux fournisseurs, partenaires, intégrations et projets.
  • Faire un suivi 60-90 jours à l’avance des audits, attestations, tests d’intrusion, revues d’accès, renouvellement et besoins de preuves.
  • Effectuer les suivis auprès des propriétaires de contrôles, risques, non-conformités et actions correctives afin que les éléments soient complétés dans les délais.
  • Soutenir les demandes de clients et prospects en matière de sécurité, confidentialité et conformité, incluant les RFP et activités de diligence raisonnable.
  • Coordonner les évaluations d’impact sur la vie privée (EFVP/PIA) et l’évaluation des risques associés aux nouveaux outils ou usages de l’intelligence artificielle.
  • Administrer les activités de formation et de sensibilisation en sécurité et conformité.
  • Effectuer une veille réglementaire et identifier les nouvelles exigences nécessitant une action.
  • Coordonner les activités de conformité lors d’incidents de confidentialité ou de sécurité.

What you'll bring

Location: Remote, with mission-driven travel. Travel volume varies considerably by season and program; we’re happy to discuss specifics with candidates.

About Somewear Labs

Somewear Labs builds communication and unmanned systems technology for mission-critical operations in challenging environments.

Job Summary

The Mission Support Engineer – Networking is a hands-on, forward-deployed technical expert who owns the success of our communications and networking deployments — from pre-mission preparation through execution and recovery. You will translate mission requirements into working network architectures, diagnose problems in austere conditions, and enable operators to use the capability confidently on their own.

Key Responsibilities

Mission Support & Field Execution

  • Own technical execution of communications and networking deployments, including trials, evaluations, demonstrations, exercises, and operational missions.

  • Serve as the on-site technical owner for network readiness, configuration, troubleshooting, and mission performance.

  • Conduct pre-mission checks, equipment preparation, configuration, and readiness assessments; support post-mission recovery, documentation, and after-action review.

  • Translate mission requirements into practical connectivity and network architecture.

  • Drive issues to resolution in the field using structured troubleshooting and sound engineering judgment rather than escalation.

Network Engineering & Troubleshooting

  • Configure, operate, maintain, and troubleshoot mission networking and communications equipment.

  • Troubleshoot IP addressing and subnetting, routing, NAT, DHCP, DNS, VPNs, tunnels, encrypted overlays, and firewall and traffic filtering rules.

  • Diagnose MTU, latency, packet loss, and constrained-bandwidth problems, and capture and analyze traffic using tools such as tcpdump and Wireshark.

  • Deploy and troubleshoot video streaming over constrained and contested links, including RTSP, RTP/UDP, SRT, MPEG-TS, WebRTC, and HLS; H.264/H.265 encoding; and ONVIF-compliant cameras and encoders.

  • Tune video streams for available bandwidth and latency budgets — bitrate, resolution, GOP and keyframe interval, buffering, multicast versus unicast — and resolve firewall, NAT traversal, and transcoding issues affecting feeds to ATAK, ground control stations, and downstream consumers.

  • Work with RF communications and satellite or other beyond-line-of-sight connectivity as the mission requires.

Linux, Software & Automation

  • Administer and troubleshoot Linux from the command line: processes and services, logs, network interfaces, routing tables, firewall rules, permissions, packages and dependencies, and system resource utilization.

  • Work with APIs, configuration files, logs, and command-line tools to configure systems and diagnose mission issues.

  • Build temporary diagnostic tools, scripts, or workarounds when needed to isolate a problem or keep a mission moving.

Customer Enablement & Product Feedback

  • Train operators on network setup, communications workflows, and troubleshooting, and support onboarding into operational use.

  • Advise customers on incorporating the technology into SOPs, CONOPs, and training pipelines, and deliver technical briefs and demonstrations covering capabilities and limitations.

  • Synthesize operator feedback and field observations for Product and Engineering, and help validate new capabilities and integrations prior to launch.

Qualifications

Required

  • Hands-on, engineering-level experience diagnosing and resolving networking and communications problems in field, tactical, or other mission-critical environments.

  • Strong practical networking knowledge across the areas described above, including packet capture and analysis.

  • Working experience with video streaming protocols and codecs (RTSP, RTP/UDP, SRT, MPEG-TS, WebRTC, HLS; H.264/H.265) and with troubleshooting video delivery over bandwidth-constrained links.

  • Proficiency administering and troubleshooting Linux systems from the command line.

  • Working knowledge of RF communications and at least one beyond-line-of-sight, satellite, or tactical communications environment.

  • Ability to read and interpret technical documentation, network diagrams, configurations, and standard operating procedures.

  • Experience briefing, training, or supporting military, government, or defense customers.

  • Strong problem-solving, field judgment, and communication skills.

  • Ability to travel a minimum of 25%.

  • Relevant field, military, technical, or operational experience may substitute for an engineering degree.

Preferred

  • Prior Mission Operations, Field Operations, Program Support, Field Service, Network Operations, or Technical Pre-Sales experience.

  • Experience supporting large-scale government evaluations, operational tests, field exercises, or deployed communications missions.

  • Experience with satellite communications, tactical or mesh networking, or RF systems in austere environments.

  • Familiarity with Somewear Labs' platforms or similar technologies.

jobs.title: Event Manager, India
jobs.excerpt: This is a remote position. Event Manager, IndiaRemote (India) | Full-Time Also searched as: Event Coordinator, Event Project Manager, Event Operations Manager, Project Manager Could you deliver a flawless day for hundreds of students in a city you have never set foot in?
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Event Manager, IndiaRemote (India) | Full-Time

Also searched as: Event Coordinator, Event Project Manager, Event Operations Manager, Project Manager

Could you deliver a flawless day for hundreds of students in a city you have never set foot in?

On a typical day you might walk a venue coordinator in Melbourne through your room and AV requirements in the morning, lock catering numbers against the live registration count and follow up two presenter confirmations with the academic team after lunch, and update the run sheet and brief the on-ground leads before you log off.

About Contour

We started in 2020 with a handful of students and a belief that great education should not be out of reach. Today we operate across three brands with 8,000+ students and 425+ team members: roughly 100 in India and 325 onshore in Australia. The India team runs publishing, student experience, CRM and technology, operations, and people and culture, and this role sits with the events function that delivers Contour's event calendar across Australia.

A great event looks effortless to the family walking in. Someone has to be the reason it looks that way.

About This Role

You are the dedicated project manager behind Contour's events. The calendar runs from full exam simulation days for hundreds of students to revision lecture series selling thousands of tickets across Victoria and Queensland, with parent workshops and online sessions in between. You take each one from first brief to post-event review: timeline, venue, suppliers, registration milestones, comms deadlines, run sheet, event-day coordination, wrap-up.

You report to the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO). The CMO owns marketing strategy and the onshore event-day call when someone must be in the room. Everything else about how events get planned and delivered is yours. Marketing owns promotion, creative, and the registration campaigns. Academics owns session content and who presents it. Operations owns student data and check-in technology. On event day, teams on the ground in Australia execute in the room. The plan that ties them together, the dates they all work to, and the accountability for the day landing well: those are yours.

Two qualities separate a strong hire from an average one here. First, you think in dependencies: you see that catering numbers hang off registration close, which hangs off a reminder email, which hangs off a presenter confirming a title, and you fix the weak link three weeks early instead of discovering it three days out. Second, you follow up without souring relationships: you ask specifically, escalate when twice was enough, and people still enjoy working with you.

One more reality worth naming: you will rarely be in the room. You run events from India that are delivered in Australia, which means your plans, run sheets, and briefings have to be strong enough that the day runs without you standing in it.

You start as the sole dedicated event project manager, plugged into established marketing, academic, operations, and student experience teams. The calendar has grown faster than the way it is run: the biggest series now sell out lecture theatres, and until now no single person has owned how events get delivered. You build that playbook: the standard project plan, the run sheet format, the review loop that makes each event sharper than the last.

By the end of month three, you will have taken at least one major event from brief through delivery to review, built the project plan and run sheet templates the team reuses, and mapped the full calendar with owners, dates, and dependencies visible to everyone involved. What you build in those months will run every event Contour delivers after them.

Where the Work Lives

  • monday.com: project plans and task ownership live here. Keeping status current is how a remote team knows an event is on track without asking.

  • Google Sheets: run sheets, attendee lists, and event-day logistics. The people delivering the day work from your latest version, so document discipline is part of the job.

  • Eventbrite: registrations and ticketing. You watch the numbers daily because rooms, catering, and comms decisions all key off them.

  • HubSpot: student and guardian event comms run through it, alongside the lifecycle comms team.

  • Slack: where cross-team, cross-timezone coordination happens, in writing.

What You Will Do

  • Own each event end to end.Scope, timeline, suppliers, delivery, invoices, review: nothing about the event is someone else's problem.

  • Build and drive the project plan.Every task with an owner, a date, and a dependency in monday.com. When something slips, you catch it while there is still room to re-sequence.

  • Keep the full event calendar visible.Every event, owner, and key date in one place in monday.com, so anyone can see what's coming without asking you.

  • Coordinate Marketing, Academics, and Operations.Registration launches, presenter confirmations, resource handovers, comms milestones: you set the dates and hold every team to them.

  • Lock venues and suppliers.Room requirements, AV, catering, printing, signage: briefed clearly, confirmed in writing, and settled before their cutoffs.

  • Run registrations as a control signal.Work with the digital team on ticket setup in Eventbrite, track numbers daily, and trigger capacity, waitlist, and extra-session calls in good time, because 850 registrations against 760 seats is a problem you want weeks of notice on, not days.

  • Write the run sheet and brief the day.Minute by minute, with named owners for every stage, and briefings that leave the teams in the room certain of their part.

  • Close the loop.Attendance data, feedback, supplier invoices, a short post-event report, and fixes carried into the next plan.

If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.


Requirements

What You Need

  • 4 to 6 years delivering projects or events where you held the whole timeline, not a slice of it

  • You have delivered work that depended on people who did not report to you, and it landed anyway

  • Comfortable chasing and escalating. A quiet slip three weeks out becomes an event-day crisis, so persistence here is method, not personality, and the people you chase still want to work with you again.

  • Writing that lands exactly as intended. Your documents are how a remote coordinator directs a live day, so they carry more weight than they would in an office

  • Clean document and data habits: plans, lists, and versions other people can trust without checking with you

  • Comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference, with the flexibility to be on deck when events go live

Nice to Have

  • You have run an event remotely, delivered in a city or country you were not in

  • Events for education, exams, or student and family audiences

  • Hands-on with monday.com, Eventbrite, or HubSpot

  • Negotiating with venues and suppliers

The Kind of People Who Thrive Here
The people who do well here see a gap and close it without being asked, holding the bar even when the clock is short. They give a direct read on the work in front of them, including when it's wrong, and when their own idea doesn't hold up, they say so and bring a better one. They build something that keeps running after they step back. Problems here don't show up on schedule or in the same shape twice, and they'd rather make the right call on limited information than let something break while they wait for a sign-off. That's the job. They name the blocker and the ask the moment they have it, on a call or a text, because decisions get made on the information you bring.

Contour's current cluster heads started as team leads. The path from operator to leader is real here.

What Good Looks Like

  • Nothing slips silently:every at-risk date is flagged with a re-plan attached, not just an apology.

  • The day runs off the document:venue and floor teams execute from your run sheet without needing you on the phone every ten minutes.

  • Stakeholders answer you:your asks are specific, dated, and easy to action, so people respond instead of stalling.

  • Every event beats the last:reviews turn into changes in the next plan, not a document nobody opens.


Benefits

Fully remote, anywhere in India. The events themselves happen in Australia; you coordinate them from wherever you are, and onshore teams deliver on the day. Compensation details shared early in the hiring process. After you apply: a short screen, a practical planning task, then a culture conversation with our People team, and a final interview with the Chief Marketing Officer, in about four weeks.

Apply with a CV and one paragraph on the most complex event or project you have delivered, and the moment it nearly went wrong.

Are you ready to own the cloud foundation behind a market-leading financial data business? At OptionMetrics, we're looking for a Senior Cloud Infrastructure & DevOps Engineer to own our multi-account AWS environment, our client-facing file-delivery platform, the deployment pipelines and scheduled workflows that ship our data, and the security controls around all of it. Our clients and internal teams depend on this infrastructure every day. You'll keep it reliable, automate how it runs, and leave it better documented than you found it.

You'll report to the Head of IT Operations and work closely with Engineering, Product, Sales and Customer Support.

What You'll Own:

    Client file delivery (CrushFTP): Production, test and DMZ environments on autoscaling and S3, client and support account provisioning, and operating the legacy platform through its retirement.

    AWS multi-account foundation: Organizations, SSO and IAM, the Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke network, and the migration of workloads off the main account.

    TLS and certificates: A full certificate inventory, auto-renewing ACM certificates, and alerting on expiring or mismatched certificates across every domain.

    Edge and application security: Cloudflare and AWS WAF rules, rate limiting, bot mitigation, and incident response for customer-facing applications.

    DevOps and release engineering: CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, TeamCity), deployments to production and non-production environments, and release plans for every production change.

    Workflow automation and monitoring: Our scheduled data workflows (Stonebranch/OpsWise), plus monitoring, alerting and on-call (Site24x7, Opsgenie) for business-critical jobs and services.

    Infrastructure as Code: Terraform and GitHub Actions with OIDC-based deployment, a sandbox account, and code-reviewed changes.

    Cost and compliance: Cost reporting, tag enforcement with AWS Config, and CrowdStrike coverage and access audits.

What You'll Do:

    Design, build and operate highly available AWS infrastructure across dev, test, prod and DMZ accounts.

    Plan and run production changes with a published change notice covering scope, impact, rollback and confirmation.

    Perform and oversee deployments to production and non-production environments, with a release plan, a rollback path and a Jira record for each.

    Build, maintain and troubleshoot CI/CD pipelines, and help development teams ship safely and repeatably.

    Coach junior engineers and hand off repeatable work to them with written runbooks.

    Disagree, then commit. Push back with evidence. Once a decision is made, deliver it as agreed, or agree an alternative in writing.

    Respect for colleagues. Criticize the problem, not the people or teams involved, in every channel.

    Stay calm when escalated. Answer with status and next steps.

    Make your work visible. Post a daily written standup update (Shipped / Next / Blockers) and take part in team rituals.

    Review every change. Production changes go through code review, including urgent ones.

    Own the whole job. Documentation, legacy systems and request handling are part of the role, not a distraction from it.

Fastmarkets is seeking a highly experienced and commercially driven Head of Forest Products Consultancy to lead and scale our consultancy offering from the US market. This is a senior leadership and management role responsible for building and delivering a market-leading strategic advisory business across the forest product sector, with a focus on the global pulp, paper, and packaging value chain.

The role combines hands-on strategic consulting delivery, commercial leadership, and team building, with full accountability for revenue generation, client development, and the growth of the consultancy business line within a broader Price Reporting Agency (PRA) environment.

The successful candidate will act as the principal consultancy lead for our global business, with direct responsibility and accountability in driving sales and revenue generation in Forest product consultancy, working closely with global analysts and commercial teams to develop and deliver high-impact client solutions.

Specifically, you will generate business development opportunities, lead and deliver all strategy and market-based consultancy projects that include tailored market overviews and outlooks, feasibility assessments and analysis, cost benchmarking and competitiveness analysis, supply-chain mapping, go-to-market and commercial due diligence advisory, packaging value chain strategy and circular economy insights, and other bespoke engagements.

Responsibilities

  • Act as the principal lead for all forest products consultancy engagements across pulp, paper, and packaging markets globally
  • Winning, executing, and project managing (both independently and in collaboration with our delivery teams and business partners) a range of strategic and market-based consultancy projects in the forest products space.
  • Managing consultancy deliverables (self-sufficiently and managing others) that are robust, accurate, and well-researched and project managing resources utilising modelling, data collection, and research interview techniques
  • Position the Fastmarkets consultancy practice as a credible and leading alternative to established rival firms
  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing US consultancy team
  • Establish scalable processes, frameworks, and methodologies for consultancy delivery
  • Foster a high-performance, client-focused consulting culture
  • Lead the development of market insights, reports, and client-facing thought leadership
