  • Build a strong pipeline of project-based and retainer-based advisory engagements
  • Work closely with commercial and account teams to integrate consultancy offerings into broader client relationships
  • Developing and building existing customer relationships and acquiring new consultancy customers, as well as repeat/retainer business
  • Forecasting and CRM reporting
  • Represent the business externally at industry events, client presentations, and conferences
  • Utilise professional network to surface opportunities and to source independent contractors to support the delivery of engagements.

We recruit talented, dynamic people with diverse backgrounds and experiences, all united by a belief in our mission to provide the world’s leading and most trusted price reporting, events, and intelligence service for the markets we serve. We’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to creating a fully inclusive workplace, where everyone feels able to participate and contribute meaningfully.

If you are open-minded, curious, resilient, solutions-oriented and committed to promoting equality, then read on.

KNOWLEDGE, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

We are looking for an individual who is highly motivated, driven, and have a passion to be part of a fast-paced, successful team. Being a strong team player is also important as well as someone who is happy to work flexibly.

Experience and skills required

  • A seasoned individual with consulting experience in Forest product consultancy, proven business development and research
  • Proven experience in a top-tier consulting firm (e.g. McKinsey, BCG, Bain) or specialist commodities consultancy
  • Demonstrated experience in building or scaling a consulting practice or business line in the Forest products space
  • Deep knowledge of global pulp, paper, and packaging markets and value chains
  • Strong track record of leading client-facing advisory engagements at a senior level
  • Experience in complex solution selling and project execution/management involving single-client consultancy services work
  • Fluent in English, a second language preferred
  • Flexibility and willingness to travel when required
  • An already established client and industry contact network would be desirable
  • Self-starter and ‘hunter’ mentality with strong personal drive is essential, with the ability to thrive in a multitasking environment
  • Accountable and performance-driven
  • Effective communication in person, on the phone, in writing and online
  • Effective and amiable team player keen on making clients, project members, and colleagues happy while achieving ambitious objectives.

This is a rare opportunity to build and lead a global forest products consulting practice within a leading commodities intelligence organisation. The role offers significant autonomy to shape strategy, develop a high-performing team, and drive meaningful commercial growth, while competing directly with the world’s leading consulting and specialist advisory firms.

If you're excited about the role but your experience, skills or qualifications don't perfectly align, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Our Values

Fastmarkets people come from all different walks of life. It’s this mix of brilliant personalities, experiences and insights that gives us that warm, open, and friendly culture you can feel as soon as you meet us. But however wonderfully different we all are, there are six things we all have in common – and they form our Fastmarkets values.

Created by our own employees to reflect some of the personal traits that Fastmarkets people have, our values are key to what makes our culture unique. They reflect who each of us are and they're embedded in everything we do. Our values are:

  • METRICS DRIVEN. We use insights to improve our customers’ experience and our business performance
  • ACCOUNTABLE. We are accountable to ourselves and those we work with: we keep our promises and get things done
  • GROWTH MINDSET. This value enables us to be nimble to the changing realities and operate with a sense of urgency
  • INCLUSIVE. We are inclusive and respectful, celebrating each of us and giving everyone a deep sense of belonging with the desire to bring their best self to work every day.
  • CUSTOMER CENTRIC. We are customer-centric in all that we do
  • COLLABORATIVE. We are collaborative, able to work across teams and capitalise on the diversity of intellect, perspectives, and experiences.

We are committed to ensuring all candidates feel welcomed and supported. Should your application advance and you require accommodations for the interview process, please inform us so we can make the necessary arrangements.

• Pennsylvania

• Texas*

Otherwise the position will be located as shown in the advert.

You’ve read a little about us – now it’s over to you!

If you like what you’ve read so far and think you can see yourself as a Fastmarkets person, it’s time to fill in your application form. This form is an important part of the selection process: it’s used to determine whether or not you’ll be chosen to have an interview and acts as a basis for the questions we’ll ask you on the day.

It’s vital that you try to capture all the relevant information we have asked for on the form so we can get a good feel for who you are and why you’re great.

Fastmarkets is an industry-leading price-reporting agency (PRA) and information provider for global commodities, providing price data, news, analytics and events for the agriculture, forest products, metals and mining and new-generation energy markets.

Fastmarkets' data is critical for customers seeking to understand and predict dynamic, sometimes opaque markets, enabling trading and risk management. Fastmarkets is a global business with a history dating back to 1865 and is built on trust and deep market knowledge. It has more than 700 employees spread across global locations in the UK, US, China, India, Singapore, Brazil, Belgium, Bulgaria, Finland and beyond.

Why this role exists

K0rdent AI is the orchestration layer that turns raw, disaggregated GPU infrastructure into a multi-tenant, production-ready AI cloud — without locking companies into a single hyperscaler or hardware vendor. We sell accelerated compute: GPU clusters, bare metal, and managed AI infrastructure to Neoclouds, AI-native startups, enterprise AI teams, research labs, and sovereign/regulated buyers. These are technical, high-value, long-cycle deals where the sale is won or lost on credibility: whether we can architect the right cluster, model the real TCO, prove performance, and de-risk a customer's move onto our platform.

This person owns the technical win. They build and lead the sales engineering function that turns "interested" into signed, multi-year committed-capacity contracts, and they set the pre-sales bar as we scale headcount and deal volume.

This is not a demo-jockey role. We need someone who has genuinely stood up training and inference workloads, argued interconnect topology with a customer's ML infra lead, and closed large deals with cycles measured in quarters, not weeks.

What you'll own

Lead and build the SE / Solutions Architect team

  • Hire, coach, and retain a team of sales engineers and solutions architects; define the pre-sales operating model as the org scales.

  • Build the reusable machinery: discovery frameworks, reference architectures, TCO/benchmark models, POV playbooks, demo and benchmark environments, RFP response libraries.

  • Set and hold a technical quality bar across the team; run enablement so every SE can speak credibly to GPU architecture, networking, and orchestration.

Own the technical win in large, complex deals

  • Partner with Account Executives as the technical lead on strategic and enterprise opportunities from discovery through technical close.

  • Run qualification with a real methodology (MEDDPICC or equivalent) — surface the economic buyer, decision criteria, and the technical champion, and build the win plan around them.

  • Architect solutions across compute, networking, storage, and orchestration; produce sizing, capacity plans, and TCO comparisons vs. hyperscalers and self-build.

  • Design and drive POCs/POVs: define success criteria up front, run benchmarks, and convert results into commercial momentum.

Be the Technical voice of the Customer internally

  • Feed structured product and capacity requirements back to product, platform, and supply/capacity planning.

  • Work alongside the NVIDIA field and partner ecosystem (Cloud Partner program, reference architectures, joint pursuits) to strengthen deals.

  • Influence roadmap and packaging based on what you learn in the field.

Required:

Real, hands-on AI/ML infrastructure experience

  • You have actually run or stood up ML workloads — distributed training and/or production inference — not just talked about them.

  • Practical fluency in the training and inference lifecycle: data pipelines, distributed training (multi-node/multi-GPU), fine-tuning, and serving; you understand where bottlenecks actually live (interconnect, memory bandwidth, I/O, scheduling).

  • Comfortable in the frameworks and tooling customers use — PyTorch and the surrounding ecosystem (e.g., NCCL, CUDA-level concepts, containers, schedulers).

Deep knowledge of the NVIDIA platform and GPU products

  • Current on the NVIDIA compute stack across the Hopper and Blackwell generations (e.g., H100/H200, GB200 NVL72 / B200-class systems, Grace-Hopper superchips) and the reference-system families (DGX, HGX, MGX); aware of what's coming next-generation.

  • Networking fluency: NVLink/NVSwitch domains, InfiniBand (Quantum) vs. Spectrum-X Ethernet fabrics, RDMA/RoCE, DPUs — and why fabric choice makes or breaks large training clusters.

  • Software and platform layer: NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NIM, NeMo, Triton / TensorRT-LLM, Base Command, Run:ai / GPU orchestration, and the NGC ecosystem.

  • Understands the NVIDIA Cloud Partner motion and how to co-sell with NVIDIA.

Enterprise sales engineering on long, high-value cycles

  • Track record supporting complex B2B deals with cycles of 6–18+ months and large ACV/TCV, ideally including multi-year committed-capacity or reserved-capacity structures.

  • Skilled at multi-stakeholder navigation — ML/infra leads, platform engineering, procurement, finance, security, and executive sponsors.

  • Can build and defend a TCO/ROI model against hyperscaler and on-prem alternatives, and translate performance benchmarks into commercial value.

  • SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central (EC) implementation and support.

The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on expertise in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central configuration, reporting, and implementation, along with experience leading client engagements and cross-functional teams.   • Opportunities for professional growth and development
  • A collaborative and inclusive work environment

Overview

The Staff, Lease Administration Analyst role requires a thorough understanding of lease documents as well as integrating lease documents on behalf of The RMR Group Inc. and its subsidiaries, three publicly traded affiliated entities and a privately held fund, into a centralized database which is the foundation of reporting analysis utilized by the broader organization. This role requires the candidate to accurately discern and abstract lease documents, as well as ensuring the financial terms of the deal are accurately represented in Yardi, the system of record, to ensure accurate reporting for the broader organization. This role requires close coordination with various business functions of Accounting, Asset Management, Asset Services and Legal departments.

Responsibilities

  • Integrate Executed Deals received and incorporate vital data within the Yardi application.
  • Abstract critical lease terms, including recovery clauses, for new Leases, Lease Amendments, Lease Terminations, Assignments and other lease documents within Yardi.
    • Review and approve of lease abstractions processed by third-party for Executed Deals.
    • Abstractions must provide a heightened focus on properly capturing Revenue Recognition items and Encumbrance data to ensure effective reporting.
  • Review and approve of lease abstractions processed by third-party for Acquisition related deals.
  • Actively assess the impact of Revenue Recognition items which impact Straight-Line Rent Calculations. Collaborate and discuss Revenue Recognition items with Accounting Manager and Manager, Lease Administration to ensure compliance with established SOX 404 Narratives.
  • Maintain open communication with Real Estate Services regarding the building square footage modifications, unit changes, lease document status, move-in/out forms, major tenant information, and other open portfolio issues.
  • Work with Real Estate Services monthly to identify tenants in Holdover status.
  • Create and execute the approval process and posting of monthly Recurring Charges, as well as any miscellaneous billings/adjustments associated with Recurring Charges.
  • Calculate Consumer Price Index (CPI) Adjustments as they become due on a monthly basis.
  • Coordinate and process reconciliation of accounts which may have outstanding A/R issues (Government CPI for example).
  • Assist with the calculation and booking of Percentage Rent and Sub-Rent Receivable Income, when applicable.
  • Work with Records Management Administrators to resolve discrepancies relating to tenant lease files to ensure documents are properly reflected in the Digital Lease Library.
  • Assist with new acquisitions by setting up core Tenant information in Yardi.
  • Assist with capital recycling efforts as they arise by supporting the team with the Estoppel Management process.
  • Assist with the integration of new annual escrows for Operating Expenses and Taxes. Maintain Recovery Clause data and accurate Tenant base amount information within Yardi and the Excel based Templates in Progress on a daily basis throughout the year.
  • Discuss lease document status, questions and/or open issues with the Manager and follow up with Real Estate Services, Asset Management or Accounting as the need arises.
  • As part of the monthly close process, assist with reconciliation of Yardi and Executed deals in RMR Reporting.
  • Perform special projects as needed, such as assist with internal and external audit requests, and provide support for the Accounting, Legal, Real Estate Services and Asset Management departments.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Proficiency with accounting software package (Yardi) preferred. Proficiency with Excel and other Microsoft applications.
  • This position requires keen attention to detail, self-motivation, flexibility, a solution mindset and excellent organizational and interpersonal skills.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills are required.
  • Overall knowledge and interest in the commercial real estate industry is critical to success in this position. Working knowledge of leases is a plus.
  • Demonstrates ability to work with evolving technologies and business applications, including AI-assisted tools, to support research, data validation, workflow efficiency and process improvement.
  • 3+ years of commercial real estate lease administration experience, knowledge of standard and non-standard lease components. Ability to interpret complex retail and commercial lease language and an understanding of the accounting requirements of leases is essential.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative and results driven environment with the ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines.

Total Rewards

The RMR Group offers an extensive total rewards package to ensure that your benefits align with your needs. Employees who work at least 21 hours per week are eligible to participate in The RMR Group’s benefits plans, including:

  • Health Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Life & Disability Insurance
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) & Flexible Spending Plans (FSA)
  • 401(k) Plan with Employer Match
  • Holidays, Vacation & Sick Time
  • Parental Leave
  • Tuition Assistance
  • Matching Gift Program
  • Wide Array of Voluntary, Employee-Paid Benefits to choose from including Critical Illness & Accident Insurance, Identity Theft Protection & Pet Insurance

The estimated base compensation range for this position is $70,000 to $90,000 per year. RMR considers several components including an individual's skills, qualifications, experience, internal equity, and market data.

Company Overview

The RMR Group (Nasdaq: RMR) is a leading U.S. alternative asset management company, unique for its focus on commercial real estate (CRE) and related businesses. RMR’s vertical integration is strengthened by over 800 real estate professionals in more than 30 offices nationwide who manage over $37 billion in assets under management and leverage 40 years of institutional experience in buying, selling, financing and operating CRE. RMR benefits from a scalable platform, a deep and experienced management team, and a diversity of real estate strategies across its clients. RMR has been recognized by The Boston Globe as a “Top Place to Work”, by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) as an “ENERGY STAR Partner of the Year” and ranked by the Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) as having one of the highest number of BOMA 360 designated properties in its portfolio. RMR is headquartered in Newton, MA and was founded in 1986.

RMR’s mission is to create long term value for our clients by managing their investments and assets “like we own it” – an approach that consistently and repeatedly generates opportunities for all our employees, investors and stakeholders. We are guided by six core values:

  • Integrity at Our Core.
  • Perform Passionately and Effectively.
  • Inspired Thinking.
  • Like We Own It.
  • Power of We.
  • Mutual Respect.

Visit our website to learn more about what makes The RMR Group a rewarding place to build a career.

Follow RMR on LinkedIn and Instagram @thermrgroup.

jobs.excerpt: SUMMARYAs an Escrow Closer, you will assist with the escrow closing process, including compliance with lender instructions, title insurance requirements, and other written instructions.
jobs.description:
SUMMARY

As an Escrow Closer, you will assist with the escrow closing process, including compliance with lender instructions, title insurance requirements, and other written instructions. You will be the single point of contact for all parties from the time we receive the transaction through closing. You will prepare all closing documents necessary to ensure title insurance is issued at closing. High levels of accuracy, attention to detail, and the ability to prioritize, multi-task, and focus on deadlines will determine your success in this role.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Responsible for effectively managing the real estate closing transaction. This position requires the Escrow Closer to exercise independent judgment and to possess the knowledge and experience necessary to efficiently handle situations which may arise during the closing process.
  • Understand the escrow process to determine what steps need to be taken to properly cure e title of properties pursuant to the conditions called for in the real estate contract and/or lender instructions.
  • Prepare all closing documents necessary to ensure title insurance is issued at closing.
  • Secure all documents (corrective and others) that may be required for the issuance of title insurance.
  • Single point of contact for borrowers, loan officers, processors and others.
  • Assist customers and clients with closing related questions.
  • Prior to disbursement, confirm all funds are collected, all appropriate documents are checked for accuracy, signatures are collected, and acknowledgements and legal descriptions are correct.
  • Collect all taxes due, HOA dues, and any delinquencies and/or principal and interest.
  • Verify against the closing disclosure or settlement that all disbursements have been paid correctly.
  • Prior to recording, verify all legal documents for correct acknowledgements, legal, and lien information.
  • Manage and develop client relationships to ensure future real estate closing transactions.

SUCCESS CRITERIA

  • Customer-first: you care deeply about our customers (Borrowers, Lenders and internal customers) and you understand that we exist, first and foremost, to serve a customer's needs.
  • Solutions-orientation: you thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment, and are able to shift gears comfortably. You can decide and act without having the total picture.
  • Both a thinker and a “doer”: you’re a strategic thinker who can go deep on a business and understand its core drivers, and how various processes throughout the business interplay with each other. You’re biased towards action, and have a knack for making things work, even with limited resources.
  • A creative problem solver: you have a proven track record of thinking “outside the box” to solve complicated problems. You have a global perspective, sound business judgment, and are truth-seeking in your solutioning and decisioning. You are also willing to roll up your sleeves and do whatever it takes to solve the problem.
  • Highly collaborative: you’re a strong communicator with the ability to motivate, inspire, and influence cross-functional teams. You’re a natural planner and organizer, and can effectively manage bandwidth and resources inside and outside your organization to bring about the successful completion of key objectives and initiatives.
  • Eager to drive impact: you believe results matter. You’re motivated to drive improvements in the business as reflected in operating metrics, our P&L, and reduced pain points for internal and external customers.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Must be located in MD or WA
  • Experience in the title and escrow industry
  • Excellent customer service skills are required, including the ability to interact professionally and knowledgeably with Borrowers, Loan officers, Processors, and Underwriters
  • Familiarity with Refinance transactions and requirements
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Knowledge of the escrow process and mortgage lending regulations
  • Strong problem-solving, analytical, and organizational skills. Deadline-driven.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in cross-functional teams

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience in escrow closing

  • Experience with Qualia/Resware is strongly preferred. Experience with Softpro or similar software will also be considered.
  • Multi-state residential closing experience strongly preferred

jobs.description:
Who we are:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit to learn more.

About the Role:

Motive's GTM Intelligence & Operations team owns the systems, data, and governance behind how 2,000 sellers, managers, and marketers engage our customers worldwide. As Manager, GTM Intelligence & Operations, reporting to the Senior Director of GTM Intelligence & Operations, you'll lead a team of systems administrators and program owners responsible for our end to end GTM SaaS stack: Salesforce at the core, plus sales engagement, prospecting, enrichment, gifting, references, conversation intelligence, and the integrations that connect them. You'll own the stack's roadmap, architecture, budget, and licensing, and partner with Sales Operations, Sales leadership, Enterprise Systems, Marketing, Legal, Finance, Procurement, and other teams to deliver our biggest GTM initiatives.

You're a battle tested enterprise systems leader with a business owner's mindset. You've run GTM platforms at scale, built and led admin teams, and seen enough implementations, migrations, and outages to know what good looks like. You know why every field, integration, and setting you own exists, and you use that to make better decisions, not just faster ones. You stay calm when a platform goes down and the field still needs to sell by lunch. You lead with data and translate technical and regulatory requirements into plain language that sellers and executives can act on. Above all, you grow your people into independent experts and keep the focus on the business.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead, coach, and grow a team of GTM systems administrators and program owners by setting clear priorities, delegating platform ownership, and developing each person into a trusted subject matter expert.
  • Own the end to end GTM platform ecosystem as a connected system, with Salesforce at its center, including architecture, data model, profiles and permissions, automation, integrations, and the downstream tools that depend on it. Serve as the final escalation point for complex platform issues.
  • Set the standard for Salesforce administration across the GTM org, including release management, change control, documentation, and the quoting and CPQ processes that connect pipeline to revenue, in partnership with Enterprise Systems.
  • Own the strategy, budget, renewals, and license governance for the broader GTM SaaS portfolio, including our sales engagement platform, and partner with Finance and Procurement on ROI, seat forecasting, and investment decisions.
  • Lead vendor evaluations and major tool migrations from requirements and diligence through build, launch, change management, and retirement of the legacy tool, so that multi-million dollar decisions are grounded in data and the voice of the user.
  • Partner with Legal, Security, and Marketing to design and enforce GTM compliance and governance across markets, covering consent management, Do Not Contact, call recording, texting, and email deliverability. Provide data and audit support to Legal and leadership when needed.
  • Act as the systems lead for major cross-functional initiatives such as new market launches, rebrands, and new sales motions, and partner with Enablement to deliver onboarding, training, and documentation that drive lasting adoption.
  • Keep the revenue engine running when things break by leading incident response with vendors and ESYS, engineering workarounds, protecting data integrity, and keeping field and executive leaders informed.

What We're Looking For:

  • 10+ years of experience in GTM operations, sales or revenue operations, or GTM systems within an enterprise or high-growth B2B SaaS organization, including 5+ years of direct people management experience leading systems administrators or GTM operations teams.
  • Deep, hands-on Salesforce administration experience at an enterprise scale of 1,000+ users, including objects, security and sharing, profiles and permission sets, automation, reporting, and integrations. Salesforce Administrator, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder, CPQ Specialist, or other Salesforce certifications are a plus.
  • CPQ experience is strongly preferred, ideally Salesforce CPQ or Revenue Cloud, including product and pricing configuration, discount approvals, and quote to cash handoffs.
  • A proven track record of managing an entire end to end GTM platform within an enterprise org, spanning CRM, sales engagement (Outreach, Salesloft, or a comparable platform), data and enrichment (such as ZoomInfo and LinkedIn Sales Navigator), conversation intelligence, gifting, and customer reference platforms. Experience with AI features in GTM tools is a plus.

  • Working knowledge of outbound compliance and deliverability requirements (GDPR, TCPA, CAN-SPAM, CCPA, and Do Not Contact) and experience partnering with Legal to put them into practice in your systems.
  • Experience owning a software budget and license governance, and presenting clear, data-backed recommendations to executive leadership.
  • Remote position (must already be located in North America).

jobs.description:
The Corporate Development Manager will own the financial evaluation and execution of two types of transactions: acquisitions of existing medspa practices generating $2–20M in annual revenue, and "acqui-hire" transactions that bring independent providers into our new and existing clinics. You will be the primary analytical engine behind every deal, from first look through close, determining whether an opportunity is attractive, building a defensible view of adjusted EBITDA or provider-level economics, and supporting leadership in valuation and negotiation discussions with practice owners and providers. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys both the rigor of financial analysis and the pace of live deals.

Key Responsibilities

Deal screening and evaluation
• Review inbound and outbound opportunities, quickly assessing fit against our acquisition criteria (market, service mix, provider base, growth potential, and financial profile)
• Prepare concise investment memos and recommendations for leadership on whether to pursue, pass, or restructure a deal
• Build and maintain a pipeline tracker and deal database
Financial analysis and quality of earnings
• Analyze practice financials, including P&Ls, tax returns, bank statements, and point-of-sale/EMR data, often from owners with limited financial reporting
• Build adjusted EBITDA bridges, normalizing for owner compensation, medical director arrangements, provider compensation, one-time and personal expenses, related-party rent, and non-recurring revenue
• Analyze key operating metrics such as revenue by service line, provider productivity, patient retention and rebooking rates, membership revenue, product and injectable margins, and customer concentration
• Coordinate with third-party quality-of-earnings providers, accountants, and attorneys as needed

Valuation and deal structuring
• Develop valuation models using EBITDA multiples, comparable transactions, and DCF where appropriate
• Model deal structures including cash at close, seller notes, earnouts, rollover equity, and provider retention incentives
• Prepare materials to support leadership in valuation discussions and negotiations with sellers

Provider Acqui-hires (independent providers)
• Identify and evaluate independent injectors, aestheticians, and other providers operating in salon suites or similar settings as candidates to join our clinics
• Assess each provider's book of business, including revenue, service mix, client count, rebooking and retention rates, pricing, and how much of the client base is likely to follow them
• Build provider-level economic models comparing their current earnings to our compensation structure, and project the incremental revenue and contribution to the receiving clinic
• Structure offers such as sign-on or book-of-business payments, earnouts tied to client retention, guaranteed compensation periods, and retention incentives
• Verify licensing, scope of practice, and supervision requirements, and assess fit with the receiving clinic's capacity, service menu, and team
• Partner with clinic leadership on onboarding and client transition plans, and track retention and productivity against the original business case

Diligence and closing
• Manage the financial diligence process, including data requests, document review, and issue tracking
• Help identify operational, regulatory, and integration risks (e.g., provider licensing and scope of practice, medical director and ownership structure requirements, key-person dependence)
• Support LOI drafting and the path to close alongside legal counsel

Post-close support
• Track acquired practice and acqui-hired provider performance against the investment case
• Help refine acquisition criteria and underwriting assumptions based on results

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

Required
• 3–5 years of experience in private equity, investment banking, transaction advisory/quality of earnings, corporate development, or a comparable finance role
• Hands-on experience building adjusted EBITDA analyses and valuation models for small and lower-middle-market businesses (roughly $2–10M in revenue)
• Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills
• Ability to evaluate individual provider economics and client portability, not just practice-level financials
• Ability to work with incomplete or messy financial data and turn it into clear, defensible conclusions
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations to senior leadership
• High degree of ownership, judgment, and ability to manage multiple deals at once

Preferred
• Private equity experience, particularly with add-on acquisitions or buy-and-build strategies
• Experience in healthcare services, multi-site consumer services, or franchise businesses; medical aesthetics experience is a strong plus
• Familiarity with the salon-suite model or experience recruiting and valuing producer-based talent (e.g., providers, advisors, stylists)
• Undergraduate degree in Business, Accounting, or Finance preferred
• MBA a plus
• Familiarity with healthcare transaction considerations such as MSO structures and corporate practice of medicine rules

Physical Requirements
• Ability to perform computer-based work for extended periods.
• Ability to communicate effectively via phone, video conference, and written communications.
• Ability to use standard office equipment.
• Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Benefits

Team members enjoy generous employee and Friends & Family discounts, and the opportunity to work alongside a talented and supportive team. Benefits also include paid holidays and a 401(k) plan with company match.

jobs.title: Junior Developer Advocate
jobs.excerpt: In shortWe are building a HuggingFace / npm for ontologies.
jobs.description:
In short

We are building a HuggingFace / npm for ontologies. Ontologies are what gives data meaning – the new wave of AI applications needs them badly. We capture this wave.

We are looking for a student or junior community enthusiast to join our team as a Junior Developer Advocate. You don’t need years of experience or an impressive resume. We care about your curiosity, drive, and willingness to learn. Your focus will be supporting our developer advocacy efforts: helping us engage the community, create content, and get our open-source software into the hands of AI & data developers.

Fully remote within the EU/EFTA, some travel, small team, lots of ownership.

What you’ll do

You will work alongside a Community & Ecosystem Lead and core team to help build and nurture our developer community. You’ll get hands-on mentorship while having real ownership over your tasks. Depending on your strengths and interests, you’ll help us:

  • Organize tutorials / workshops at developer, technical, or scientific conferences

  • Talk to OSS communities – understand their needs, get partnerships

  • Make upstream contributions to OSS projects

  • Write tutorials and editorial content

  • Engage the community via social media and other channels (e.g., Discord)

  • Maintain our relations with key partners (e.g., content publishers, software companies)

  • Tell the dev team what the community really needs – what features unlock new use cases, for example

Who are we looking for

Rigid requirements (MUST have):

  • Fluent in English.

  • Living in the EU or EFTA.

  • Able to travel.

What we will look for (you don’t need to tick all boxes):

  • Good public speaker, experience in giving talks at technical or scientific conferences

  • Can code, at least to a degree to be able to teach people basic programming

  • Familiar with the open-source ecosystem (track record of OSS contributions preferred)

  • Good writing skills, preferably demonstrated with blog posts, research papers, or other content

  • Experience with operating social media profiles (especially engaging communities, not just blasting corporate propaganda)

  • Experience in organizing physical events

  • Very familiar with the data & AI spaces (e.g., agents, analytics, databases, graph analytics, ontologies)

  • Experience building or growing a technical community

NOT needed:

  • Formal education or an impressive resume. We are looking for people at all experience levels.

  • Speaking Polish – we speak English only!

  • Experience with ontologies – we can quickly teach you that, but if you know them, it’s a plus.

What can we give you

  • Work on high-visibility open-source projects with direct ownership over your tasks and mentorship from senior engineers.

  • Travel: scientific and technical conferences.

  • Equity on top of the base salary.

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Fully remote work.

  • Negotiable type of contract.

  • Competitive salary – strongly dependent on your experience level and motivation.

  • Regular team integrations (physical and virtual)

How we work

We are a small team, where we strongly prefer to give each team member ownership of a particular topic. There is no bureaucratic process. If you want to talk to the CEO/CTO, just hit them up on chat.

We are remote-first. You can work any hours that are the most convenient to you.

Our team members come from open source communities, academia, and tech. It’s a place where you’ll have access to some very smart folks that are a pleasure to work with.

How to apply

Your resume is not our main focus – your work is. Please include links to your relevant work: OSS projects, organized community events, talks you gave, social media pages managed by you, scientific papers, or anything else that is relevant to interacting with communities.

You can put these links either in the resume, or in the dedicated application form field.

About NeverBlink

AtNeverBlink we are on a mission to make knowledge graphs and ontologies accessible to the masses, making AI systems more useful and more aligned with human intent. We build infrastructure software – the new generation of data products to be used by top companies worldwide. jobs.title: Senior People Ops Manager - Payroll & Systems
jobs.excerpt: About Convergent ResearchConvergent Research is a nonprofit science studio best known for pioneering the Focused Research Organization (FRO).
jobs.description:
About Convergent Research

Convergent Research is a nonprofit science studio best known for pioneering the Focused Research Organization (FRO). We architect critical infrastructure that removes bottlenecks to breakthrough scientific research.

FROs are mission-driven, time-bound organizations built to solve important scientific and engineering bottlenecks. Convergent secures funding and provides the operational backbone that allows scientists and engineers to move quickly, from legal formation and governance to hiring, finance, communications, and operational systems. We’ve taken 14 FROs from idea to operating entity, including four launches in 2026.

About the Role

Payroll probably isn’t the first thing that comes to mind when you think about breakthrough science. But scientists can’t do their best work if they aren’t paid correctly, benefits aren’t working, or their organization isn’t set up to employ them.

That’s where you come in.

We’re looking for a Senior People Ops Manager - Payroll & Systems to own the people ops infrastructure that keeps Convergent and our FROs running smoothly. You’ll make sure our employees get paid accurately and on time, our policies and systems keep pace with our growth, new FROs become functioning employers, and organizations completing their missions can wind down responsibly.

This is a senior, hands-on expert role. We’re looking for someone who knows parts of this work better than we do. Someone who doesn’t just identify problems but brings recommendations, builds solutions, and sets the standard for how we operate. You’ll have significant autonomy to make decisions within your domain, with the Head of People providing final approval on decisions that impact company-wide strategy or multiple teams.

You’ll report to our Head of People and work closely with our People Ops Manager – Employee Experience, who owns recruiting, onboarding, and internal communications, and our Sr. HRBP, who serves as the primary point of contact for FRO employees. You’ll also partner with our Launch team, which coordinates the many moving pieces involved in getting a new FRO off the ground or winding one down. As we grow, there may be an opportunity to add a coordinator to support routine administrative work.

A quick note on payroll: We use TriNet as our US PEO and Rippling for UK payroll. Our providers handle tax calculations and filings, but that doesn’t mean we’ve outsourced accountability. You’ll own the accuracy of the inputs, review the outputs, and make sure issues get resolved. A second member of People Ops will provide an independent pre-run review.

This role will initially be approximately 60% hands-on execution and 40% policy development, infrastructure building, and continuous improvement. We need someone who enjoys both.

You Will (Duties)

  • Own payroll and make it bulletproof. You'll manage US and UK payroll end to end, including timesheets, payroll changes, initial review, and accuracy. We use TriNet (US) and Rippling (UK), so providers handle tax calculations and filings, but accountability stays with you. You'll build and maintain controls for input validation, independent pre-run review by another People Ops team member, pre- and post-run reconciliation, change approvals, and audit trails. You'll document processes so someone else can run payroll safely and push providers to fix gaps when needed.
  • Keep benefits, retirement, and leave running smoothly. You'll own benefits administration, COBRA, open enrollment, US 401(k) and UK pension administration, including contributions, records, and provider coordination. You'll also manage leave administration in our HRIS and workers' compensation, partnering with the Sr. HRBP when accommodations or employee-specific issues arise.
  • Make our people systems work for us. You'll own our HRIS architecture, configuration, integrations, data integrity, governance, and reporting, including source-of-truth rules, field ownership, and auditing. You'll troubleshoot escalated issues, manage vendor relationships and platform performance, and recommend when to build, buy, change, or simplify systems, with costs and risks clearly laid out.
  • Keep our policies and compliance ahead of our growth. You'll partner with the Head of People to write and maintain compliant policies across US federal and state jurisdictions, the UK, and EOR-covered countries, with a jurisdictional compliance matrix, version control, and review dates. You'll also own the people compliance calendar, covering filings, renewals, notices, audits, and policy reviews, with clear owners and lead times. You'll know when to involve outside counsel, while the Head of People retains final statutory policy approval and decisions with company-wide strategic implications.
  • Coordinate immigration and compensation processes. You'll facilitate FRO introductions to immigration counsel, coordinate vendors, track timelines, and provide HRIS documentation (not manage substantive immigration cases). You'll support reporting for compensation reviews, while the Head of People owns compensation strategy.
  • Help new FROs become functioning employers. You'll stand up the people infrastructure for each new FRO, including entity and EOR setup, payroll and benefits activation, policies, and a usable Notion workspace. You'll coordinate the people workstream within the broader plan owned by the Program Launch Manager, managing dependencies such as TriNet and Rippling onboarding timelines and flagging risks early.
  • Help FROs wind down responsibly. Because FROs are designed to be time-bound, finishing well matters. You'll own the operational side of wind-downs, including individual terminations, jurisdiction-specific final pay, benefits termination, platform and entity closure mechanics, and records retention. You'll partner with the Sr. HRBP on transition planning and employee communications, and with the Head of People on severance and counsel-involved matters.

In Six Months, You Will Have (6-Month Goals)

  • Taken full ownership of US and UK payroll, and pension/401k administration, with documentation detailed enough for someone else to run these processes safely.
  • Audited and updated our source-of-truth salary data.
  • Created a process for managing timecards and hourly payroll in Rippling, even though we don’t currently have hourly employees in the UK.
  • Built a 12-month roadmap with OKRs and success criteria, agreed upon with the Head of People, covering SOPs, controls, and infrastructure improvements, and completed 2-3 of the highest-priority initiatives.
  • Designed and implemented a payroll controls framework and people compliance calendar, with clear ownership, review processes, and accountability.
  • Completed a gap assessment of our policies by jurisdiction and closed the highest-risk gaps.
  • Supported at least one new FRO launch and one FRO wind-down from start to finish on the people operations side, assuming project timelines permit.

You Are (Skills)

  • A seasoned people ops expert who enjoys doing the work. You’ve owned payroll and people systems before. You’re comfortable being the person everyone turns to for answers, and you’re equally comfortable getting into the weeds. When we have something wrong, you’ll tell us and bring a better solution.
  • Detail-oriented. You sweat the details where it matters (ie payroll and compliance), but you also know when to not let perfect get in the way of done.
  • A builder of repeatable processes. You see a one-off problem and start thinking about how to prevent it from happening again. You create playbooks, templates, controls, and documentation that make our systems easier to run and safer to scale. You also protect the time needed to improve those systems, even when things get busy.
  • An owner of new and hard things. You’ve helped stand up operations for a new entity, location, or country. You’re comfortable starting with a blank page, identifying dependencies, and turning a complicated problem into an actionable plan without waiting for someone else to make the checklist.
  • A confident recommender and decision-maker. You bring options, explain the risks, and have a point of view. You know which decisions are yours to make and which need to go to the Head of People. We value expertise and thoughtful pushback, not just agreement.
  • Fluent in systems and providers. You’re comfortable working with HRIS platforms, payroll providers, PEOs, and external partners. You know what our vendors are responsible for, what remains our responsibility, and how to hold them accountable when things aren’t working.
  • A great juggler. Some months involve routine payroll and benefits admin. Others involve a new FRO launch, open enrollment, or a wind-down. Sometimes things happen all at once. You’re able to prioritize, anticipate collisions, and keep things moving without dropping the important details.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity. You’ve worked somewhere the process didn’t exist yet, or where version one left plenty of room for improvement. You bring structure to messy situations without assuming there’s always a standard answer.
  • Curious and questioning. You want to understand why something works the way it does, not just learn how to repeat it. You’re constantly looking for better tools, smarter processes, and ways to make the organization more effective.
  • A kind, low-ego teammate. You assume positive intent, communicate clearly, and treat people with respect. We don’t tolerate jerks, even exceptionally competent ones.

Qualifications

  • 12+ years of experience in HR ops, payroll administration, or a closely related field (or 8+ years with a directly relevant master’s degree).
  • 5+ years of direct, accountable ownership of payroll administration across multiple jurisdictions, including California.
  • Experience standing up or substantially building people operations processes for a new entity, location, or country.
  • Hands-on experience administering benefits, including coordinating at least one open enrollment cycle.
  • Experience owning an HRIS, including configuration, integrations, data integrity, data governance, and reporting.
  • Experience developing complete, compliant policy suites across multiple states or countries, including knowing when to engage legal counsel.
  • Strong documentation and process-building skills, with examples of playbooks, controls, or operational systems you’ve created.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled tools for documentation, reporting, and workflow automation.

Nice to Have

  • UK payroll experience, including PAYE, RTI, and pension administration.
  • Experience working in a PEO environment, ideally with TriNet, and with Rippling or a comparable international payroll platform.
  • Experience with international employer of record (EOR) arrangements.
  • Experience in a nonprofit, startup, research organization, or other fast-moving, mission-driven environment.
  • Experience supporting multiple legal entities.

We Offer (Amazing Benefits):

  • A rare chance to build institutional architecture for frontier science and work with some of the smartest and most talented experts from different fields
  • Competitive Salary: The salary range for this role is $165,000 - 175,000. Convergent uses a consistent compensation philosophy across all roles, and we offer a 5-10% premium for those working from especially high cost of labor locations (e.g. NYC, San Francisco) or from our NYC office. This structure helps us keep pay transparent, consistent, and equitable.
  • Up to a 6% 401k match because future-you deserves comfort
  • Top-tier medical, dental, and vision insurance—majority of options are fully covered for you and your dependents. Stay healthy, my friend
  • Company-paid life insurance, AD&D, long- and short-term disability insurance, as well as voluntary supplemental insurance options
  • 19 holidays (including a full week off at the end of the year—yes, we enforce it)
  • 3 weeks PTO with tenure increases, with separate allotments for sick and parental leave
  • Generous fertility benefits and childcare reimbursement—because tiny humans are a big deal
  • Education and professional development benefits
  • Wellness allowance for fitness and wellness activities (treat yourself to climbing shoes or —no judgment)
  • Quarterly offsite team retreats and additional opportunities to meet your teammates in person
At Convergent Research, we are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. We believe in hiring individuals based on their unique talents, not on race, color, religion, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law or our company policies. We are more than a proud Equal Employment Opportunity employer. Our goal is to foster a healthy, safe, and respectful environment where all employees are valued and treated with dignity. Harassment of any kind is not tolerated here.

  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.

About Turno

Since 2016, Turno has been on a mission to transform the way the world manages short-term rentals, and we're just getting started!

We're the leading operations platform for short-term rental hosts and property managers. But we're more than software: we power the largest Marketplace of "boots on the ground" services that make the Short Term Rental industry possible. Our SaaS platform and mobile apps automate the high-stakes world of turnover logistics, including scheduling, payments, quality control, and communication, connecting hosts with a network of 65,000+ vetted service professionals across the globe. We're scaling fast, evolving from a single-solution startup into a multi-product platform serving customers worldwide, with 150+ teammates across eight countries building something global, meaningful, and lasting.

Our Mission

We empower hosts to manage rentals effortlessly, anywhere in the world, with reliable, intuitive, proactive, and automated support. We create seamless connections that help hosts maximize ease and service providers grow their businesses, moving with speed, discipline, and innovation driven by customer obsession and a team that genuinely collaborates across every function. If you want to build products that real people depend on every day and do it alongside a team that values creativity, ownership, and impact, Turno is your place.


Turno Source CODE

C - Customer Obsessed

O - Outcome Focused

D - Data Driven

E - Entrusted Ownership

Role Overview

As Senior Product Manager for our Core Experience, you'll own the essential workflows hosts and service providers use every day to run short-term rental operations. This includes how work gets planned, scheduled, communicated, completed, verified, and resolved across features such as task management, checklists, problem reporting, notifications, and operational workflows.

You'll spend time understanding how hosts and service providers actually work, identifying friction in their day-to-day routines, and turning those problems into intuitive product experiences.

This is a customer-facing product role. You should be comfortable working with technical systems and integrations, but your primary focus will be owning and improving the product experiences our customers depend on to get work done.

You'll work daily with Engineering, Design, Operations, Support, and other Product teams, and you'll be accountable for customer and business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Own the core operational experience

  • Own critical host and service provider workflows end to end. Set the strategy, roadmap, and execution for the experiences hosts and contractors use to manage work across their properties and projects.

  • Make daily operations simpler. Simplify multi-step and exception-heavy workflows without losing the flexibility customers need to operate their businesses.

  • Balance supply and demand. Make trade-offs that keep the marketplace healthy for everyone. A win for hosts that hurts cleaner retention (or the reverse) is not a win.

  • Design for the edge case as if it were the happy path. Substitutions, late arrivals, no-shows, damage reports, and engagement notifications get the same rigor as the primary flow, with workflows Operations can actually run.

  • Create consistency across the product. Help ensure Turno feels like one coherent system as we add new products, services, and markets.

Product strategy, discovery & execution

  • Lead continuous discovery. Translate customer behavior, qualitative research, support insights, and product data into clear problem statements, hypotheses, and opportunities.

  • Prioritize based on customer and business impact. Balance usability improvements, product growth, operational efficiency, reliability, and longer-term platform needs.

  • Define meaningful product outcomes. Establish metrics for adoption, engagement, task completion, reliability, satisfaction, and operational efficiency.

  • Ship with Engineering and Design. Partner daily to define solutions, prioritize ruthlessly, and release high-quality work on a steady cadence.

  • Drive alignment. Communicate clearly, make decisions in a structured way, and bring stakeholders and leadership along.

Systems & technical fluency

  • Think in connected systems. Understand how shared concepts such as properties, projects, users, schedules, tasks, payments, and communications interact across Turno.

  • Partner effectively with Engineering. Be comfortable discussing technical tradeoffs, integrations, data models, and platform constraints without needing to be the technical architect.

  • Be your own best data analyst. Build Looker dashboards that track the health of your product area, and define the KPIs and instrumentation behind them.

  • Use AI pragmatically. Apply AI where it meaningfully reduces customer effort, automates repetitive work, improves quality, or helps users resolve operational problems.

Qualifications

Must-have qualifications

  • Experience: 6+ years of product management in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, operations software, or products with complex customer journeys and multi-sided interactions (supply and demand, buyers and sellers).

  • Product sense and curiosity: Strong instincts grounded in real user understanding. You keep asking "why" until the root problem is clear.

  • Systems thinking: Ability to understand how multiple product areas and workflows interact while keeping the customer experience coherent.

  • Data fluency: Experience defining KPIs, building instrumentation, and using BI tools to make decisions.

  • AI experience: You leverage AI throughout your entire product tasks and planning.

  • Communication: Ability to explain complex customer, technical, and operational problems clearly and make thoughtful trade-offs visible.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience owning products involving tasks, projects, scheduling, operational workflows, collaboration, or multi-step processes.

  • Experience with mobile-first products where users complete work while on the go.

  • Hands-on experience implementing customer engagement solutions such as Braze or Iterable, including lifecycle messaging, push, in-app, and email journeys tied to product events.

  • A track record of leading a migration from a legacy tech stack to a modern one, paired with a UX redesign, across both web and mobile apps. You know how to sequence the move, protect existing users, and measure the impact.

We need someone who understands the entire paid acquisition ecosystem, from advanced bidding strategies and attribution to creative performance, customer acquisition economics, and full-funnel growth.

  • Evaluate attribution, tracking, and conversion data to distinguish profitable growth from platform-reported results.
  • Collaborate with the Creative Strategist to analyze creative performance, identify winning concepts, and guide testing priorities.

jobs.excerpt: Apple Client Platform Engineer (Remote, US)About AlectronaCustomer experience is more than meeting an SLA.
jobs.description:
Apple Client Platform Engineer (Remote, US)

About Alectrona

Customer experience is more than meeting an SLA.

Our team is passionate about making Apple “just work” for our clients, because we want you to experience the delight of a truly functional technology environment, without the friction of IT getting in the way. We get excited about what we do, and we love sharing that passion with our partners.

Enterprise IT becomes enjoyable again.

We actually love what we do, we take a lot of pride in the quality of our work, and for us, customer experience is paramount. The SLA is not the only metric that drives us. We get deeply invested in finding ways to keep our clients as excited as we are. In an industry that hasn’t changed much in over a decade, we are actively reimagining what clients should expect from technology vendors. So we want to show off what’s possible -- not just what’s been promised.

We treat all people as if they’re smart and know what's best.

...because our clients are smart, and they do know. We work with clients that inspire us, and whose missions we want to support. That mutual respect results in trusting relationships and productive communication about business pain points and solutions. We won’t hide behind intimidating security-speak and IT jargon. We say what we mean, and mean for clients to understand what we say.

Our clients put their people first - and so do we.

Happy employees create happy customers. Downtime is expensive, and top talent shouldn’t spend entire days downloading apps and setting up workstations. Our clients understand this, and demand the best for their people as a matter of business strategy. We bring a matching sense of purpose and excitement to every client engagement.

What you’ll do at Alectrona

You will lead professional services engagements for organizations running Apple at scale. That means designing the management platform, building the parts that do not exist yet, and telling the customer the truth about what will and will not work.

  • We're a fully remote team across multiple time zones, and we expect you to work well in that environment and be willing to meet in person a few times per year, present at conferences, and be an active member of the team.
  • Design, deploy, and hand over Apple management platforms: MDM, identity, patching, security tooling, and the integrations that tie them together.
  • Own services engagements end to end in accordance with our company values. You scope the work, plan it, run it, document it, and close it out. We expect you to be able to effectively manage your own time and projects. Our team enjoys this flexibility and autonomy and the responsibility that comes with it.
  • Solve the problems that get escalated after everyone else has tried. Packet captures, log spelunking, protocol-level MDM debugging, troubleshooting undocumented behavior in macOS.
  • Understand software development concepts: automations, integrations against vendor APIs, custom agents, deployment tooling. We don't expect you to write apps, but it is important to understand the code you're deploying and know how to fix stuff that isn't working.
  • Challenge customers when their plan will not survive production. Arguing for a better approach is part of the job, and you have to do it well enough to keep the relationship.
  • Run scoping calls. Uncover the business driver behind the request, and then explain what the work will take in plain language.
  • Support our small and medium business managed services customers alongside the rest of the Alectrona team.
  • Provide technical support and guidance to our managed services customers, including properly recording notes, updating documentation, and resolving tickets within SLA targets.
  • Mentor other engineers and colleagues to raise the standards and help everyone learn.
  • Shape new products and services. Alectrona builds its own software, and the ideas come from the field.
  • Perform all job responsibilities in alignment with the core values, mission and purpose of the organization.
  • Adhere to the highest moral, ethical and legal standards to deliver an environment that promotes respect, innovation and creativity.
  • Support and promote a positive, inclusive workplace where the talents and strengths of our increasingly diverse workforce are welcomed, further developed, and expressed in our work.

What we’re looking for

This is a high mid-level to senior role. We are looking for an engineer who is an expert in Apple management and knows the rest of IT well enough to work across the whole stack a customer runs. You will be supporting a variety of customer types, from end users to IT managers.

Apple and endpoint management

  • Deep experience managing Apple devices in a variety of types of environments. This means complex management beyond help desk support and basic engineering
  • Solid hands-on expertise in at least two enterprise Apple device management platforms, and the ability to pick up the others fast. Our work spans Jamf Pro, Microsoft Intune, Omnissa Workspace ONE, Fleet, Iru (formerly Kandji), Addigy and Mosyle.
  • Command of the Apple management stack itself, not just one vendor’s console: this includes an understanding of the MDM protocol, Declarative Device Management, Automated Device Enrollment and Apple Business, APNs, configuration profiles, TCC and PPPC, FileVault, code signing and notarization, Platform SSO, etc.
  • Experience migrating fleets between platforms, and a solid understanding of what each vendor does well and where another solution might be stronger.

Software/DevOps skills for managing endpoints

  • You are familiar with more than just using basic shell scripts. Confidence in writing your own Shell scripts and troubleshooting code at a minimum. Swift, Python, Go or other experience is a plus.
  • Use AI to accelerate and complement your code, not as a wholesale replacement. We want efficiency, productivity, and anti-slop creativity. At Alectrona, we view AI not as a replacement for human expertise, but as a multiplier for your existing skills.
  • Using git, participating in code review, leveraging CI, and testing and packaging are part of how you work, not something another team does for you.
  • You leverage APIs, webhooks, and automation workflows to complete tasks and build processes that scale.

The rest of IT

  • IP networking: familiar with TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing, 802.1X, VPN, proxies and TLS inspection.
  • Server and identity administration: supporting Platform SSO, WebAuthn, Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, Active Directory, SAML, OIDC, SCIM, Kerberos, and certificate authorities.
  • Security and compliance: CIS Benchmarks, NIST 800-53, SOC 2, ISO 27001, endpoint detection tooling, vulnerability management, and how each of these applies to securing Macs in production.

Working with customers

  • Experience and confidence delivering paid professional services or consulting to external customers.
  • You are comfortable actively leading and training customers on implementing configuration changes when we aren't provided direct access to systems.
  • Experience and confidence in supporting end users and small businesses in our managed services operation.
  • You explain complex technical work to people who do not share your background, in writing and out loud.
  • You participate in discovery, kickoff, and project scoping calls as the engineering voice; ask good questions and translate client context into technical decisions.
  • You have the confidence to stand up for what's right, whether it's about a technical best practice or just common sense. You challenge your customer to think differently and maintain trust in our recommendations.
  • You stay steady when a project goes sideways, the workload swings, or a customer is unhappy.
  • Fluent English language proficiency (required).

Education and certifications

  • Four-year degree, or the equivalent in experience and knowledge. We understand these skills don't come from higher education alone.
  • Appreciated, but not required; however, you should have the skill to obtain any or all of these certifications quickly: Apple Certified IT Professional, Jamf Certified Expert (400), Microsoft MD-102, CompTIA Network+ and Security+, CISSP. If you don't have certs, you will be expected to obtain them in the first few months of employment.

You’re the right fit for Alectrona if

You enjoy your work and enjoy helping the people around you without being asked. You seek out perspectives that are not your own. You are curious and resourceful; you dig into the parts nobody else wants, and you improve on your own work. New challenges excite you rather than worry you. You take calculated risks and share your mistakes with the team so we can all improve. You approach hard conversations with empathy. Like us, you enjoy solving the really hard problems as a team and hearing how we've significantly improved our clients' working environment. We're serious about building a great place to work where we all get to enjoy what we do together.

Pay and benefits

The approximate annual compensation range for this role is $95,000 to $165,000, including base salary and any related bonuses or commissions. In addition, Alectrona provides benefits, including 401(k) (6% non-elective company contribution), group medical, dental, vision insurance (99% paid by Alectrona), and an unlimited vacation policy.

Salary: $95,000 – $165,000 / year

jobs.title: M&E Associate - Rapid Experimentation
jobs.excerpt: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011.
jobs.description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

Priority Application Deadline: May 15, 2026

About this role

The Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Associate for Rapid Experimentation will support the execution and analysis of A/B tests across GiveDirectly’s programs, contributing to the use of data to inform program and product decisions. This role is fast-paced and iterative - the team runs frequent, lightweight experiments designed to generate actionable answers quickly, and then uses those learnings to refine and improve programs in real time. This includes:

  • Supporting the execution and analysis of rapid A/B tests across GiveDirectly projects, ensuring that experiments are implemented effectively and contribute to learning within and across projects
  • Ensuring experiments are implemented correctly, measured reliably, and analyzed to produce clear and credible results, working closely with Programs, Product, Research teams, and external academic partners to align experimental design with program delivery, data collection, and operational realities
  • Translating findings into actionable insights and well-structured learning products that serve multiple audiences - internal program and product teams, and external academic partners, ensuring results inform both immediate decisions and longer-term program direction

In practice, this role is about managing a high volume of rapid experiments and turning results into clear, credible evidence that continuously shapes how GiveDirectly’s programs are refined and improved.

Reports to: Senior Manager, Monitoring and Evaluation

Level: Associate

Travel Requirement: This role is based in Rwanda. Travel within East Africa is a regular part of the role, estimated at up to 25% of the time, to support field operations across country programs.Additional international travel may occur for trainings or team convenings, as needed (estimated up to 10%)

What you’ll do:

Execute and manage A/B tests across programs

  • Conduct power calculations to ensure experiments are both statistically rigorous and feasible to implement within program constraints
  • Set up pre-specified experimental designs, applying defined experimental groups, outcome measures, and measurement timelines
  • Review experiment setups prior to launch and flag execution and measurement risks that may affect interpretability
  • Ensure experiments are well-coordinated and executed as designed, aligning implementation with research plans and integrating smoothly into program delivery across Programs and Product teams
  • Work at a fast pace across a portfolio of 2–3 live A/B tests at any given time, designed to generate actionable answers quickly and feed rapid iteration of programs and products

Ensure accurate measurement and high-quality data for experiments

  • Collaborate with external Principal Investigators (PIs) to ensure measurement approaches and data collection are aligned with research design and implementation realities
  • Ensure experimental outcomes are captured accurately and consistently by applying established indicator and measurement approaches
  • Prepare and manage datasets that are clean, well-structured, and ready for analysis using survey, administrative, and product data
  • Identify and flag data quality risks (e.g., missingness, inconsistencies, measurement error) that could affect the validity of experimental conclusions
  • Conduct targeted literature reviews to ensure measurement approaches are grounded in evidence and aligned with best practices

Analyze experimental data and interpret results to inform decisions

  • Generate reliable and decision-ready analyses of experimental data from A/B tests
  • Assess the magnitude and direction of effects and highlight what the results do and do not suggest, noting key limitations
  • Ensure results are clearly understood and appropriately interpreted, given data quality, sample size, and implementation considerations

Translate results into actionable insights and learning across experiments

  • Translate experimental results into clear, actionable recommendations to guide program and product decisions for individual country programs, and for the direction of GiveDirectly’s programming as a whole
  • Structure results and key learnings so they can be reused to inform future experiments and program design
  • Prepare concise learning products (e.g., memos, summaries) that serve multiple audiences, including internal Programs and Product teams, and external academic partners, ensuring findings are clearly communicated for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Prepare and clean de-identified datasets for sharing with external PIs and academic partners, ensuring data is structured, well-documented, and ready for independent analysis
  • Contribute to cross-country discussions to ensure learnings from experiments are shared and applied across contexts, and maintain clear documentation so experiments are easy to track, understand, and build on over time

What you’ll bring:

  • Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem-solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from candidates who have personal or professional experience in the low-income and/or historically marginalized communities that we serve.
  • Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Economics, Statistics, Public Policy, or a related quantitative field
  • 2–4 years of experience working with data in applied settings (e.g., experimentation, evaluation, analytics, or program learning), ideally in development, tech, or operations-focused roles
  • Solid understanding of experimental design and causal inference concepts (e.g., randomization, treatment/control groups, units of randomization, statistical power, bias) and how to apply them in real-world program contexts
  • Experience using R, Python, or Stata to clean, manipulate, and analyze data, including working with multiple data sources (e.g., survey or administrative data)
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (e.g., programs/operations, product, or research) and external partners to implement projects and solve problems
  • Fluency in English required
  • Comfort working at pace - able to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously, make progress with imperfect data, and iterate quickly based on emerging findings
  • Ability to interpret results beyond statistical significance and communicate clear, actionable insights to both technical and non-technical audiences

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.
