jobs.description:
Habitat Health empowers older adults to experience more good days in their homes and communities. Through the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), we provide comprehensive medical care along with support for daily needs such as meals, transportation, and in‑home assistance. We deliver coordinated clinical and social care in our centers and directly in participants’ homes, creating a fully integrated experience that brings peace of mind and a true sense of belonging. As we expand our scalable, affordable PACE model to meet the growing and complex needs of aging populations, our mission‑driven care teams continue to help participants live well on their own terms.

Habitat Health is supported by leading healthcare organizations and investors including New Enterprise Associates, Kaiser Permanente, and Town Hall Ventures. We are entering a period of significant growth and are looking for exceptional teammates to help us scale a better model of care for older adults. To learn more, visit www.habitathealth.com.

Role Scope

Habitat Health is hiring its first Data Product Manager to report to the VP of Product. We are looking for a generalist, hands-on, highly technical individual contributor who will own the roadmap for Habitat's data products and infrastructure, setting direction and priorities across the data function. You will own data products end-to-end across the two major Habitat Health pillars that the data team supports:

  1. Platform & Integrations, including Engineering / IT / Product / Technical & AI vendors
  1. Dashboards & Reporting, across growth, clinical, financial, and administrative data sets

In this role you will serve as the key bridge between our Product and Data functions, working closely with C-Suite and VP level stakeholders to align on the right product strategy, then rolling up your sleeves and collaborating with our development team to build data products that align with business needs. To succeed as a Data PM, you will need to balance Habitat’s high level business objectives against end user needs and development constraints.

In a given week you'll move across all of the modes below: figuring out what's actually worth building (Discovery), writing specs precise enough for developers to build from without back-and-forth (Specs), running the Jira backlog and sprint process (Delivery), keeping development unblocked (Execution management), mocking up and shipping dashboards (Design, QC, UAT), and triaging the daily stream of ad hoc requests from a diverse set of data customers (Triage).

Core Responsibilities & Expectations for the Role

  • Discovery: define the business problem before the build (e.g. is automating LOPMR for CMS audits the right priority this quarter?).
  • Build and ship: own the full delivery cycle – specs, Jira/sprint process, dashboard design and sign-off, UAT, and rollout.
  • Hands-on data work: use SQL and Git to independently query, validate, and review code, not just manage a backlog.
  • Triage: distinguish quick fixes from roadmap work across a steady stream of ad hoc requests.
  • AI fluency: use AI tools (e.g. Claude) to accelerate the work and model that fluency for the team.
  • Range: move across all Platform & Integrations, Clinical & Operational Services, Regulatory and Enterprise Reporting, helping shape how data product works at Habitat.

Required Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5+ years of experience in product management, data/BI, or a closely related field, with a track record of shipping data products, dashboards, or reporting tools end-to-end (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
  • Solid understanding of healthcare data ontologies, systems, and information technology
  • Proficiency in SQL sufficient to independently query, validate, and troubleshoot data.
  • Demonstrated ability to write clear technical specs (metric definitions, cohort logic, source-to-target mapping ,etc.)
  • Experience partnering directly with business stakeholders and end users – e.g., operations, compliance, or clinical leadership – to gather requirements, design solutions, and lead user acceptance testing.
  • Familiarity with a modern data development stack (e.g., Jira, Git, Power BI, and cloud data platforms such as Databricks or Azure) sufficient to spec, review, and troubleshoot alongside engineering.
  • Comfort and enthusiasm using AI tools to enhance productivity in requirements writing, documentation, analysis, and workflow automation.
  • Aligns with our purpose and our values, and is excited about living those out in daily practice
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with comfort navigating ambiguity, adapting quickly, and contributing to continuous improvement
  • Strong learning and growth mindset, including seeking feedback, engaging in healthy debate and using data and curiosity to inform decisions.
  • Acts with integrity and ownership, considering the broader organizational impact, doing the right thing, and following through to deliver results.

Nice to have:

  • Working knowledge of Agile/Scrum practices, including backlog grooming, sprint planning, and Jira (or similar tools).
  • Experience in PACE, VBC, or another regulated, compliance-driven environment, including deep working knowledge of healthcare data ontologies (e.g., CPT, ICD-10, NDC).
  • Experience with Epic (Clarity, Caboodle, Chronicles), medical/pharmacy claims data, or FHIR/HL7-based integrations.

jobs.title: Growth Manager
jobs.excerpt: The role: UCT Vocational College launches its first student intake in July 2027, offering occupational qualifications designed to build job-relevant skills and create pathways to employment.
jobs.description:
The role:

UCT Vocational College launches its first student intake in July 2027, offering occupational qualifications designed to build job-relevant skills and create pathways to employment. We are looking for a Growth Manager to build the growth engine that attracts and converts students to it.

This is a role for a builder. There is no existing funnel to inherit, no channel benchmarks and no conversion baselines – you will create them. You will own how prospective students discover UCT Vocational College, how they move from interest to application, and how many of them are enrolled and paying when the doors open.

You will have support: dedicated data, technology and sales resources, external paid media help, and a marketing team around you. We are also honest that a new institution means a good deal is still being worked out. As an early member of the Vocational College team, you will help shape how its growth and sales function operates, within the commercial priorities, budget and brand parameters agreed with the COO and relevant functional leaders.

Key responsibilities for this role include:

Demand generation

  • Own paid and organic acquisition across search, social and SEO
  • Manage the vocational marketing budget and channel mix, and be accountable for its return on investment
  • Develop creative and messaging briefs in partnership with our marketing and creative teams, and keep a continuous testing programme running
  • Establish the cost and conversion benchmarks we do not yet have

Paid media

  • Set direction for paid media, with day-to-day execution delivered through our digital consultant and delivery partners
  • Own the cost-per-conversion and cost-per-enrolled-student numbers
  • Ensure paid-media campaigns are properly tracked and optimised towards enrolled students rather than raw lead volume

Funnel and conversion

  • Own performance across the full funnel, from first click through to enquiry, application and enrolment
  • Work with our technology team on the website and application portal, shaping the flow, forms and the application journey to improve conversions
  • Find where prospective students drop off, and drive the fixes

Lifecycle marketing and nurture

  • Build the vocational funnel in HubSpot, including lead capture, routing, scoring, pipeline stages and marketing and sales automation
  • Design and build nurture programmes across channels such as email and WhatsApp for a decision cycle measured in months
  • Use AI within the funnel for personalisation, qualification and re-engagement, within our AI and data protection policies
  • Grow and segment the marketing database, ensuring that consent is properly captured and POPIA respected

Working with sales

  • Partner daily with our vocational sales team, and help define what a good lead looks like before anyone is measured on it
  • Ensure acquisition decisions are informed by downstream sales and enrolment outcomes, rather than lead volume alone
  • Establish and act on the lead quality feedback loop

Measurement and reporting

  • Define the tracking, attribution and reporting required to manage performance across the acquisition, sales and enrolment funnel, working with Data and Technology on implementation.
  • Own the commercial assumptions and funnel inputs underpinning the enrolment forecast, working with the Data team to build and monitor it, and drive delivery against the agreed target.
  • Report performance and share what you are learning

Requirements (What you will be expected to know and do):

  • 5+ years in growth, performance or lifecycle marketing, including ownership of a paid budget and accountability for a revenue or enrolment target rather than a lead-volume target
  • Hands-on marketing automation capability, having personally built workflows and nurture programmes in a mature CRM. HubSpot experience is strongly preferred
  • Strong working knowledge of paid media platforms, enough to set direction, audit an account and hold a delivery partner to account
  • Full-funnel experience and the ability to account for what happened after the lead was created
  • Experience owning or closely leading a sales or conversion function, including pipeline management, follow-up processes and accountability for revenue or enrolment outcomes.
  • Practical AI fluency, with examples of how you have applied AI in your own work
  • Comfortable working with engineering and delivery teams, briefing work and holding a quality bar on builds you do not own
  • Sound analytical practice: self-sufficient in CRM reporting, and numerate enough to spot when a number is wrong
  • Structured approach to experimentation and the willingness to stop what is not working
  • Strong written communication and copywriting skills
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to getting things live
  • Knowledge of POPIA and its implications for marketing data and direct communication
  • A degree in Marketing, Business or a related field is preferable. Relevant demonstrable experience will be considered on merit in place of a formal qualification

Advantageous:

  • Experience in education, EdTech or another considered-purchase category with a long decision cycle
  • South African market fluency, including how price sensitivity, payment behaviour and language shape marketing to South African adult learners
  • Experience launching a new brand, product or market
  • Familiarity with the South African qualifications landscape, including QCTO, SAQA and NQF frameworks
  • Hands-on capability in Webflow, Intercom, or landing page and CRO tooling
  • Experience using WhatsApp as a conversion channel in an African market
  • Experience with seasonal or single-intake demand patterns
  • Proficiency in an additional South African official language

Benefits:

  • Family member discount on Valenture Institute programmes
  • Remote working
  • Voluntary savings programme
  • Half-day birthday leave

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are:We are a tech-enabled growth firm–at the intersection of marketing, consulting & data intelligence–igniting revenue and brand recognition for leading and emerging companies around the world.
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

We are a tech-enabled growth firm–at the intersection of marketing, consulting & data intelligence–igniting revenue and brand recognition for leading and emerging companies around the world. As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. Our vision is to be recognized as the most valued and respected private growth marketing firm in the world–with a scalable brand, culture and services. Our mission is to power the relentless pursuit of growth and redefine what’s possible through a team of growth-obsessed experts who demand innovation and results - driven by integrity, autonomy, and grit.

As a full-service growth marketing firm, we offer best-in-class services including: SEO, Content Marketing, Paid Media, Social Media Marketing, Programmatic + CTV, Public Relations, Influencer Marketing, Email + SMS, Conversion Rate Optimization, Retail Marketing, and Creative. Here at Power Digital, we are hyper-focused on helping brands drive revenue growth and brand recognition, ultimately driving irrefutable value for our clients.

At the heart of Power Digital is our proprietary technology, nova, which analyzes businesses through first-party data, simplifying investment planning for marketing and diligence in M&A––putting marketers in a strategic seat at the table––and providing value in unparalleled ways.

Managing billions in media, our dynamic team––of consultative marketers, creatives, analysts and technologists––challenge traditional ways of planning and measurement through meticulous testing and data science across each milestone of the customer journey.

***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

A day in the life:

As a Search Experience Specialist, you will begin to own search experience strategies and workflow for your own clients A-Z. You will be responsible for the SEO, GEO/AEO and content strategy and execution of the workflow to help achieve your client’s goals. In addition to driving the strategy, you are also responsible for managing your workflow and the on-time delivery of those deliverables. From keyword research to content optimizations, you will master the execution and presentation of the core SEO, GEO and Content deliverables. Some of the daily tasks include: optimizing content, doing keyword research, assigning deliverables out to deliverable support resources, completing monthly reports, updating internal and external tracking documents, attending internal team calls and external calls with clients, and actively communicating with your account teams. The Search Experience Specialist is a fast learner and a team player who is eager to grow their craft and make a real impact for clients. As you build fluency with Claude and Power Digital's nova ecosystem, AI becomes your default way to speed up keyword research, first-draft reporting, and QA — freeing up time to focus on learning the craft and building client relationships, not replacing your judgment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Execute core SEO, GEO, and content deliverables on time and at a high level of accuracy, with sufficient QA to prevent revenue-impacting errors
  • Conduct keyword research, build and maintain keyword mapping and content clusters, and align topic selection to client business goals and qualified traffic opportunities
  • Assign deliverables to appropriate support resources and review returned work for quality, accuracy, and brand voice alignment
  • Flag patterns, anomalies, or early warning signs noticed during day-to-day execution to the strategist or AD, even when not specifically asked
  • Complete monthly and quarterly reports with minimal feedback, clearly connecting organic search efforts to client business goals and KPI performance
  • Develop a foundational understanding of GEO/AEO concepts and AI search behaviors, and begin incorporating that awareness into strategy and client communication
  • Communicate proactively with account teams and clients, flagging updates, questions, and relevant changes in a timely and professional manner
  • Support execution of the team's search testing roadmap, documenting test results clearly so the senior strategist can build on them
  • Begin building fluency in the client's specific vertical (e.g., B2B, Fashion, CPG) growth patterns rather than treating every account the same
  • Keep deliverable status and QA notes visible in Asana/nova so a strategist or AD can check progress without needing to ask
  • Sign up for Strategy Syncs with the organic search strategy team when a fresh perspective is needed or when an account is in escalation
  • Leverage the Nova ecosystem, AI technologies, and Power Digital workflows (Asana, Slack, novaPulse, Google Drive) to manage workflow and support execution
  • Power Circuit completion and adoption across all assigned accounts
  • Adoption and completion of Omega R&Rs for your role
  • 100% on-time delivery of assigned deliverables and launches, tracked via Asana due dates

Role Requirements:

  • Previous experience in an organic search role (internship or other). Client-facing experience is a plus
  • Basic to foundational understanding of search experience (SEO and GEO) including: on-page, technical, and off-page and how they connect to business goals
  • Familiarity with SEO, GEO and analytics tools such as SEMrush, Ahrefs, Google Search Console, GA4, Profound and Screaming Frog
  • Strong time management, prioritization, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple deliverables across client accounts
  • Fast learner with a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset and a cooperative team-player attitude
  • Clear and professional written and verbal communication skills, both internally and in client-facing settings
  • Comfort using Claude or comparable AI tools as part of daily workflow, with an eagerness to build fluency quickly if not there yet

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Client Book Revenue per Employee: $30k
  • Client Retention Rate: 90%
  • Range of the number of accounts (10-13)
  • Team Retention (of DRs if applicable): 90%

Most Important Things (MITs)

  • Organic Search and GEO production work and strategy to help maintain strategic relationships with organic search clients
  • Tailoring strategies, and thus deliverables that are tied to client goals and being able to explain why you chose those deliverables
  • Professional communication and presentation skills (both internal and external) while showcasing strong problem solving ability.
  • Build daily fluency with Claude and nova tools to accelerate execution — increasingly the default way work gets done, not an occasional shortcut

Benefits & Perks:

  • Base salary + commission opportunities
  • Prepaid Medicine Plan
  • 15 paid vacation days (PTO) per year
  • Up to 4 hours per quarter for paid Volunteer Time Off (VTO) towards philanthropic endeavors
  • Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid
  • A one time 400.000 COP Work From Home (WFH) stipend automatically added to your first paycheck
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • 17 observed Colombian national holidays + 2 mental health recharge days per year
  • Legal benefits like Prima, Cesantias
  • Paid Social Security
  • Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm
  • Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)
  • Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance
  • Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

Power Digital’s people and culture are at the core of our success, which is why diversity in our team’s backgrounds and experiences are paramount. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Please be aware of fictitious job openings, consulting engagements, solicitations, or employment offers from suspicious sources. These engagements may be an attempt to obtain private information, or to induce you to pay a fee for services related to recruitment or training. Power Digital does NOT charge any application, processing, or training fee at any stage of the recruitment or hiring process. All genuine job openings will be posted on our careers page at . If you have any doubts about the authenticity of any messaging behalf of Power Digital, please send us an email at before taking any further action in relation to the correspondence.

About Aegis Ventures

Aegis Ventures partners with entrepreneurs and industry leaders to launch and scale transformative companies in digital health and artificial intelligence. Our platform brings together market-shaping ideas, growth capital, and ambitious individuals to solve major societal problems. With a focus on innovations in healthcare, Aegis has launched four successful portfolio companies in partnership with Northwell Health and recently announced the Digital Consortium to co-develop, invest in, and launch new companies.

About the Company

Avandra Imaging's mission is to unlock clinical data to overcome previously impossible medical challenges, bringing hope and medical breakthroughs that transform patient lives. Avandra is poised to revolutionize healthcare research and innovation by creating the largest indexed data cloud of medical imaging. This platform will unlock unprecedented access to real-world imaging data, essential for biopharma research, medical device innovation, AI model training, and improved patient care.

Leveraging its strategic acquisitions, Avandra aims to aggregate and de-identify vast amounts of imaging data, providing frictionless access to this invaluable resource. With a national footprint of over 5,000 customer integrations and a market share of approximately 70%, this robust infrastructure supports their core business, ensuring continued growth and cash flow to fuel their innovative data cloud platform.

About the Job

As a Senior Software Engineer, help build and scale a category-defining healthcare data platform and you will have experience in Elixir and/or Python. You will play a critical role in designing, developing, and maintaining the systems that power our imaging data marketplace and enable healthcare innovation at scale.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on builder who thrives in an early-stage environment, enjoys solving complex technical problems, and takes ownership of outcomes. Beyond technical expertise, we're looking for someone who embraces collaboration, continuous learning, and helping cultivate a positive engineering culture.

What You’ll Do

Software Development & Architecture

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain scalable software applications using Elixir and Python.
  • Build and support both early-stage and mature production systems that power Avandra's imaging data platform.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into technical solutions.
  • Participate in architecture discussions and contribute to long-term platform strategy.

Technical Leadership & Ownership

  • Take ownership of projects from concept through deployment and ongoing support.
  • Lead technical initiatives with minimal supervision while driving high-quality outcomes.
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to engineering best practices, code quality, and development standards.
  • Help establish scalable processes and frameworks that support company growth.

Continuous Improvement & Innovation

  • Identify opportunities to improve system performance, reliability, and scalability.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend improvements to the engineering stack.
  • Contribute to a culture of experimentation, learning, and technical excellence.
  • Support a startup mindset by flexing across functions and helping solve challenges wherever needed.

Required

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience.
  • Proven experience building and deploying production-grade applications using Elixir and/or Python.
  • Strong understanding of software engineering principles, design patterns, and development best practices.
  • Experience developing and maintaining scalable distributed systems.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently drive projects and manage competing priorities.
  • Passion for continuous learning and staying current with evolving technologies.

Preferred

  • Experience working with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Experience with containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Proficiency with PostgreSQL and/or NoSQL databases.
  • Previous experience mentoring engineers or serving in a technical leadership capacity.
  • Experience working within healthcare technology, health data, medical imaging, or regulated environments.
  • Familiarity with data-intensive applications, APIs, and large-scale platform development.

  • Meaningful Impact: The work we do directly enables medical breakthroughs — such as earlier cancer detection, better Alzheimer's treatments, AI diagnostics that save lives. This isn't abstract; it's the reason our health system partners invest in us.
  • Career-Defining Opportunity: You'll have a front-row seat to every aspect of building a category-defining company—strategy, operations, fundraising, M&A, scaling.
  • Exceptional Team: Work alongside a founder with a track record of building and exiting healthcare technology companies, backed by investors who are true partners.
  • Competitive Package: Competitive salary, equity, comprehensive benefits, and hybrid work flexibility.
  • Values-Driven Culture: We’re building a team grounded in Avandra’s 5 Core Values that guide how we show up every day:
    • WIN with Integrity
    • Radical Accountability
    • Engage with Empathy
    • Innovation Through Playful Curiosity
    • Patients First

Aegis Ventures is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer — we recruit, train, compensate and promote our team members based on qualifications. We encourage you to apply regardless of your race, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, veteran status, or any other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Life as a Sprinter -

Nobody succeeds at Sprinto by staying in their lane.

We are organized around problems, not job titles. Sprinters take ownership beyond their role, solve hard problems, and care deeply about the impact they create. If something can be improved, fixed, or built, we don't wait for permission; we step in.

Being remote means we rely less on proximity and more on trust. We write things down, communicate openly, and move quickly because great teams aren't built by sitting together, they're built by pulling in the same direction.

We believe progress beats perfection, feedback is a gift, and doing the right thing matters, even when nobody is watching.

The Senior Specialist works closely with the Compliance & QA Supervisor and Head of Compliance and operates with a high degree of autonomy on day-to-day program decisions, escalating only complex or precedent-setting issues.

This role is ideal for an experienced compliance professional who wants to lead an agency monitoring program, serves as a go-to subject matter expert for the department, and is comfortable representing compliance externally with carriers and internally with leadership.

What You'll Do

  • Downline Agency Monitoring & Risk Oversight (40%)
    • Lead the Monitoring Framework: They lead the design and evolution of Spark's risk-based monitoring framework for downline agencies, including risk-tiering methodology and monitoring thresholds, operating with minimal day-to-day oversight from the Supervisor and Head of Compliance.
    • Cross-Functional Input: They partner with call quality and case management functions to ensure QA and case findings are incorporated into agency risk tiers.
    • Program-Level Trend Analysis: They independently analyze monitoring data to identify systemic or emerging agency-level risks, and bring findings and recommended program changes directly to the Head of Compliance.

At the same time, the role will translate these global partnerships and policy opportunities into practical value for Teach For All network partners. Working closely with regional teams, the Senior Director will advise and support partners to engage governments, access public and multilateral funding, strengthen enabling policy environments, and expand opportunities to place fellows and influence education systems in their local contexts.

Global Teacher Workforce Strategy & Coalition Building

Lead Teach For All's global strategy on teacher workforce development by building a coalition of governments, multilateral organizations, philanthropy, researchers, and civil society to advance policy frameworks and collective action that strengthen the teaching profession.

Strategic Advisory to Network Partners

Support network partners in translating global policy momentum into national impact by developing government engagement strategies, unlocking public and multilateral funding, strengthening enabling policy environments, and expanding opportunities for fellow placement and long-term organizational sustainability.

Network Learning & Thought Leadership

Generate and disseminate learning, practical tools, and evidence that strengthen partners' public sector engagement while positioning Teach For All as a global thought leader on teacher workforce development and systems change.

    You will own the consumer lifecycle end to end: the moment someone installs the WISECode app through activation, engagement, subscription conversion, retention, and support. Marketing and service are one motion in this role, not two departments. You will work daily with our consumer product lead, our CMO, and the EVP of Customer Success, and you will have real authority to build and evolve our consumer lifecycle via the app. This is a fully hands on role, not a management role, and will be executing each and every day on activities that drive success.

    We are building a consumer lifecycle business at scale. That includes:

    • AI-native, agent-assisted support that solves consumer issues before they escalate.

    • Lifecycle journeys that personalize themselves and adjust as our offerings grow from UPF identification and scanning to coaching to food recommendation and delivery, leveraging our unique food knowledge on our own or through industry partnerships.

    • A knowledge base for consumers that improves as it is used.

    • Reporting that dynamically surfaces opportunities for improvement and growth.

    • Close partnership with Marketing and Consumer Product team on business improvement to exceed customers needs, product development roadmap and proactive messaging to drive retention and growth.

      • We are looking for a systems builder who can scale what used to take a team of ten. If that sentence excites you, keep reading.

What You Own & Execute

    • Onboarding and activation flows that get a new user to their first moment of value fast, and measurably.

    • Lifecycle messaging across email, push, and in-app: welcome, engagement/habit-building, win-back, and the free-to-Premium conversion motion for WISEcoach and other offerings.

    • Consumer support, built AI-first: deflection, escalation paths, SLAs, and voice-of-customer loops back into product.

    • Retention, engagement, and re-engagement: cohort analysis, churn signals, and the programs that move them.

    • The consumer health dashboard: one view of acquisition handoff, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, and support health.

    • Systems that scale. You will select, build, and connect the tooling, with AI agents as first-class workers in every process.

What Success Looks Like

    • Meet and exceed key metrics from activation through Daily/Weekly/Monthly Active User goals in the app, D1/D7/D30 retention, LTV, ARPU, churn/winback rates, strong AppStore and Google play reviews

    • Strong integrated partnership with consumer marketing and product that drives app improvements and increasing engagement.

    • Lifecycle journeys live across the full funnel, with activation and retention baselines set and improving quarter over quarter.

    • Support scales with users, not headcount. Resolution and satisfaction both trend up.

    • A working free-to-Premium conversion engine with strong unit economics behind it.

    • Weekly consumer reporting the executive team uses to make decisions.

What We Are Looking For

    • A senior level doer! This is a hands on opportunity, with no burden of team management or ownership. We are looking for an experienced resource that is energized by being the executor, the point of action and the one making things happen.

    • Experience building AI-native operations and AI tools, that includes agents, automations, and workflows in production and driving customer retention and satisfaction.

    • Five or more years in consumer B2C lifecycle, growth, CRM, or consumer success, with direct ownership of activation, retention, or conversion metrics at meaningful scale.

    • Hands-on fluency with lifecycle and analytics tooling (AppsFlyer, Braze, Iterable, OneSignal, Mixpanel, Amplitude, or equivalents).

    • Strong past experience with consumers in a customer success, support or equivalent role, bonus for business and govt experience.

    • Comfort with speed and ambiguity necessary in a fast paced and multi opportunistic environment.

    • Bonus: health, nutrition, wellness, or subscription consumer app experience.

How We Work

    We are a fast paced, AI first organization built to scale. Decisions are fast, titles matter less than outcomes, and the founder is deep in the details. Company culture of ownership. You to run your area like you own it, because you will.

Compensation

    Competitive base, bonus, and meaningful equity. The position is fully remote, with occasional travel for in person meetings. Details shared in process.

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

We are a tech-enabled growth firm–at the intersection of marketing, consulting & data intelligence–igniting revenue and brand recognition for leading and emerging companies around the world. As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. Our vision is to be recognized as the most valued and respected private growth marketing firm in the world–with a scalable brand, culture and services. Our mission is to power the relentless pursuit of growth and redefine what’s possible through a team of growth-obsessed experts who demand innovation and results - driven by integrity, autonomy, and grit.

As a full-service growth marketing firm, we offer best-in-class services including: SEO, Content Marketing, Paid Media, Social Media Marketing, Programmatic + CTV, Public Relations, Influencer Marketing, Email + SMS, Conversion Rate Optimization, Retail Marketing, and Creative. Here at Power Digital, we are hyper-focused on helping brands drive revenue growth and brand recognition, ultimately driving irrefutable value for our clients.

At the heart of Power Digital is our proprietary technology, nova, which analyzes businesses through first-party data, simplifying investment planning for marketing and diligence in M&A––putting marketers in a strategic seat at the table––and providing value in unparalleled ways.

Managing billions in media, our dynamic team––of consultative marketers, creatives, analysts and technologists––challenge traditional ways of planning and measurement through meticulous testing and data science across each milestone of the customer journey.

***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

A day in the life:

As a key player in our Analytics Engineering & BI team, you'll be at the forefront of how Power Digital designs, governs, and scales its Looker semantic layer. A critical part of your role will be owning the semantic layer modeling that powers every data product we ship, and making sure that layer serves multiple analytics surfaces including conversational analytics. You'll translate ambiguous stakeholder asks into flexible, durable models, ship best-in-class data products, and make sure every consumer of that model, human or AI, gets the right answer every time.

Responsibilities:

- Own and evolve Power Digital's enterprise LookML semantic layer as the governed foundation for analytics across our 1,000+ person organization and 600+ clients.
- Write scalable and performant LookML with rich metadata to support emerging conversational analytics use cases
- Translate ambiguous stakeholder and client asks into clear technical implementations, then design and optimize Looker assets that support scalable, reusable self-service analytics.
- Build best-in-class data products in Looker for internal stakeholders and clients, applying strong data visualization and UI/UX principles.
- Design LookML for scale and performance, partnering with Analytics Engineering on aggregate layer tuning and query optimization, and deploy and govern LookML across multiple Looker instances.
- Own the LookML style guide and naming conventions, train and support users adopting self-service analytics, and mentor junior developers and analysts.
- Employ AI technologies to maximize team leverage and efficiency.
- Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements:

  • 4+ years owning the full lifecycle of production-grade LookML models and data products
  • Advanced SQL proficiency with a modern cloud data warehouse (Snowflake and BigQuery preferred).
  • Strong foundation in dimensional modeling and data warehousing fundamentals.
  • Agency experience, including performance marketing analytics. Comfortable with the measurement, channels, and multi-client pace of a digital marketing agency serving multiple clients from eComm to B2B
  • Experience deploying and governing LookML across multiple Looker instances.
  • Experience with extensible LookML and modular visualizations in a multi-tenant environment
  • Experience mentoring and leveling-up the technical expertise of junior team members.
  • Experience with git-based version control and CI/CD workflows.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, comfortable with both engineers and executives.

Nice to have:

    • Experience routing LLM queries (directing natural-language questions to the right model/Explore.)
    • Conversational Analytics or comparable natural-language BI tooling experience.
    • Claude Code or similar agentic coding tools for accelerated LookML development
    • dbt or equivalent analytics engineering experience

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

- Reuse / leverage ratio: within the first 6 months, achieve >50% of client-facing reporting delivered from shared, governed semantic components (vs. bespoke client-specific LookML). Thereafter, maintain >= 75% quarter-over-quarter, measured from Looker content lineage
- Self-service deflection: within the first 6 months, increase the share of analytical questions resolved by users independently (Self-Service functionality or Omega) to 50% vs. adhoc requests from Asana and Slack. Thereafter, maintain >= 75%
- Source-of-truth integrity: hold production metric-definition discrepancies and data-quality incidents at < 5%, reconciled at each monthly close across Looker and downstream surfaces (Pacing Sheets, LLMs).
- User Experience: 95% of production data products load in 5 seconds or less, measured weekly
- Code quality: 95% style-guide and naming-convention conformance, measured monthly

Most Important Things (MITs)

- Establish and maintain the LookML style guide, naming conventions, and metric-definition source of truth the rest of the team builds against.
- Deliver the highest-priority Looker data products for active client and internal engagements on committed timelines.
- Build and ensure routing scalability of the field-level semantic metadata required for Conversational Analytics and AI-driven queries.
- Partner with Analytics Engineering to methodically tune diagnose and clear performance bottlenecks on production data products.
- Mentor and deputize junior developers through hands-on PR review and pairing on modeling and visualization work.

Power Digital’s people and culture are at the core of our success, which is why diversity in our team’s backgrounds and experiences are paramount. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

These engagements may be an attempt to obtain private information, or to induce you to pay a fee for services related to recruitment or training. Power Digital does NOT charge any application, processing, or training fee at any stage of the recruitment or hiring process. All genuine job openings will be posted on our careers page at . If you have any doubts about the authenticity of any messaging behalf of Power Digital, please send us an email at before taking any further action in relation to the correspondence.

jobs.title: Remote UGC Content Creator (On-Camera)
jobs.excerpt: We are looking for a remote, on-camera UGC Content Creator to become a recurring face of our app across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and paid social content.
jobs.description:
We are looking for a remote, on-camera UGC Content Creator to become a recurring face of our app across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and paid social content.
You will turn product ideas, trends, and everyday social moments into short videos that feel natural to Gen Z audiences: direct, relatable, warm, and entertaining without feeling overproduced.

Responsibilities:

  • Concept, script, film, and edit short-form vertical videos.
  • Appear on camera in relatable scenarios, product demonstrations, reactions, and story-led content.
  • Create organic social posts and UGC-style paid advertisements.
  • Translate briefs into natural creator language rather than reading corporate scripts.
  • Test different hooks, openings, captions, and calls to action.
  • Follow TikTok and Reels culture and propose relevant content formats.
  • Use performance feedback to improve and iterate on successful ideas.
  • Build a consistent and recognizable on-camera presence for the app.
  • Female creator aged 18 or older who is comfortable becoming a recurring on-camera representative for a consumer social app.
  • Strong understanding of Gen Z language, humor, references, creator formats, and viewing habits.
  • Natural and confident camera presence.
  • Clear spoken English; Arabic is a strong advantage.
  • Portfolio of short-form content, UGC, TikTok, Reels, or similar creator work.
  • Able to produce clean vertical videos with good lighting and clear audio using your own phone and basic setup.
  • Working knowledge of CapCut, Premiere Pro, Final Cut, or an equivalent editor.
  • Strong scripting instincts, especially for the first one to three seconds of a video.
  • Reliable, responsive, and able to work independently from briefs and deadlines.
  • Comfortable receiving direct feedback and producing multiple iterations.

Follower count is not a requirement. Communication, taste, consistency, and authenticity matter more.

To apply, please include:

- Links to three to five short-form videos that best represent your work.
- A short introduction explaining how you connect with Gen Z audiences.
- Your location, spoken languages, equipment, availability, and expected rate.
- Optional: a 30–60 second sample showing how you would introduce an app that helps close friends share spontaneous updates through a home-screen widget.

We are building a mobile social app that helps close friends stay connected through spontaneous photos, short updates, private conversations, and home-screen widgets.

We are a small, fast-moving team creating a more personal alternative to crowded social feeds. We care about honest communication, playful creativity, and content that feels human rather than corporate.

jobs.title: Senior Vaccination Researcher
jobs.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

Summary

GiveWell is seeking a Senior Vaccination Researcher to help us direct tens of millions of dollars annually to the most cost-effective vaccination programs that we can find. You will have an outsized influence on our funding decisions and help us save and improve lives on a global scale.

Our vaccination grantmaking is focused on increasing coverage of routine immunization in children under the age of two in areas with high burden of vaccine-preventable disease. This has included supporting targeted outreach and mobile vaccination, demand-side incentives, and support for malaria vaccine rollout. In the future, we may expand into new areas such as campaigns, subsidizing vaccine procurement, supply chain support, surveillance and outbreak response, and R&D for vaccines or vaccine delivery technology. Vaccination is one of our fastest-growing areas, from $12 million in 2024 to $50 million in 2025 and more than $70 million expected in 2026.

As a Senior Vaccination Researcher, you’ll create and lead ambitious research agendas related to our portfolios of work and answer complex questions that will inform GiveWell’s grantmaking decisions. The researchers on our team combine rigorous evidence review, cost-effectiveness modeling, and thoughtful judgment.

We’re open to a wide variety of professional development pathways depending on your preferences and our needs.

The role

You will be joining a small grantmaking team to contribute to our ambitious research agenda on vaccination. You’ll sift through the countless questions we could try to answer, and home in on those that matter most. You’ll also communicate externally about your work and mentor and advise other researchers on the team.

You will shape a research agenda that brings rigor and creativity to the thorniest questions the GiveWell vaccination team faces. Your work will combine empirical evidence review and critical synthesis, cost-effectiveness modeling, discussions with subject matter experts, understanding of the broader context, and your own judgment.

What you might work on in your first year:

  • How should GiveWell’s portfolio of investments change in response to new technologies and shifts in government or funder resources and priorities?
  • What are the most promising opportunities for grant-making in areas such as surveillance and outbreak response and R&D for vaccines or vaccine delivery technology? How should we prioritize those relative to current core areas?
  • How can we improve our methods for evaluating the impact of programs on vaccination coverage? How can we collect more useful data and combine various sources of information to generate a holistic picture of which programs to expand and which to exit?
  • What are the core differences between GiveWell's cost-effectiveness model and other vaccine cost-effectiveness models and what learnings from the external models should we apply to our model?
  • What is the best design for a study to improve available estimates of the impact of key childhood vaccines on disease-specific mortality or all-cause mortality?

The Senior Vaccination Researcher will help shape a major annual grantmaking portfolio, own grant investigations end-to-end (from research question through grant recommendation), and represent GiveWell to external counterparts. You'll have significant latitude to propose new areas of work.

Team structure

Our research department has over 60 people, and is currently organized into seven teams:

  • Five of the teams (Livelihoods, Malaria, Nutrition, Vaccination, and Water) focus on specific areas of grantmaking.
  • The New Areas team focuses on interventions in domains that are new to GiveWell.
  • The Cross-Cutting team focuses on methodological issues, research quality, and other big-picture concerns that cut across all of our research work.
  • The Commons team provides generalized research support to each of the other teams, including landscaping research, vetting, and publishing.

There are currently four people on our vaccination team.

Team values

We think our research team has unique qualities:

  • We care deeply and centrally about finding and sharing truth. Truth-seeking is one of our core values. We post our mistakes and we prize our team members who keep our culture of free-flowing feedback strong.
  • We are independent. We focus 100% on finding the most cost-effective opportunities to save and improve lives. Our researchers assist in communicating our research findings to the public and our donors, and on occasion we provide tailored advice to ultra-high-net-worth donors who want to rely on our expertise to direct their giving—but we never ask our researchers to trade off against honesty, or to hide their real beliefs.
  • We don’t waste time. Once it’s clear that a particular research question is unlikely to change our bottom-line funding recommendation, we drop it as quickly as possible. We encourage our research staff to constantly re-evaluate their portfolios and only work on the highest-priority questions.
  • Lean research team = huge personal impact. In 2026,our research team of ~80 people is directing close to 1 billion dollars and we expect grantmaking dollars per research team member to increase in the future.
  • We work well together. Our research team is lean because we’re able to attract top-tier people, all of whom complete skills-based assessments before joining our staff. We maintain a high-performing, collegial culture and pay our staff accordingly.

About you

We expect the Senior Vaccination Researcher to have

  • A quantitatively oriented advanced degree (e.g., in epidemiology, statistics, economics or related fields)
  • Substantial professional experience in the vaccination landscape (broadly defined). This could include experience in epidemiological or health economics modeling, and/or in program implementation or funding.

We expect that people with the soft qualities below will be the most successful and happy on our team. This isn’t a full list, but hopefully it conveys the gist of our team’s professional personality:

  • GiveWell’s mission and methods are personally energizing—you like our approach to research and you find personal meaning in our story of impact.
  • You’re abnormally curious—you ask lots of questions, and you’re willing to interrogate others’ work. Your curiosity also extends to your own work—you aren’t defensive when your research comes under scrutiny.
  • You routinely think about and surface the value judgments, background knowledge, and strategic commitments that undergird your work. You understand the potential effects of mistaken mental models, so you strive to improve yours and your team’s.
  • You dislike it when people express strong confidence in views that don’t seem to rely on commensurate evidence. You carefully and legibly communicate about your confidence levels.
  • You appreciate the value of an excellent reputation and strong relationships. You can moderate your directness and intensity when you’re communicating with external folks.
  • You love a gnarly problem. You figure out the most important questions to answer, go deep on the details where they matter (and move on where they don’t), and reassess your mental models based on what you’ve learned.
  • You constantly assess whether you and the team are working on the most important things.

If you’re interested in working on GiveWell’s research team but don’t have vaccination expertise, consider applying to our generalist Senior Researcher role.

The details

  • Compensation: We set salaries using a location-based tier system. Our pay for this role:
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $308,000.
    • All other U.S. locations: $280,000.
    • International: Similar to the “all other U.S. locations” salary, based on historical exchange rates and delivered in locally-denominated currency. We can share a precise figure upon request after the first work trial stage.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the US for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year, plus a one week organization-wide summer break
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • Automatic contribution equal to 5% of your gross salary into your 403(b) retirement plan (for U.S. based staff)
  • Location: GiveWell’s staff work primarily remotely within the U.S. and abroad. This position is eligible to work fully remotely. A successful candidate will need to commit to a work schedule that has some overlap with American working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California; Brooklyn, NYC; or London, UK. We'll cover relocation expenses for candidates who wish to move to any of our physical office locations.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Visa Sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we’ll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Travel: Research team members are sometimes required to attend international site visits and conferences (on average 1-2 per year), with additional travel for those interested in traveling more. Additionally, we strongly encourage staff members to attend whole-org and department retreats 3 times per year to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. We'll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we’ll accommodate staff who have conflicting family or other obligations.
  • Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer, but we’ll offer flexibility for candidates whose personal or professional circumstances require them to moderately delay their start date.

Miscellaneous details:

  • Please apply to only one Senior Researcher posting. If you have deep expertise in this area, this pod-specific role is the right fit. If not, there's no need to apply here — our generalist Senior Researcher role is designed for strong researchers who don't have a single specialization, and you don't need to apply to both. Applying to the generalist role won't put you at any disadvantage!
  • Please note that our hiring process consists of the same work trials for the following roles: Researcher, Senior Researcher, Senior Cross-Cutting Researcher, Senior Livelihoods Researcher, Senior Malaria Researcher, Senior New Areas Researcher, Senior Nutrition Researcher, Senior Vaccination Researcher, and Senior Water Researcher. If, within the last year, you applied and were rejected for one of these roles, you should hold off on applying to the other roles, unless explicitly asked to do so by a member of our team. If you're interested in all of these roles, please just apply once and note in your application that you'd like to be considered for the other roles, too.
  • After application review, our hiring process consists of a short application exercise and up to 15 hours of compensated work trials. You can see more details about our hiring process on our FAQs page.
  • We devote significant staff capacity to initial application review, and we respond to all applications as quickly as possible.
  • We have a strong preference for full-time applicants, but we’ll consider applications for part-time work. We aren’t interested in reviewing applications for contract or project-based work at this time.
  • If we settle on an application deadline, we’ll write it in bold here. If you’re on our website job posting and don’t see a deadline, there is no deadline. If you’re reading this on an external job board and don’t see a deadline, you should double-check on our website.
  • You don't need to submit a cover letter—we rely mainly on your resume and answers to the application questions below when we're making early decisions.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

GiveWell is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer by choice. At minimum, this means that we comply with all federal, state, and local EEO and employment laws. Beyond the requirements of those laws, we value our team’s diversity in all respects, and we desire to maintain a work environment free of harassment or discrimination—we want our team members to thrive at GiveWell. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at . We will consider employment for qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that you have read and consent to GiveWell's Privacy Statement for Applicants. By completing an application exercise, you acknowledge and assent to GiveWell's Work Trial Policy.

jobs.excerpt: Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm.
jobs.description:
Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. Most modernization work doesn't ship, it stalls in pilots, slips a year, or lands at three times the budget. We exist to ship it: production systems running, legacy retired, outcomes measured. Our delivery is built on Aedeon, the agent platform built by Mactores' founders' sister company, which absorbs the repetitive 60–70% of engagement work, discovery, dependency mapping, validation, test generation, that traditional consulting bills human hours against. Forward-deployed engineers own the rest: architecture, judgment, and cutover, on dates we commit to in the contract.

Modernization only counts when the release lands and the legacy system gets switched off and the DevOps team is where that discipline lives. As a DevOps Engineer intern, you'll join the team managing large customer deployments: Linux and Windows administration, large enterprise applications, and big data workloads. This work serves our infrastructure and application modernization pillar the migrations that move customers off dedicated hardware and onto AWS.

You're here to learn the agent-native craft, not to own cutover the senior engineers carry that commitment. What you will own is real operational work: tickets, provisioning automation, release support. Automation is the core skill you'll build, because in a firm where agents absorb the repetitive majority of delivery work, the engineers who matter are the ones who automate the rest.

What you will do

  • Work the operations tickets and project task queue with the DevOps team.
  • Communicate with the rest of Engineering to roll out broad changes for customers.
  • Automate operational and server provisioning workflows using AWS CloudFormation templates.
  • Share responsibility for deploying releases and other operations maintenance.
  • Improve operations infrastructure — Jenkins clusters, Bitbucket, monitoring tools (Consul), and metrics tools such as Graphite and Grafana.
  • Provide operational support for the rest of the Engineering team.
  • Help migrate our remaining dedicated hardware infrastructure to the cloud retiring hardware, not just racking new services.

What you need for this opportunity

  • Conceptual understanding of version control systems (git), including branching and merging strategies.
  • Conceptual understanding of cloud platforms: AWS, Azure, GCP.
  • Conceptual understanding of Snowflake.
  • Conceptual understanding of or exposure to software build tools (Maven, Gradle) and continuous integration tools (Jenkins); must have supported Java-based applications in a production environment.
  • Conceptual understanding of Linux environments and scripting languages — bash, Python, Groovy.

How we work?

    Mactores delivers through agents plus forward-deployed engineers. Aedeon, the agent platform we deploy, handles the repetitive majority of engagement work discovery, mapping, validation, test generation and engineers handle the judgment calls and the cutover itself. We commit to fixed delivery dates, so operational discipline isn't optional here. As an intern you'll learn that discipline where it's most visible: in the release pipeline, the monitoring stack, and the automation that keeps both honest.

Life at Mactores

We care about creating a culture that makes a real difference in the lives of every Mactorian. Our 10 Core Leadership Principles that honor Decision-making, Leadership, Collaboration, and Curiosity drive how we work.
1. Be one step ahead
2. Deliver the best
3. Be bold
4. Pay attention to the detail
5. Enjoy the challenge
6. Be curious and take action
7. Take leadership
8. Own it
9. Deliver value
10. Be collaborative
We would like you to read more details about the work culture on

A series of evaluations of your technical proficiency and suitability for the role.
Managerial Interview: The hiring manager engages with you in multiple discussions, 30 minutes to an hour each, covering technical skills, hands-on experience, leadership potential, and communication.
