jobs.title: Senior Cross-Cutting Researcher
jobs.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

Summary

GiveWell is seeking a Senior Researcher on our Cross-Cutting team to help us make better funding decisions across our entire portfolio. The Cross-Cutting team works on methodological questions, research quality, and big-picture problems that don't sit naturally inside any single program area.

Cross-Cutting team’s work has included pressure-testing our work through retrospective evaluations of completed grants ("lookbacks") and scrutinizing grantmaking areas ("red teaming"), collecting more on-the-ground quantitative and qualitative information to check what our grantmaking might be missing, looking for ways to use AI to improve our research process, experimenting with new ways to solicit feedback, figuring out how to quantify the “value of information” in our grantmaking, and answering thorny research questions that affect our entire portfolio.

As a Senior Cross-Cutting Researcher, you'll shape ambitious research agendas that cut across GiveWell's portfolios and answer complex questions that inform grantmaking decisions across the organization. The researchers on our team combine rigorous evidence review, cost-effectiveness modeling, and thoughtful judgment.

We're open to a wide variety of professional development pathways depending on your preferences and our needs.

The role

You will be joining a small team focused on the methodological and cross-portfolio questions that shape how GiveWell does research. You'll sift through the countless questions we could try to answer, hone in on those that matter most, and partner with grantmaking teams (Malaria, Water, Nutrition, Vaccines, Livelihoods, New Areas) to pressure-test and extend their work. You'll also communicate externally about your work and mentor and advise other researchers on the team.

You will shape a research agenda that brings rigor and creativity to the thorniest questions GiveWell faces across its grantmaking. Your work will combine empirical evidence review and critical synthesis, cost-effectiveness modeling, discussions with subject matter experts, understanding of the broader context, and your own judgment. In the course of your work, you might approach questions like:

  • Are our grants actually achieving what we predicted? How do we know, and how can we improve our decisions over time?
  • How do we systematically incorporate field insights, monitoring data, and external feedback into our work?
  • How do we design M&E systems that tell us whether grants are working, not just whether grantees are reporting what we asked for?
  • How can we use AI tools to speed up or increase the quality of our work?
  • How should we model spillover effects? Do health programs affect income, and vice versa? Are we consistent in how we handle this across program areas?
  • How should we set our cost-effectiveness bar over time when funding and spending vary unpredictably year to year?
  • How should we value averting a death versus improving health outcomes versus increasing income? (Our "moral weights" problem)
  • Where are the systematic risks in our research (i.e., the areas where if we're wrong, we're making big mistakes in how we allocate funding)?

Team structure

Our research department has over 60 people, and is currently organized into eight teams, including Cross-Cutting:

  • Five of the teams (Water, Livelihoods, Nutrition, Malaria, and Vaccines) focus on specific areas of grantmaking.
  • The New Areas team focuses on interventions in domains that are new to GiveWell.
  • The Commons team provides generalized research support to each of the other teams, including landscaping research, vetting, and publishing.

The Cross-Cutting team works closely with other grantmaking teams. Projects typically involve partnering with a team to pressure-test or extend their work, or running methodological projects that set standards across the department.

Team values

We think our research team has unique qualities:

  • We care deeply and centrally about finding and sharing truth. Truth-seeking is one of our core values. We post our mistakes and we prize our team members who keep our culture of free-flowing feedback strong.
  • We are independent. We focus 100% on finding the most cost-effective opportunities to save and improve lives. Our researchers assist in communicating our research findings to the public and our donors, and on occasion we provide tailored advice to ultra-high-net-worth donors who want to rely on our expertise to direct their giving—but we never ask our researchers to trade off against honesty, or to hide their real beliefs.
  • We don’t waste time. Once it’s clear that a particular research question is unlikely to change our bottom-line funding recommendation, we drop it as quickly as possible. We encourage our research staff to constantly re-evaluate their portfolios and only work on the highest-priority questions.
  • Lean research team = huge personal impact. In 2026,our research team of ~80 people is directing close to 1 billion dollars and we expect grantmaking dollars per research team member to increase in the future.
  • We work well together. Our research team is lean because we’re able to attract top-tier people, all of whom complete skills-based assessments before joining our staff. We maintain a high-performing, collegial culture and pay our staff accordingly.

About you

Senior Cross-Cutting Researchers typically have quantitatively oriented advanced degrees and substantial relevant experience using empirical tools to make rigorous, evidence-based decisions in the real world. Practically, our senior research staff typically has 5-10 years of post-grad work experience prior to joining GiveWell. We're happy to consider applicants who do not have advanced degrees, but we'll look for a commensurate amount of relevant experience.

We expect that people with the soft qualities below will be the most successful and happy on our team. This isn’t a full list, but hopefully it conveys the gist of our team’s professional personality:

  • GiveWell’s mission and methods are personally energizing—you like our approach to research and you find personal meaning in our story of impact.
  • You’re abnormally curious—you ask lots of questions, and you’re willing to interrogate others’ work. Your curiosity also extends to your own work—you aren’t defensive when your research comes under scrutiny.
  • You routinely think about and surface the value judgments, background knowledge, and strategic commitments that undergird your work. You understand the potential effects of mistaken mental models, so you strive to improve yours and your team’s.
  • You dislike it when people express strong confidence in views that don’t seem to rely on commensurate evidence. You carefully and legibly communicate about your confidence levels.
  • You appreciate the value of an excellent reputation and strong relationships. You can moderate your directness and intensity when you’re communicating with external folks.
  • You love a gnarly problem. You figure out the most important questions to answer, go deep on the details where they matter (and move on where they don’t), and reassess your mental models based on what you’ve learned.
  • You constantly assess whether you and the team are working on the most important things.

Senior Cross-Cutting Researcher vs. other Senior Researcher roles

We're hiring Senior Researchers for both our Cross-Cutting team and our grantmaking teams. If you're energized by variety and methodological questions that span multiple program areas, Cross-Cutting may be a better fit. If you're excited to develop deep expertise in a specific program area and eventually own a grantmaking portfolio, our grantmaking-team-specific Senior Researcher roles (e.g., Senior Malaria Researcher or Senior Livelihoods Researcher) may be a better fit.

Not sure? Apply to whichever sounds more appealing—we'll help you figure out the right fit during the process, and we're open to moving candidates between tracks.

The details

  • Compensation: We set salaries using a location-based tier system. Our pay for this role:
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $308,000.
    • All other U.S. locations: $280,000
    • International: Similar to the “all other U.S. locations” salary, based on historical exchange rates and delivered in locally-denominated currency. We can share a precise figure upon request after the first work trial stage.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the US for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • Automatic contribution equal to 5% of your gross salary into your 403(b) retirement plan (for U.S. based staff)
  • Location: GiveWell’s staff work primarily remotely within the U.S. and abroad. This position is eligible to work fully remotely.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California; Brooklyn, NYC; or London, UK. We'll cover relocation expenses for candidates who wish to move to any of our physical office locations.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis. A successful candidate will need to commit to a work schedule that has some overlap with American working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Visa Sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we’ll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Travel: Research team members are sometimes required to attend international site visits and conferences (on average 1-2 per year), with additional travel for those interested in traveling more. Additionally, we strongly encourage staff members to attend quarterly whole-org and department retreats to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. We'll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we’ll accommodate staff who have conflicting family or other obligations.
  • Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer, but we’ll offer flexibility for candidates whose personal or professional circumstances require them to moderately delay their start date.

Miscellaneous details:

  • Please note that our hiring process consists of the same work trials for the following roles: Researcher, Senior Researcher, Senior Cross-Cutting Researcher, Senior Livelihoods Researcher, Senior Malaria Researcher, Senior New Areas Researcher, Senior Nutrition Researcher, Senior Vaccination Researcher, and Senior Water Researcher. If, within the last year, you applied and were rejected for one of these roles, you should hold off on applying to the other roles, unless explicitly asked to do so by a member of our team. If you're interested in all of these roles, please just apply once and note in your application that you'd like to be considered for the other roles, too.
  • After application review, our hiring process consists of a short application exercise and up to 15 hours of compensated work trials. You can see more details about our hiring process on our FAQs page!
  • We devote significant staff capacity to initial application review, and we respond to all applications as quickly as possible.
  • We’re aiming to hire four to six full-time Senior Researchers.
  • We have a strong preference for full-time applicants, but we’ll consider applications for part-time work. We aren’t interested in reviewing applications for contract or project-based work at this time.
  • If we settle on an application deadline, we’ll write it in bold here. If you’re on our website job posting and don’t see a deadline, there is no deadline. If you’re reading this on an external job board and don’t see a deadline, you should double-check on our website.
  • You don't need to submit a cover letter—we rely mainly on your resume and answers to the application questions below when we're making early decisions.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

GiveWell is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer by choice. At minimum, this means that we comply with all federal, state, and local EEO and employment laws. jobs.description:
Wir wachsen schneller, als unsere Betreuungsstruktur mitkommt. Aktuell hängen zu viele Entscheidungen an zu wenigen Köpfen — und unsere Account Manager:innen brauchen jemanden, der sie führt, nicht nur jemanden, der über ihnen steht.

Deshalb bauen wir die Ebene der Key Account Manager aus. Du übernimmst ein eigenes Team und ein eigenes Kundenportfolio — und gestaltest mit, wie Betreuung bei MAILODY in Zukunft funktioniert.

Wir sagen offen dazu: Diese Rolle ist gerade die anspruchsvollste im Unternehmen. Du bekommst Druck von oben (Wachstumsziele) und von unten (ein Team, das sich erst einspielt). Wir wissen das, wir lassen dich damit nicht allein — aber wir tun auch nicht so, als wäre es bequem.

Aufgaben

Führung

  • Du führst 3–5 Account Manager:innen fachlich und disziplinarisch.
  • Du führst wöchentliche 1:1s nach klarer Struktur (Fortschritt / Probleme / Pläne) und verantwortest die Gesundheit deines Teams.
  • Du entwickelst deine Leute aktiv weiter — Schulungen, Feedback, strukturierte Einarbeitung.

Kunden

  • Du verantwortest Entwicklung und Ergebnis deines eigenen Kundenportfolios (Richtwert 6–8 Accounts, ausschließlich unsere anspruchsvollsten Kunden). Das Tagesgeschäft liegt bei deinen AMs.
  • Du bist geschätzter Ansprechpartner auf der Senior-Entscheiderebene deiner Kunden und platzierst Themen aktiv in Kunden-Calls.
  • Du erkennst Churn-Risiken früh, entscheidest die Gegenmaßnahmen für dein Team und drehst gefährdete Accounts zurück in Wachstum.

Fachlichkeit & Prozesse

  • Du bist die fachliche Rückfallebene deines Teams — Klaviyo- und CRM-Architektur beherrschst du in der Breite.
  • Du coachst deine AMs fachlich und baust ihre Fähigkeiten auf, statt nur Fragen zu beantworten.
  • Du ownst einen unternehmensweiten Prozess rund um unsere Mitarbeitenden (z. B. Onboarding oder Offboarding).
  • Du stimmst Standards mit den anderen Key Account Managern ab und teilst Learnings aktiv.

Qualifikation

  1. Mindestens 3–4 Jahre Erfahrung im E-Mail-Marketing oder CRM; davon idealerweise ein Teil in einer Agentur oder im E-Commerce.
  2. Tiefe Praxis in Klaviyo oder einem vergleichbaren System (Braze, Emarsys, Bloomreach, Salesforce Marketing Cloud). Du hast komplexe Set-ups selbst gebaut, nicht nur begleitet.
  3. Erste Führungs- oder Mentoring-Erfahrung— du hast schon einmal Verantwortung für die Arbeit anderer getragen. Das muss nicht disziplinarisch gewesen sein.
  4. Sicherheit im Kundenkontakt auf Entscheiderebene— du hast schon mit Geschäftsführung oder Marketingleitung auf Augenhöhe gesprochen.
  5. Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und gutes Englisch, schriftlich wie mündlich.
  6. Wohnsitz in Deutschland(steuer- und sozialversicherungsrechtlich zwingend).

Und was wir uns wünschen, aber nicht voraussetzen: Du gibst Feedback direkt und nimmst es genauso an. Du fragst nach dem Warum hinter den Zahlen eines Kunden. Du wartest nicht, bis dir jemand einen Prozess gibt.

Das ist nichts für dich, wenn …

  • … du Führung als Beförderung siehst und nicht als eigenes Handwerk, das man lernen muss.
  • … du Dinge lieber selbst machst, als sie abzugeben und jemanden dabei besser zu machen.
  • … du eine fertige Struktur erwartest. Wir bauen sie gerade — mit dir.
  • … du unangenehme Gespräche aufschiebst. Ein Teil dieser Rolle besteht daraus.
  • … du im Homeoffice Struktur von außen brauchst. Wir arbeiten vollständig remote.

Benefits

  • Ein Team, das dir gehört — und die Freiheit, es zu formen.
  • Klarheit über deinen eigenen Weg: Wir haben eine ausformulierte Level-Matrix. Du siehst schwarz auf weiß, was auf deinem Level erwartet wird und was der nächste Schritt ist.
  • Halbjährliche Entwicklungsgespräche mit echtem Feedback statt Formularen. Gehalt wird bei uns nach System vergeben, nicht nach Verhandlungsgeschick.
  • Führungskräfte-Ausbildung mit einem externen Coach, der Führungsteams bei Meta und in mehreren Scale-ups aufgebaut hat.
  • 100 % remote, überall in Deutschland — plus regelmäßige Team-Offsites und Workations.
  • MacBook, bei Bedarf zusätzliche Hardware.
  • 50 € monatliche Sachbezugskarte nach der Probezeit.

Sechs Sätze, an denen wir uns messen lassen — auch als Führungskraft:

Be confident.

We don't need all the answers to start, just the grit to find them first.

Be curious.

Let's be obsessed to find the ‚Why‘ to unlock the ‚How‘.

Keep growing.

Treat yourself like brilliant software: ship a new upgrade every month.

Be accountable.

Openness over cosiness. We own our words.

Act entrepreneurial.

Don't just do tasks: own real business impact.

Over-deliver where it matters.

Promise what's possible. Then challenge these boundaries.

  • Accountable & Dependable
  • Team Centric
  • Systems & Process Oriented

  • Apply underwriting-level financial, construction, and risk analysis to guide workout, modification, and foreclosure decisions.

  • Identify discrepancies and red flags in draw requests, budget revisions, borrower documentation, and guarantor/ownership structures; escalate suspected fraud or misrepresentation with clearly documented support.
  • Execute loss mitigation strategies — including modifications, forbearance, added guarantors, workout agreements, deed-in-lieu, and foreclosure — in partnership with legal and senior leadership.

  • Understanding of business purpose loans, loss mitigation, and the mechanics of default, workout, and foreclosure.

  • Advanced Excel proficiency; strong Word skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to lead difficult conversations professionally and confidently.
  • Sound judgment and critical thinking — able to evaluate situations on their merits rather than by checklist alone.

jobs.description:
The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $8,000 per month (Gross in USD)

About Sezzle:
With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

About the Role:
We are seeking a talented and motivated Senior Technical Product Manager who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement.

Sezzle is building the platform that will carry us from a BNPL provider into a full-stack financial institution. This role owns the system at the center of that: Sezzle’s banking core — the ledger, accounts and balances, and the money movement that every future Sezzle financial product will run on.

You would own it end to end. Discovery, architecture and vendor decisions, requirements, build, launch, and everything after — not a slice of someone else’s roadmap, but the full product lifecycle for the platform itself. You’d work directly with Engineering, Finance, Compliance, Treasury, and Risk, with real authority over how this gets built.

Ideally you’ve built something like this before. If you haven’t, but you’ve owned a ledger, a payments platform, an issuing program, or other financial infrastructure — and you’re the kind of person who learns a domain properly rather than around the edges — we want to talk to you. What matters most is that you’ve owned real infrastructure and that you’re willing to go deep on the parts you don’t know yet.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the banking platform roadmap. Define and sequence the platform work required to support accounts, deposits, cards, and lending on a single ledger and account model.
  • Help drive the build-vs-buy decision. Evaluate core banking platforms and processors, run vendor diligence, model cost and time-to-market, and help leadership decide whether we extend what we have or integrate a third party.
  • Shape the account and ledger model. Work with Engineering and Finance on account hierarchies, sub-ledgers, chart-of-accounts mapping, posting rules, holds, interest and fee accrual, and general ledger integration.
  • Specify money movement. Own product requirements for transfers, ACH, card issuing and network settlement, real-time rails, and returns and reversals — including exception handling, cutoff windows, and settlement reconciliation.
  • Make the platform auditable. Ensure the system produces the reporting, traceability, and controls that Finance, audit, and regulators need — reconciliation breaks, balance attestation, and complete transaction history.
  • Partner on regulatory readiness. Work with Compliance and Legal to turn their requirements into platform capabilities: screening hooks, onboarding data, error resolution, disclosures and statements, and reporting. You don’t need to arrive fluent in US banking regulation — you do need to be someone who learns it properly.
  • Plan migration and cutover. If a migration is in scope, own data mapping, parallel-run strategy, validation criteria, rollback plans, and phased cutover.
  • Write the technical requirements. Own detailed specs, API contracts, event schemas, data models, user stories, and release plans end-to-end.
  • Use data to prove it works. Write your own SQL. Define platform KPIs — posting latency, reconciliation break rate, settlement accuracy, failure rates — and monitor them relentlessly.
  • Manage risk early. Anticipate technical risks, edge cases, race conditions, and dependencies before they become incidents. Money movement defects are the expensive kind.
  • Operate with urgency. Deliver against an evolving regulatory and business timeline with incomplete information.

What We Look For:

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or other technical discipline (required).
  • 5–10 years of product experience, with meaningful time spent on financial infrastructure rather than only customer-facing surfaces.
  • Real ownership in at least one of the following. You do not need all of them, and we care much more about depth in one than exposure to several:
  1. Ledgers, general ledger, or balance and transaction systems
  2. Payments processing, orchestration, or money movement — ACH, card networks, transfers, settlement, or the LATAM equivalents (PIX, SPEI, PSE, CCE)
  3. Card issuing or card program management
  4. Deposit, wallet, or account platforms
  5. Lending origination or loan servicing platforms
  6. Product work at a processor, BaaS provider, or core banking vendor
  • Comfort with double-entry accounting concepts as they show up in software — debits and credits, sub-ledgers, accruals, reconciliation — or a genuine appetite to get comfortable with them quickly.
  • Deep technical understanding of APIs, event-driven architecture, idempotency, distributed system failure modes, batch vs. real-time processing, and data flows.
  • Strong SQL skills and comfort querying and interpreting data independently.
  • Experience working directly with Compliance, Legal, Finance, or Treasury as stakeholders — not only Engineering and Design.
  • Comfortable working in ambiguity and making sound, documented decisions with incomplete information.
  • Strong written and verbal communication — can hold your own in an engineering standup, a Finance review, and an executive discussion.
  • Hands-on familiarity with AI tools, data models, or generative AI applications—personally, professionally, or better yet, both!

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Direct experience with a core banking platform, in-house or vendor (Thought Machine, Mambu, 10x, Finxact, Temenos, Technisys, Galileo, Pismo, or similar).
  • Experience with a core migration, conversion, or major ledger replacement.
  • Experience at a chartered or licensed financial institution, or supporting a charter, banking licence, or deposit insurance application.
  • Familiarity with consumer finance regulation — US (Reg E, Reg DD, Reg CC, Reg Z, TILA, FCRA, BSA/AML) or equivalent local regimes.
  • Background in consumer credit or BNPL, card products, or bank-fintech sponsorship programs.
  • Experience with third-party risk management and vendor oversight in a regulated environment.

About You:

  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome:
At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

This is a fully remote, full-time role that places you at the heart of a globally connected, learning-focused firm – one where your contributions are valued, your growth is supported, and your voice is heard.

Deliver Post-Production Support

  • Provide day-to-day functional support for US-based clients using Sage Intacct, resolving issues, processing enhancement requests, and optimizing system configurations.
  • Troubleshoot functional problems across core Sage Intacct modules including General Ledger, Accounts Payable/Receivable, Billing, Procurement, Expenses, and Revenue Recognition.
  • Support finance and accounting workflow improvements tied to key processes such as Procure-to-Pay, Order-to-Cash, and Month-End Close.

Collaborate with US-Based Teams

  • Partner closely with US-based CrossCountry consultants and client stakeholders during overlapping business hours, ensuring timely resolution of support tickets and enhancement requests.
  • Prepare clear, concise status updates and escalate issues or risks to CrossCountry project managers as appropriate.
  • Participate in team meetings, client calls, and knowledge-sharing sessions, contributing strong written and verbal English communication throughout.

Drive Quality & Continuous Improvement

  • Assist with data analysis, import/export formatting, testing, and documentation to support client deliverables and system integrity.
  • Identify patterns in support requests and proactively recommend configurations or process changes to reduce recurring issues.
  • Maintain thorough documentation of support activities, configurations, and resolutions in line with CrossCountry standards.

Embrace AI & Emerging Tools

  • Leverage AI-powered tools and automation to enhance the quality, accuracy, and efficiency of your work.
  • Stay current on AI developments relevant to finance and ERP systems, bringing a mindset of curiosity and responsible adoption to your day-to-day work.

What You’ll Bring

Experience

  • 4-6 years of hands-on experience supporting or implementing Sage Intacct in a consulting, advisory, or client-services environment.
  • Solid command of core Sage Intacct modules: General Ledger, AP/AR, Billing, Procurement, Expenses, and Revenue Recognition.
  • Strong understanding of foundational accounting concepts, including Chart of Accounts, Journal Entries, Trial Balance, and Intercompany transactions.
  • Demonstrated experience collaborating with remote, cross-functional teams, ideally with US-based stakeholders across multiple time zones.

Skills

  • Strong spoken and written English communication skills, with the ability to translate technical issues into clear updates for clients and internal teams.
  • Ability to analyze and format data for Sage Intacct imports and exports based on system requirements.
  • Detail-oriented and self-motivated, with a track record of managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Comfort with AI tools and openness to leveraging emerging technologies to improve personal and team productivity.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Sage Intacct Implementation Specialist certification strongly preferred.
  • Chartered Accountant (CA) or equivalent accounting designation is a plus.
  • Experience with project coordination tools, ticketing platforms, and remote collaboration software (e.g., Jira, Salesforce, Microsoft Teams).
  • Availability for partial overlap with US Eastern or Central time zones (typically mornings in Philippine Standard Time).

jobs.description:
About Lendesk:

We’re a financial technology company on a mission to make the mortgage experience easy, accessible, and transparent. Our flagship product is an advanced digital mortgage origination platform that connects borrowers, brokers, and lenders. We’re a fast-growing team of 70+ employees, composed of innovative and engaged individuals working collaboratively to deliver a unique digital home buying experience.

At Lendesk, diversity is our strength. What makes us different, makes us stronger. We believe that a variety of backgrounds, cultures, beliefs, experiences, identities, and voices make for a better and inclusive workplace.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a meaningful area of our product. You'll work within a small, focused team - close to the problem, close to the customer, and close to the decisions that matter. The scope of what you own will be shaped by where the business needs are highest and where your strengths are best applied.

This isn't a role for someone who needs a well-defined playbook handed to them. It's for someone who asks better questions, listens carefully to customers and colleagues, and uses what they learn to build something worth using.

It's also an exciting time to be in product at Lendesk. You'll use AI in your day-to-day workflow and have a genuine opportunity to design and deliver AI-powered solutions for the mortgage industry - a space where that kind of thinking is still early and the upside is real.

What You'll Do

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for your product area: from discovery through delivery and iteration
  • Build and maintain a signal system that brings together customer interviews, analytics, sales insights, and industry research, then turn those signals into clear, actionable recommendations
  • Lead a cross-functional team through discovery, delivery, and iteration - keeping engineering, design, and business stakeholders aligned without losing momentum
  • Partner with sales, marketing, and operations to plan and execute go-to-market motions for new features and releases
  • Develop and own growth analytics for your area: define what success looks like, measure it rigorously, and use it to drive decisions
  • Build genuine expertise in the Canadian mortgage industry - the workflows, the regulations, the competitive dynamics, and the people
  • Contribute to how the product team develops its craft - including how we leverage AI to work smarter

What We're Looking For

This role is probably a strong fit if you:

Are genuinely curious. Not just about the product, but about the industry, the customer, and the problem underneath the problem. You ask questions other people stop asking once they think they know the answer.

Lead with empathy

but balance it with business judgment. You deeply understand the people who use your product and you advocate hard for them. You also know when the right call for the business and the right call for the customer aren't the same thing. You can hold both.

You also bring:

  • 5+ years of experience as a product manager in B2B SaaS, with meaningful time in environments where you had to create direction rather than receive it
  • Genuine comfort with ambiguity; not just tolerance for it, but the ability to turn a messy problem into a clear path forward
  • Strong analytics instincts: you know how to instrument a product, interpret what the data is telling you, and make growth-oriented decisions from it
  • An understanding that in fintech, regulatory and compliance work isn't a side task - it's part of the job, and you take it seriously
  • The ability to earn trust across functions (with engineers, executives, salespeople, and customers) through clear thinking and direct communication
  • Proven ability to thrive in a fully remote environment — you're self-directed, communicate proactively, and don't need an office to do your best work

Nice to Have

  • Experience in mortgage, real estate, or an adjacent regulated industry
  • Familiarity with AI tools in a product or workflow context
  • A business degree (BA or MBA) - though we care more about how you think than where you studied

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salaries
  • Comprehensive benefit plan including dental, medical and vision
  • Remote first, work from where you are in Canada
  • Budget to improve your home office set-up
  • Flexible work hours
  • The latest in hardware and software tools
  • Budget for continuous development and training
  • Stock purchase program in our parent company (“NYSE:RKT”)

You must be a current Canadian resident to be considered for this role. A candidate selected for this position must pass a criminal background check.

Lendesk is committed to offering competitive salaries to all our team members. This role has a salary range of $102,500 - $154,000 CAD. For experienced candidates, we typically hire at or near the midpoint of the salary band to ensure there’s room for continued growth and development. Compensation is determined based on the skills, experience, and qualifications you bring to the team, as well as the impact you will have on the business and the growth you’ll achieve in the role. Throughout your time at Lendesk we’ll continue to have conversations about your career development and you’ll have the opportunity to build an amazing career with us.

jobs.description:
About Product

VyOS is an open-source network operating system that provides an all-in-one platform for network management. Built on Linux, VyOS integrates powerful routing, firewall, VPN, and network services into a unified system. Unlike traditional networking hardware, VyOS can be deployed on a wide range of platforms, from physical routers and cloud environments to virtual machines, giving users flexibility and control over their network infrastructure.

The key strength of VyOS lies in its comprehensive feature set. It supports dynamic routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, RIP), multiple VPN types (IPsec, OpenVPN, WireGuard), firewall rules, traffic shaping, and more - all configured through a unified command-line interface (CLI) familiar to network engineers. Its ability to scale across various environments makes it popular with organizations seeking open-source networking solutions.

Job description

The Network Support Engineer is responsible for developing, validating, and optimizing VyOS networking solutions to ensure performance, stability, and usability. This role involves designing Proof of Concept (PoC) scenarios, testing new features, troubleshooting complex issues, and maintaining technical documentation. The Network Engineer will work closely with developers, support teams, and external partners to enhance VyOS compatibility and functionality across diverse network environments.

Responsibilities

  • Develop new features and optimize existing code for VyOS, ensuring efficient and maintainable implementations.
  • Collaborate with developers to review and validate code changes, test feature implementations, and provide feedback on bugs, optimizations, and feature proposals.
  • Create technical content, including solution briefs, datasheets, and graphical materials, tailored to address specific networking use cases and technical requirements.
  • Design, deploy, and configure network infrastructures using VyOS and other networking equipment to meet project objectives and performance standards.
  • Design and deploy PoC scenarios using VyOS, documenting configuration setups, performance benchmarks, and solution viability for customer-specific requirements.
  • Diagnose and resolve network performance, security, and connectivity issues, utilizing advanced debugging and analysis tools.
  • Investigate escalated technical issues, conduct root cause analysis, and deliver reproducible solutions or detailed technical reports for development resolution.
  • Conduct functional, performance, and regression testing for VyOS features and fixes, creating and maintaining detailed test documentation.
  • Develop and manage automated test frameworks for repetitive test cases, enhancing testing accuracy and efficiency.
  • Enhance testing methodologies by introducing advanced tools and frameworks to optimize validation processes and outcomes.
  • Conduct interoperability testing with third-party systems to ensure seamless integration of VyOS into diverse networking environments.
  • Maintain a centralized knowledge base with detailed, technically accurate articles and solution documentation to support internal and external stakeholders.

Requirements

Skills

  • Strong understanding of networking protocols such as BGP, OSPF, VPNs, and firewalls.
  • Hands-on experience with VyOS or other open-source networking platforms.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages like Python or Bash for automation and testing.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities in complex network environments.
  • Experience with network performance tuning and security best practices.
  • Familiarity with software-defined networking (SDN) and cloud networking principles.
  • Ability to develop and execute test cases for network functionality and performance.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and collaboration.
  • Strong ability to analyze packet captures, system logs, and debugging outputs.
  • Japanese conversational level

Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in networking, system administration, or network security.
  • Experience working with VyOS, open-source network operating systems, or enterprise-grade networking solutions.
  • Prior experience in feature validation, troubleshooting, and debugging network-related issues.
  • Hands-on experience with virtualization platforms (VMware, KVM, Hyper-V) and cloud networking (AWS, GCP, Azure).
  • Experience conducting Proof of Concept (PoC) demonstrations and documenting technical findings.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and automated testing frameworks for networking products.

Work Conditions and Compensation

Fully Remote Work:This 100% remote position allows you to work anywhere.

Flexible Work Schedule:We offer a flexible work schedule that allows you to manage your time while ensuring effective collaboration across our globally distributed teams. The official workday starts between 8 AM and 11 AM (employee local time) and ends between 5 PM and 8 PM (employee local time). While flexibility is encouraged, occasional work outside typical hours may be required to align with colleagues in different time zones. Open communication and availability for cross-time-zone meetings are essential for seamless teamwork.

Time Tracking:Employees are required to use time tracker software to monitor working hours and productivity.

Vacation:Enjoy 20 days of annual paid vacation

National Holidays:You are entitled to up to 10 days of paid leave for recognized national holidays.

Sick Leave: is provided in accordance with company policy

About VyOS Networks

VyOS Networks is a company dedicated to creating cutting-edge, open-source network solutions that empower organizations to manage their networks with flexibility and control. As the company behind the VyOS network operating system, we are committed to delivering a robust, scalable, and secure platform that meets the diverse needs of businesses, service providers, and network professionals worldwide.

At VyOS Networks, our work goes beyond just providing technology - we’re shaping the future of networking with a global, community-driven project. We foster an environment where talented individuals come together to solve complex networking challenges, while continuously improving both our products and ourselves.

Our Mission

Powering a connected world, engineering for the future.

We believe that the future of networking lies in open collaboration, continuous innovation, and delivering solutions that keep the world connected, efficiently and securely.

Our Core Values

Our values define who we are as a team and how we approach our work every day:

  • Respect: We believe in fostering a respectful environment where we value each other's perspectives and contributions. We maintain a deep respect for our colleagues, our open-source community, and our clients, ensuring that all interactions are guided by understanding, professionalism, and empathy.
  • Responsibility: Trust is the foundation of our success. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of honesty, dependability, and accountability. Whether delivering on a commitment to a client or collaborating with a team member, we take responsibility for our actions and their impact.
  • Improvement: We are driven by a relentless desire to improve - ourselves, our products, and the world of networking. Continuous learning, innovation, and refining our processes are key to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
  • Contentment: At VyOS Networks, we believe that work should inspire and fulfill. We create an environment where people are excited to collaborate, share ideas, and find joy in solving real-world problems. We aim to inspire others while finding inspiration in the work we do.

We are Supply Chain & Engineering: We embed innovation, intelligence, and sustainability in the way the world makes things and the things it makes. We help leaders act quickly and confidently as they pivot to the future, delivering the digital reinvention of manufacturing and engineering. We believe that smart, sustainable, connected digital products and assets are about to create hyper-personalized industrial experiences, completely new levels of operational efficiency, transparency and traceability, tangible impact on sustainability, and brand-new sources of revenue growth. This role will align with our Supply Chain & Engineering practice and fall under the Intelligent Asset Management capability.

Supply Chain & Engineering professionals help our clients achieve their ambitions for digital transformation within their core manufacturing and operations throughout the full lifecycle of their assets. With domain expertise across consulting and technology they unlock new sources of opex and capex efficiency and effectiveness.

Intelligent Asset Management professionals are focused on improving profitability and reducing asset-related operational risk over the life cycle, by defining, developing and deploying intelligent asset management solutions (EAM, EAM cloud platforms, RBI, etc.).

The Role:

As an IFS Cloud Solution Architect, you will define and own the end-to-end solution across IFS Cloud engagements, serving as the technical and functional authority our clients rely on from pursuit through delivery. IFS Cloud is a broad enterprise suite, and you will architect across its functional footprint — spanning Finance, Supply Chain, Procurement, Manufacturing, Projects, Human Capital Management, and Enterprise Asset & Service Management. Working collaboratively with senior leadership, you will lead solution blueprinting and advisory, translate client business processes into a coherent and scalable architecture spanning configuration, extensions, and integrations, and make the critical fit-gap and build decisions. You will lead experienced teams to deliver with quality, advise client enterprise architects on the IFS Cloud solution landscape, and develop points of view and thought capital on emerging trends in enterprise transformation. jobs.excerpt: Role MissionKoronet grows when our customers succeed in buying, selling, and operating.
jobs.description:
Role Mission

Koronet grows when our customers succeed in buying, selling, and operating. Your job is to build the systems and intelligence that identify where we can add value, what blocks that growth, and how to scale our impact.

You will work as a solo operator, not a passive analyst. You will build dashboards, decision-making tools that empower teams to act faster and smarter and execute scalable campaigns. You are responsible for transforming raw data into clear, actionable insights and driving real business outcomes at scale.

How we work

We’re one team with one goal: delivering actual value. We share what we learn from customers, help our colleagues succeed, and focus on outcomes, not just checking boxes like 'completed call' or 'closed ticket.'

Transactions at Koronet

Transactions connect how our customers actually work with what our platform can do. We sit between customer feedback and product development, turning what we see in the field into real product improvements. We don't just 'do tasks'—we look for ways to solve problems and use what we learn to make the whole platform better for everyone.

What you will do

  • Build and maintain dashboards and tools for Transactions, Success, Product, and leadership.
  • Turn business questions into reliable decision systems: define the problem, find the evidence, and measure the result.
  • Connect data from calls, feedback, email, and market research to understand how customers buy, list, and sell.
  • Spot patterns across customers to identify where Koronet can add value—whether through better processes, product changes, or new integrations.
  • Drive the marketplace growth model by helping customers improve their sourcing, catalog reliability, and digital sales.
  • Create feedback loops to track if campaigns and product changes actually drive adoption, transaction volume, or efficiency.
  • Design, launch, and execute campaigns to expand and make buying and selling digitally in our ecosystem easier.
  • Track impact on and ensure data quality by investigating inconsistencies rather than guessing.
  • Turn customer insights into clear evidence for other teams to use.
  • Identify and fix internal bottlenecks with automation and better workflows.

How you will use tools:

You will be a solo operator using automation, data analysis, and research tools to move faster.

  • Define the problem, inputs, and goals clearly.
  • Use research and prototyping to build better workflows.
  • Measure results against real customer outcomes.
  • Know when to use automation and when to rely on human judgment or customer context.

Success Criteria:

  • You drive business results at scale through your campaigns and indirectly enabling teams
  • Customer-facing teams have stronger context to drive customer behavior.
  • Product receives clear, prioritized evidence of customer problems and their impact.
  • Insights compound over time into better enablement and product decisions.
  • Your dashboards are trusted because they are accurate and useful, not because they are complex.
  • You accelerate other teams without becoming a bottleneck.

A few things this role isn't!

  • A passive reporting or dashboard-making role.
  • A product manager making roadmap promises.
  • The final decision-maker on strategy.
  • An AI developer hired only to build agents.

What do we expect from you

  • Strong analytical judgment and commercial curiosity.
  • Able to solve ambiguous problems using data, spreadsheets, SQL, or code.
  • Comfortable working across structured and unstructured data.
  • Excellent communication skills; you can turn complex data into useful narratives for other teams.
  • Interest in marketplaces, B2B SaaS, and operational systems.
  • Humble, rigorous, and team-first: you surface uncertainty and improve the system rather than defending your first guess.
  • Fluent in English (must).
  • Experience in the floriculture industry will be considered a strong plus.

What We Offer:

  • An independent, flexible, and versatile role within a fast-growing international organization.
  • Flexible / Remote working environment.
  • We encourage continuous learning and professional growth.

Why Join Koronet:

  • Global and Remote-First: Work with a diverse team across the Americas and Europe, with flexibility to work from anywhere.
  • Ownership Culture: We foster an environment where each team member takes ownership and is empowered to contribute to the company's success.
  • Growth & Development: We support continuous professional growth and offer financial assistance for technical certifications and other learning opportunities.
  • Compensation: Competitive salary and an indefinite contract, with salary negotiable based on experience.

If you're passionate about making an impact and growing with a dynamic, remote-first company, we want to hear from you!

jobs.title: Senior Technical Recruiter
jobs.excerpt: Senior Technical Recruiter Department: Recruiting and Operations Team: Recruitment Location: Remote — Latin America (LATAM preferred) / US-friendly hours Commitment: Full-Time Workplace type: Remote> This is the junior counterpart to Hop's Principal Technical Recruiter role.
jobs.description:
Senior Technical Recruiter
Department: Recruiting and Operations
Team: Recruitment
Location: Remote — Latin America (LATAM preferred) / US-friendly hours
Commitment: Full-Time
Workplace type: Remote
> This is the junior counterpart to Hop's Principal Technical Recruiter role. Same mission, same Moon Engine exposure — just calibrated for recruiters with 2–5 years of technical recruiting experience who want to grow into a Principal seat over the next 18–24 months.

The Mission

    You'll start by doing what you do best: running full-cycle searches on technical roles and building strong candidate and client relationships.
    But this isn't a traditional recruiting role. While you deliver hiring outcomes, you'll also learn how to integrate AI into every part of the recruiting workflow — and eventually help clients do the same as our platform launches.
    Hop works with Fortune 500 companies and top VC-backed startups, specializing in GenAI, ML, Data Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, and Product talent.
    We're pre-launch on Moon Engine, an agent-orchestrated recruiting ops system where autonomous agents act as decision partners, coordinating hiring with governance and auditability.
    At Hop, you'll grow into a player-coach: a hands-on recruiter today, an AI-enabled recruiting advisor tomorrow. You'll work alongside senior recruiters and our engineering and product teams to test Moon Engine, give critical feedback, and master the future of recruiting.
    Think of it as dual-track growth: deepen your recruiting craft while becoming an expert in AI-orchestrated hiring workflows — with a clear path to a Principal seat as you mature.

What Makes This Different

    You're not choosing between recruiting or AI. You're learning both.
    • Hands-on recruiting excellence: You'll own searches for mid-to-senior technical talent — sourcing, engaging, interviewing, and closing. Real, high-stakes work with senior recruiter mentorship.
    • Learn AI integration deeply: As you recruit, you'll progressively adopt Moon Engine's capabilities — from AI-assisted sourcing to automated screening. You'll become fluent in how AI amplifies (not replaces) recruiter judgment.
    • Product development partner: Sit close to our engineering and product teams. Your real-world recruiting experiences become product requirements. Your feedback shapes what gets built.
    • Customer enablement track: As Moon Engine launches, you'll help onboard enterprise clients — teaching them what you've learned and growing into a trusted advisor role.

What You'll Actually Do

    Phase 1: Recruiting Execution (Day 1 onwards)
    • Run full-cycle searches for mid-to-senior technical roles: Software Engineers, Data Engineers, ML/Data Science contributors, Technical PMs
    • Partner with senior recruiters and hiring managers on intake, calibration, and offer strategy
    • Source, engage, interview, and close technical talent with white-glove candidate care
    • Build and grow client relationships under the guidance of a Principal recruiter
    • Hit weekly sourcing, pipeline, and submit-to-hire targets
    Phase 2: AI Integration & Learning (Progressive ramp)
    • Use Moon Engine daily on your real searches — flag what works, what's confusing, what's missing
    • Adopt AI-assisted sourcing, scoring, screening, and matching as features ship
    • Join feedback sessions with engineering and product; turn your day-to-day frictions into roadmap input
    • Document patterns and best practices as you discover them
    Phase 3: Client Enablement (As Moon Engine launches and you mature into the role)
    • Co-onboard enterprise clients alongside senior recruiters
    • Help train client recruiting teams on AI-enabled workflows
    • Step into more autonomous client relationships as you build trust and depth
    • Path to Principal Technical Recruiter within ~18–24 months for strong performers

Who Thrives Here

    Must-Haves
    • 2–5 years of full-cycle technical recruiting experience (in-house, agency, or RPO) with closes on engineering, data, or product roles
    • Solid recruiting fundamentals: sourcing, intake, screening, scheduling, offer support, stakeholder communication — you've done all of it, even if not yet at the most senior level
    • Strong candidate communication: you can write compelling outreach, run a clean phone screen, and build rapport with passive candidates
    • Coachable + ambitious: you actively seek feedback, iterate fast, and want to grow into Principal
    • Genuinely curious about AI: you don't need a technical background, but you're excited to learn how AI can augment recruiting
    • Growth mindset: comfortable learning new tools, sitting with ambiguity, and stretching beyond what you've done before
    • Fluent English (written + verbal); LATAM-based candidates strongly preferred for US time-zone overlap
    Bonus Points
    • Prior experience recruiting for ML/AI, Data Science, or platform/infra engineering roles
    • Hands-on use of AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, AI sourcing platforms) in your current workflow
    • Background at high-growth tech companies, well-known recruiting agencies, or in-house technical recruiting teams
    • You've experimented with automations, Boolean wizardry, or "hacks" to work more efficiently
    • Comfortable giving product feedback or working with technical teammates
    Cultural Fit
    • Execution-oriented: you deliver results, not excuses
    • Collaborative learner: ego doesn't get in the way of growing
    • Comfortable with ambiguity: Moon Engine is pre-launch — things will change
    • Naturally curious: you want to understand how things work, not just use them
    • Long-term thinker: you see this as a multi-year journey to become a recruiting + AI expert

Why This Opportunity Matters

    Most recruiters will eventually have to learn AI. You'll be years ahead.
    You're not choosing between being a great recruiter or learning AI — you're mastering both while helping build the platform. Think of it like learning digital marketing in 2005. Early movers win.

    What You Gain
    • Competitive base + commission + bonus with long-term upside as Moon Engine scales
    • Clear path to Principal Technical Recruiter within 18–24 months for strong performers
    • Direct mentorship from senior recruiters and the Head of Recruiting
    • Deep AI recruiting expertise in 6–12 months
    • Product influence — your feedback shapes what gets built
    • Unlimited PTO + thought-leadership opportunities (events, podcasts, content)

jobs.title: Backend Architect - Golang
jobs.excerpt: Point Wild helps customers monitor, manage, and protect against the risks associated with their identities and personal information in a digital world.
jobs.description:
Point Wild helps customers monitor, manage, and protect against the risks associated with their identities and personal information in a digital world. Backed by WndrCo, Warburg Pincus and General Catalyst, Point Wild is dedicated to creating the world’s most comprehensive portfolio of industry-leading cybersecurity solutions. Our vision is to become THE go-to resource for every cyber protection need individuals may face - today and in the future.

Join us for the ride!

About the Role

We're seeking a hands-on VPN Backend Architect (Golang) to lead our backend team while spending 70% of your time writing Golang code. You'll set technical direction for our backend platform serving millions of users, guide an engineering team, and own architecture decisions for distributed services that must be fast, reliable, and secure at scale.

This role suits someone who wants to design secure, scalable systems and write the code that runs them.

What You'll Do

  • Define and evolve the architecture of our backend platform serving connections from millions of users
  • Design and build highly available distributed services in Golang while setting technical direction on scalability, reliability, and performance targets
  • Lead code reviews and champion testing discipline, clean architecture, and engineering best practices across the team
  • Partner with the SDK team to integrate client features cleanly into backend systems and deliver end-to-end functionality
  • Mentor engineers and grow the technical depth of the team while collaborating with security, infrastructure, and product teams
  • Drive the team to meet performance targets and ship reliable products that protect users at scale

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field.
  • 8+ years of backend engineering & architecture experience with 5+ years in Golang
  • Proven track record designing and operating distributed systems at scale with deep understanding of networking protocols (IP, TCP, UDP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS)
  • Hands-on experience with VPN protocols (WireGuard, OpenVPN, IPsec), tunneling, NAT traversal, and low-latency networking
  • Production experience on AWS (EC2, EKS, S3, Aurora/RDS) with container technologies (Docker, Kubernetes) and strong Linux development background
  • Working knowledge of cryptography fundamentals, threat modeling methodologies, secure coding practices, and strong API design skills

Bonus Points

  • Master's degree in Computer Science or related field
  • Network performance tuning and optimization experience with knowledge of Python and Java
  • Experience with NoSQL databases and familiarity with observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)

As part of Point Wild, you will:

Solve real customer problems. Point Wild’s point solutions allow consumers to address their immediate cyber protection needs. Our mandate is to continuously anticipate our customers’ evolving digital security needs to create best-in-class solutions aimed at keeping them safe.

See your impact. We are a scrappy, nimble organization where individual contributions are needed and valued. You will see your impact every day.

Accelerate your career. As we expand, you will have the opportunity to learn new technologies, products, and markets in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment.

Most importantly, you’ll get to work with other talented people at a company where people matter. If you want to put your fingerprint on an organization and leapfrog your growth, this is the place for you.

In keeping with our beliefs and goals, no employee or applicant will face discrimination or harassment based on race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, age, gender, marital domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status, or veteran status. Above and beyond discrimination or harassment based on “protected categories,” Point Wild is committed to being an inclusive community where all feel welcome. Whether blatant or hidden, barriers to success have no place at Point Wild.

  • Leverage AI tools to build solutions to support business users and enhance business intelligence.

  • Master’s degree or bachelor’s degree in computer science, Statistics, Economics, or other quantitative related fields or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience with BI analytics or reporting tolls like Tableau, Power BI etc.
  • 5+ years of experience using SQL.
  • Working experience with schema design and dimensional data modeling.
  • Detailed orientated, highly analytical and focused on quality and accuracy of work.
  • Demonstrated experience applying AI tools to solve business problems, including automating repetitive analytical tasks, accelerating insight generation, and improving decision-making.

Ways to Stand Out from The Crowd:

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, effectively collaborate and communicate complex technical concepts to a broad variety of audiences.
  • Strong analytical skills and advance modeling experience.
  • Ability to evaluate and adopt emerging AI technologies to enhance business intelligence, reporting, and operational efficiency.

Clinical Trial Psych Rater -HungarianSpeaking

Location: Remote/Virtual
Hours: Estimated 10–16 hours per month
Role: Clinical Specialist

About IQVIA

IQVIA is a global leader in advanced analytics, technology solutions, and clinical research services, dedicated to driving healthcare forward. We partner with the world’s leading pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device companies to improve patient outcomes and accelerate innovation. Our team combines deep scientific expertise with cutting-edge technology to deliver high-quality data and insights that shape the future of clinical trials.

Position Overview

The Clinical Specialist plays a key role in ensuring the integrity and reliability of clinical trial data. This position involves reviewing scales administered by raters to confirm standardized assessment practices. Responsibilities include evaluating assessment quality, engaging in live discussions with raters to provide guidance on methodology and scoring techniques, and supporting rater performance through functional assessments (e.g., mock interviews). Additional tasks may include assisting with communication materials and documentation.

Key Responsibilities

  • Participate in all required orientation, training, and calibration activities.

  • Review case data and prepare for rater discussions, ensuring all relevant documents and scale items are available.

  • Conduct live interactions with raters to provide feedback and guidance on assessment methodology and scoring.

  • Complete assigned tasks and rater interactions according to schedule.

Founded in 2014 by a team of fixed income market experts, Trumid has quickly become one of the top three corporate bond e-trading platforms in the U.S. Today, over 1,300 traders from an extensive and expanding client network of 1,000+ buy- and sell-side institutions transact on Trumid monthly.

With a rich history of innovation and a unique ability to innovate at scale, we collaborate closely with our clients, iterating quickly toward optimal solutions. With market share and client engagement at all-time highs and our pace of product development faster than ever, this is an exciting and transformative time at Trumid.

Our business model thrives on participation, and so does our company culture. We rely on every team member's contribution to help us accomplish our goals. To succeed at Trumid, you must be curious, passionate about your craft, ambitious, collaborative, and driven. Learn more at

The opportunity.

Join our team as a Senior Software Engineer, building the trading systems at the core of our platform. We have recently been migrating critical trading workflows onto Aeron-based sequenced-log architecture and this role sits at the heart of that platform: you will join one of the teams running services on top of it, matched to the team that best fits your strengths and interests during the interview process.

We are also an AI-native engineering organization: the majority of our pull requests are AI-written and AI-reviewed, supported by in-house agent tooling built directly into our monorepo, so engineers spend their time on design, correctness, and leverage rather than boilerplate.

We are looking for an engineer with a background in capital markets, trading workflows, or electronic trading systems. You have strong skills in system design, you focus on observability and testing, and you leverage AI to move faster without sacrificing quality. Within your first six months, you will tackle key projects such as:

  • Feature Expansion: Ship new trading protocol capabilities at high velocity on our Aeron-based platform, supporting a growing client base and increased trading volumes.
  • Platform Modernization: Evolve our service architecture — migrating remaining workflows onto the new stack and designing the messaging patterns that connect it to the rest of the platform.
  • System Optimization: Improve platform scalability, performance, and test coverage for systems where correctness is the product.

Responsibilities include:

  • Design, Develop and Test: Build protocols and features to meet functional and non-functional requirements.
  • Support and Maintain: Ensure the reliability and availability of services developed by the team, addressing production issues and continuously improving operational processes.
  • Optimize Performance: Improve system performance for low latency and high throughput, crucial in trading systems.
  • Collaborate: Work with cross-functional teams to execute projects and contribute to a team-oriented culture.

About You.

We’re seeking an engineer with experience in financial services, trade workflows, or electronic trading systems. Your qualifications include:

  • Location: U.S., EST Time Zone
  • Industry Experience: 7+ years of experience in software engineering, preferably in capital markets or trading workflows.
  • Programming Skills: Proficiency in JVM-based languages (Scala preferred); ability to write clean and maintainable code.
  • Distributed Systems: Experience in designing, implementing, and maintaining scalable systems.
  • Network Protocols & Messaging: Familiarity with technologies such as TCP/IP, FIX, Kafka, or Aeron.
  • Cloud Technologies: Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and Docker.
  • AI-Assisted Development: Ability to effectively use AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Claude Code) to accelerate delivery and improve quality while maintaining strong engineering judgment.
  • Performance Optimization: Understanding of low latency, high-throughput systems.
  • SDLC Practices: Familiarity with Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) methodologies, including agile practices and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Continuous Improvement: Commitment to delivering high-quality solutions.

More About Us and our Tech Stack.

  • Languages and Frameworks: We primarily use Scala with ZIO, Pekko and gRPC.
  • Messaging Technologies: Our messaging systems include Kafka and Aeron.
  • Containerization and Orchestration: We rely on Kubernetes and Docker to build, deliver, and scale containerized services.
  • AI-Native Engineering: Agent tooling, automated review, and AI-assisted workflows are built into our development platform.
  • Company Culture: We value a collaborative team environment where your technical views and leadership abilities are highly appreciated.

Employee Benefits.

  • Highly competitive compensation
  • Fully paid medical, dental and vision coverage
  • Team-oriented and collaborative company culture
  • Remote first

In compliance with New York City Pay Transparency Law, the base salary range for this role in New York City is between $175,000 – $250,000. If a candidate’s experience differs from the requirements, the salary may be adjusted accordingly.
